recipes.title: Beef and Broccoli
recipes.localTitle: Niu Rou Chao Xi Lan Hua (牛肉炒西兰花)
recipes.description: Thin-sliced beef velveted in baking soda and cornstarch for a silky restaurant bite, stir-fried hot and fast with broccoli in a glossy oyster sauce glaze — worth the extra marinating bowl.

ingredients.item: flank or flat iron steak, thinly sliced against the grain

steps: Slice the beef thinly against the grain. Combine with the baking soda, oyster sauce, light soy sauce, cornstarch, Shaoxing wine, water, white pepper and sugar; massage until absorbed and marinate 30 minutes — this velveting step is what gives restaurant beef its tender bite.
Whisk together the sauce ingredients (oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch and water) in a small bowl and set aside.
Blanch the broccoli florets in salted, oiled boiling water for about 2 minutes until bright green and just tender; drain well and set aside.
Heat a wok over high heat until smoking, add half the oil, and sear the marinated beef in a single layer for 30-45 seconds per side until just browned; remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil, then stir-fry the garlic, ginger and scallion whites until fragrant, about 20 seconds.
Return the broccoli and beef to the wok, pour in the sauce, and toss constantly over high heat for about 1 minute until the sauce thickens and coats everything glossy.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.
tips: Massage the baking soda into the beef and don't skip straight to the pan — it's what gives restaurant beef its tender bite.
Sear the beef in a single layer and resist stirring for the first 20-30 seconds, or it steams instead of browns.
recipes.nutritionNote: Two rounds of oyster and soy sauce make this a sodium-heavy dish, so go light on extra salt and serve with plain rice and an extra side of blanched greens to round out the fiber.

fil.description: Manipis na hiwang beef, velveted sa baking soda at cornstarch para sa silky restaurant bite, hot and fast na sini-stir-fry with broccoli sa glossy oyster sauce glaze — worth the extra marinating bowl.
ingredients: flank o flat iron steak, hiwain nang manipis against the grain
steps: Hiwain nang manipis ang beef against the grain. I-combine sa baking soda, oyster sauce, light soy sauce, cornstarch, Shaoxing wine, tubig, white pepper at asukal; i-massage hanggang na-absorb tapos i-marinate for 30 minutes — ito ang velveting step na siyang nagbibigay ng tender bite ng restaurant beef.
I-whisk ang sauce ingredients (oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch at tubig) sa maliit na bowl tapos itabi muna.
I-blanch ang broccoli florets sa salted at oiled boiling water for about 2 minutes hanggang bright green at just tender; i-drain nang mabuti tapos itabi.
Painitin ang wok sa high heat hanggang umuusok, idagdag ang half ng oil, at i-sear ang marinated beef in a single layer for 30-45 seconds per side hanggang just browned; alisin muna at itabi.
Idagdag ang natitirang oil, tapos i-stir-fry ang bawang, luya at scallion whites hanggang mabango, about 20 seconds.
Ibalik ang broccoli at beef sa wok, ibuhos ang sauce, at i-toss nang paulit-ulit sa high heat for about 1 minute hanggang lumapot ang sauce at ma-coat nang glossy ang lahat.
Ihain agad over steamed rice.
tips: I-massage ang baking soda sa beef, huwag agad diretso sa kawali — ito ang nagbibigay ng tender bite ng restaurant beef.
I-sear ang beef in a single layer at huwag munang haluin for the first 20-30 seconds, kung hindi steamed ang labas instead of browned.
fil.nutritionNote: Sodium-heavy ang dish dahil sa two rounds ng oyster at soy sauce, kaya bawasan ang extra salt at ihain with plain rice at extra side ng blanched greens para sa fiber.

recipes.title: Beef Chow Fun
recipes.localTitle: Gan Chao Niu He (干炒牛河)
recipes.description: Wide rice noodles seared in a screaming-hot wok with velveted beef, bean sprouts and scallion until the noodles pick up a smoky char — the dish Cantonese cooks judge each other's wok skills by.

ingredients.item: flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
fresh wide rice noodles (ho fun), separated

steps: Massage the baking soda into the beef, then mix in the soy sauce, cornstarch and water; marinate 15 minutes for a tender, velveted bite.
Whisk the dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, sugar and Shaoxing wine together in a small bowl.
Gently separate the rice noodles by hand, taking care not to tear them, since fresh ho fun is delicate and clumps together straight from the pack.
Heat a wok over the highest possible heat until it's smoking hot, add half the oil, and sear the beef in a single layer for 30-45 seconds per side until just browned; remove and set aside.

Add another tablespoon of oil and stir-fry the garlic and scallion whites 20 seconds, then add the noodles and 1 tablespoon of the sauce mixture. Use a folding motion rather than aggressive stirring to coat the noodles without breaking them, and let them sit undisturbed for 30 seconds at a time against the hot wok to pick up char.
Push the noodles aside, add the remaining oil, and pour in the rest of the sauce; toss briefly to coat.
Return the beef to the wok along with the bean sprouts and scallion greens. Toss everything together over the highest heat for 30-45 seconds until well combined.
Serve immediately while the noodles are still hot and smoky.
tips: Maximum heat the entire time is non-negotiable — a wok that isn't smoking hot steams the noodles instead of giving them the charred "wok hei" flavor the dish is named for.
Fold, don't stir, once the noodles are in the wok; vigorous stirring with a spatula is the most common way home cooks shred fresh ho fun into mush.
recipes.nutritionNote: A high-carb, high-sodium plate from the noodles and double soy sauce, so treat it as an occasional noodle night rather than a weekly staple, and serve a plain blanched vegetable alongside since the dish itself is light on fiber.

fil.description: Wide rice noodles na na-sear sa sobrang init na wok with velveted na baka, bean sprouts at scallion hanggang makakuha ng smoky char ang noodles — ang dish na pinagbabatayan ng mga Cantonese cook sa wok skills ng isa't isa.
ingredients: flank steak, hiwaing manipis against the grain
sariwang wide rice noodles (ho fun), ihiwalay, o pinalambot na dried ho fun
steps: I-massage ang baking soda sa baka, tapos ihalo ang soy sauce, cornstarch at tubig; i-marinate for 15 minutes para maging malambot at velveted ang bite.
Ihalo (whisk) ang dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, asukal at Shaoxing wine sa maliit na mangkok.
Ihiwalay nang dahan-dahan ang rice noodles gamit ang kamay, mag-ingat na hindi mapunit, dahil delicate ang fresh ho fun at magkakadikit straight from the pack.

Painitin ang wok sa pinakamataas na heat hanggang umuusok nang husto, idagdag ang half ng oil, at i-sear ang baka in a single layer for 30-45 seconds per side hanggang medyo mag-brown lang; alisin at itabi muna.

Idagdag ang isa pang tablespoon ng oil at i-stir-fry ang bawang at puting parte ng scallion for 20 seconds, tapos idagdag ang noodles at 1 tablespoon ng sauce mixture. Gumamit ng folding motion instead of aggressive stirring para ma-coat ang noodles nang hindi napupunit, at hayaang tumigil nang 30 seconds at a time laban sa mainit na wok para makakuha ng char.
Itulak ang noodles sa side, idagdag ang natitirang oil, at ibuhos ang natitirang sauce; haluin nang saglit para ma-coat.
Ibalik ang baka sa wok kasama ang bean sprouts at berdeng parte ng scallion. Haluin lahat sa pinakamataas na heat for 30-45 seconds hanggang maging well combined.
Ihain agad habang mainit at smoky pa ang noodles.
tips: Non-negotiable ang maximum heat sa buong process — kapag hindi umuusok nang husto ang wok, nagsi-steam na lang ang noodles instead of makuha ang charred na "wok hei" flavor na pinagmulan ng pangalan ng dish.

I-fold, huwag ihalo nang malakas, kapag nasa wok na ang noodles; ang agresibong paghahalo gamit ang spatula ang pinakakaraniwang dahilan kung bakit napupunit ang fresh ho fun ng mga home cook into mush.
fil.nutritionNote: High-carb at high-sodium na plate dahil sa noodles at double na toyo, kaya gawing occasional noodle night na lang ito instead of weekly staple, at maghain ng plain blanched na gulay kasabay dahil konti lang ang fiber ng dish mismo.

recipes.title: Braised Beef Brisket with Daikon
recipes.description: Beef chuck and daikon radish simmered low and slow with star anise, ginger and a splash of soy until the meat is fall-apart tender and the radish has soaked up all the braising liquid — a Cantonese cold-weather stew built for rice.

ingredients.item: beef chuck or brisket, cut into 4cm chunks

ingredients.note: enough to cover the beef, plus more as it braises

ingredients.item: daikon radish, peeled and cut into thick chunks

steps: Cover the beef with cold water in a pot, bring to a boil, and blanch for 3 minutes to release scum; drain and rinse the beef and the pot.
Heat the oil in a clean pot over medium heat and fry the ginger, garlic and scallion until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the star anise, cinnamon and bay leaves, then the blanched beef; stir-fry 2 minutes until the beef picks up a little color.
Pour in the Shaoxing wine and let it bubble 1 minute, then add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar and enough water to just cover the beef.
Bring to a boil, skim any remaining scum, then reduce to a low simmer, cover, and braise for 1.5 hours, topping up water if it runs low.
Add the daikon chunks and continue simmering, partially covered, for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until both the beef and daikon are fork-tender and the sauce has reduced and thickened slightly.
Taste and adjust salt if needed, discard the star anise, cinnamon and bay leaves if you can find them, and serve hot over rice, garnished with sliced scallion.
tips: Chuck holds up better than lean brisket over a long braise — brisket alone can turn dry and stringy by the time the daikon is done.
This tastes better the next day: refrigerate overnight so the flavor deepens, then reheat gently before serving.
recipes.nutritionNote: The daikon makes this a genuinely balanced one-pot meal with real vegetable content built in, and the fat renders out of the chuck as it braises, so serve with plain rice and skip adding extra oil-heavy sides at the same meal.

fil.description: Beef chuck at daikon radish na ni-simmer nang mahinay at matagal with star anise, luya at kaunting toyo hanggang fall-apart tender ang karne at nasipsip na ng daikon ang lahat ng braising liquid — Cantonese cold-weather stew na para talaga sa kanin.
ingredients: beef chuck o brisket, hiwain into 4cm chunks
tubig, sapat para matakpan ang baka, plus dagdag habang nagbrabraise
daikon radish, balatan at hiwain into thick chunks
steps: Takpan ang baka ng cold water sa pot, pakuluin, at i-blanch for 3 minutes para lumabas ang scum; i-drain at banlawan ang baka at ang pot.
Painitin ang oil sa malinis na pot sa medium heat at iprito ang luya, bawang at scallion hanggang umamoy masarap, about 1 minute.
Idagdag ang star anise, cinnamon at bay leaves, tapos ang blanched na baka; i-stir-fry for 2 minutes hanggang bahagyang magbago ng kulay ang baka.
Ibuhos ang Shaoxing wine at hayaang mag-bubble for 1 minute, tapos idagdag ang light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar at sapat na tubig para matakpan lang ang baka.
Pakuluin, alisin ang natitirang scum, tapos hinaan to low simmer, takpan, at i-braise for 1.5 hours, magdagdag ng tubig kung kumonti.
Idagdag ang daikon chunks at ituloy ang pag-simmer, half-takip lang, for 45 minutes to 1 hour, hanggang parehong maging fork-tender ang baka at daikon at bahagyang lumapot ang sauce.
Tikman at i-adjust ang asin kung kailangan, alisin ang star anise, cinnamon at bay leaves kung makikita mo pa, at ihain nang mainit over rice, garnished with hiniwang scallion.
tips: Mas okay ang chuck kaysa sa lean brisket sa mahabang braise — pwedeng matuyo at maging stringy ang brisket lang by the time maluto na ang daikon.
Mas masarap ito the next day: i-refrigerate overnight para lumalim ang lasa, tapos i-reheat nang mahinay bago ihain.
fil.nutritionNote: Dahil sa daikon, genuinely balanced na one-pot meal ito na may totoong vegetable content, at natutunaw ang taba ng chuck habang nagbrabraise, kaya ihain with plain rice at laktawan na lang ang extra oil-heavy sides sa parehong meal.

recipes.title: Century Egg and Chicken Congee
recipes.localTitle: Pi Dan Ji Rou Zhou (皮蛋鸡肉粥)
recipes.description: Rice simmered down into a smooth, savory porridge with shredded chicken, ginger and jelly-textured century egg — the dish Cantonese families reach for at breakfast, when sick, or any time something gentle is needed.

ingredients.note: plus more to loosen as it simmers

ingredients.item: ginger, half sliced and half julienned
century eggs, peeled and cut into small wedges
fried shallots or youtiao (Chinese fried dough), for serving

steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then soak it in the 500ml water for 15 minutes — soaking shortens the simmer time and helps the grains break down evenly.
Bring the stock to a boil in a large pot, add the soaked rice with its soaking water and the sliced ginger, and return to a boil.
Reduce to a gentle simmer, partially cover, and cook for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally so the rice doesn't catch on the bottom.
Add the whole chicken thigh, submerging it in the porridge, and simmer 12-15 minutes until just cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, let it cool slightly, then shred it with two forks; set aside.
Continue simmering the congee 5-10 more minutes, stirring often, until the grains break down into a smooth, thick porridge — add hot water a splash at a time if it gets too thick.
Stir the shredded chicken and century egg wedges back into the pot, season with salt, white pepper and sesame oil, and warm through 1-2 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and top with julienned ginger and sliced scallion.
tips: Stirring occasionally as it simmers is what breaks the rice grains down into a creamy porridge instead of just soft rice in broth.
Century eggs taste strongest raw and cold — folding them in for the last couple of minutes rather than boiling them the whole time keeps their flavor milder for first-timers.
recipes.nutritionNote: A gentle, easy-to-digest one-bowl meal that's naturally low in fat; use low-sodium stock since congee is often eaten in larger portions than rice, and pair with a simple stir-fried green vegetable for fiber.

fil.description: Bigas na ni-simmer hanggang maging smooth at savory na porridge with shredded chicken, luya at jelly-textured na century egg — ang dish na hinahanap ng Cantonese families sa breakfast, kapag may sakit, o anytime na kailangan ng something gentle.
ingredients: tubig, plus dagdag para paluwagin habang nagsisimmer
luya, half hiwain at half i-julienne
century eggs, balatan at hiwain into small wedges
fried shallots o youtiao (Chinese fried dough), for serving, optional
steps: Banlawan ang bigas hanggang halos malinaw na ang tubig, tapos ibabad sa 500ml na tubig for 15 minutes — ang pagbabad ang nagpapaiksi sa simmer time at tumutulong para pantay ma-break down ang mga butil.
Pakuluin ang stock sa malaking pot, idagdag ang soaked rice with soaking water nito at ang hiniwang luya, at pakuluin ulit.
Hinaan to gentle simmer, half-takip lang, at lutuin for 25 minutes, haluin paminsan-minsan para hindi dumikit ang bigas sa ilalim.
Idagdag ang whole na hita ng manok, ilubog sa porridge, at i-simmer for 12-15 minutes hanggang cooked through lang.
Buhatin ang manok, hayaang lumamig nang bahagya, tapos tadtarin gamit ang dalawang tinidor; itabi muna.
Ituloy ang pag-simmer ng congee for 5-10 more minutes, haluin madalas, hanggang mag-break down ang mga butil into smooth at malapot na porridge — magdagdag ng mainit na tubig kung sobrang lumapot.
Ihalo ang shredded chicken at century egg wedges pabalik sa pot, timplahan ng asin, white pepper at sesame oil, at painitin for 1-2 minutes.
Isalok sa mangkok at lagyan ng julienned na luya at hiniwang scallion.
tips: Ang paghalo paminsan-minsan habang nagsisimmer ang dahilan kung bakit nagiging creamy porridge ang bigas instead of soft rice lang sa broth.

Pinakamatapang ang lasa ng century eggs kapag raw at malamig — sa pag-fold sa mga ito sa last couple of minutes lang instead of ipapakulo nang buong oras, mas mild ang lasa para sa mga unang beses kumain nito.
fil.nutritionNote: Gentle at easy-to-digest na one-bowl meal na naturally low sa taba; gumamit ng low-sodium stock dahil mas malaking portion ang kinakain sa congee kumpara sa kanin, at i-pair with simpleng stir-fried na berdeng gulay para sa fiber.

recipes.title: Char Siu (Cantonese BBQ Pork)
recipes.description: Pork shoulder strips marinated overnight in hoisin, five-spice and honey, then roasted hot and basted until the edges char and caramelize — the pork behind every Cantonese roast-meat window.

ingredients.item: boneless pork shoulder, cut into 3cm-thick strips

ingredients.note: for basting, mixed with 1 tbsp hot water

steps: Combine hoisin sauce, light and dark soy sauce, sugar, Shaoxing wine, five-spice, salt, garlic and sesame oil in a bowl. Reserve 2 tablespoons of this marinade in the fridge for basting later.

Rub the rest of the marinade into the pork strips, cover, and refrigerate overnight (at least 8 hours) — this long marinate is what carries the flavor all the way through the meat, not just the surface.
Let the pork sit at room temperature for 20 minutes, then set a wire rack over a foil-lined tray with a little water in the tray to catch drips and prevent burning.
Roast at 220°C (425°F) for 20 minutes, then flip the strips and roast 10 more minutes.
Brush the strips with the reserved marinade, roast 5 minutes, flip and brush the other side, and roast a final 5 minutes until the edges are lightly charred.
Brush both sides with the honey-water glaze in the last 2 minutes for shine and a touch of char.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice against the grain and serve over rice or with steamed buns.
tips: Don't skip the overnight marinate — a few hours gives you seasoned pork, not char siu; the flavor needs time to penetrate the meat, not just coat it.
Watch the last 10 minutes closely: the sugar in the marinade caramelizes fast and goes from charred-good to burnt-bitter within a minute.
recipes.nutritionNote: Pork shoulder keeps enough fat to stay juicy through roasting and the marinade is sugar- and sodium-heavy, so serve slices over plain rice with a side of blanched greens rather than more roast meats at the same meal.

fil.description: Pork shoulder strips na ni-marinate overnight sa hoisin, five-spice at honey, tapos ni-roast sa mataas na heat at binasted hanggang mag-char at mag-caramelize ang gilid — ang baboy na nasa likod ng bawat Cantonese roast-meat window.
ingredients: boneless na balikat ng baboy, hiwain into 3cm-thick strips
honey, for basting, ihalo sa 1 tbsp mainit na tubig
steps: Ihalo ang hoisin sauce, light at dark soy sauce, asukal, Shaoxing wine, five-spice, asin, bawang at sesame oil sa mangkok. Maglaan ng 2 tablespoons ng marinade na ito sa fridge para sa basting mamaya.

Kuskusin ang natitirang marinade sa pork strips, takpan, at i-refrigerate overnight (at least 8 hours) — ang mahabang marinate na ito ang nagpapasok ng lasa hanggang sa loob ng karne, hindi lang sa surface.
Hayaang mag-room temperature ang baboy for 20 minutes, tapos maglagay ng wire rack sa ibabaw ng foil-lined tray na may kaunting tubig sa loob para masalo ang tumutulo at maiwasan ang pagkasunog.
I-roast sa 220°C (425°F) for 20 minutes, tapos baliktarin ang strips at i-roast ulit for 10 more minutes.
Pahiran ang strips ng reserved marinade, i-roast for 5 minutes, baliktarin at pahiran ang kabilang side, at i-roast nang final 5 minutes hanggang bahagyang mag-char ang gilid.
Pahiran ang parehong side ng honey-water glaze sa last 2 minutes para kumintab at magka-touch ng char.
Ipahinga for 5 minutes, tapos hiwain against the grain at ihain over rice o with steamed buns.
tips: Huwag laktawan ang overnight marinate — kapag ilang oras lang, seasoned pork lang ang makukuha mo, hindi char siu; kailangan ng oras ng lasa para tumagos sa karne, hindi lang mag-coat sa labas.
Bantayan nang mabuti ang last 10 minutes: mabilis mag-caramelize ang asukal sa marinade at pwedeng maging burnt-bitter na agad mula sa charred-good sa loob lang ng isang minuto.
fil.nutritionNote: Sapat ang taba ng pork shoulder para manatiling juicy kahit ma-roast, at mataas sa asukal at sodium ang marinade, kaya ihain ang slices over plain rice with side na blanched greens instead of dagdag pang roast meats sa parehong meal.

recipes.title: Chinese Steamed Egg Custard
recipes.description: Beaten eggs loosened with warm stock and steamed low until barely set into a wobbly, custard-smooth savory pudding — the fastest, gentlest dish in the whole repertoire and the one kids ask for by name.

ingredients.note: about 1.5x the volume of the eggs

steps: Beat the eggs in a bowl until just combined, avoiding whipping in too much air, which causes bubbles in the finished custard.
Whisk in the warm stock or water and salt until fully blended.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a shallow heatproof bowl to remove any bubbles or unmixed bits — this step is what gives the custard its glass-smooth surface.
Cover the bowl tightly with foil or a plate to keep condensation from dripping in and pitting the surface.

Set up a steamer with water at a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil, and steam the covered bowl over medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes, until the custard is just set with a slight wobble in the center.
Carefully remove the bowl and let it rest, covered, for 2 minutes.
Uncover, drizzle with sesame oil and a little light soy sauce, and scatter with scallion.
Serve warm, straight from the steaming bowl, with rice.
tips: Keep the steam gentle, not rolling — high heat is what causes the pitted, honeycombed texture instead of a smooth custard.
Straining the egg mixture takes ten extra seconds and is the single biggest difference between a silky restaurant version and a lumpy home one.
recipes.nutritionNote: Low in fat and easy to digest, with protein from the eggs and almost no added oil; pair with a vegetable stir-fry and rice for a complete meal, and use low-sodium stock if serving to young kids.

fil.description: Beaten na itlog na pinaluwag ng maligamgam na stock at ni-steam sa mahinang init hanggang barely set into wobbly at custard-smooth na savory pudding — ang pinakamabilis at pinaka-gentle na dish sa buong repertoire at ang hinihingi ng mga bata by name.
ingredients: maligamgam na chicken stock o tubig, mga 1.5x ng volume ng itlog
light soy sauce, for drizzling sa dulo
steps: I-beat ang itlog sa mangkok hanggang just combined lang, iwasan ang sobrang pag-whip na nagdudulot ng hangin, dahil nagiging bula ito sa tapos na custard.
Ihalo (whisk) ang maligamgam na stock o tubig at asin hanggang fully blended.
I-strain ang mixture sa fine sieve papunta sa mababaw na heatproof na mangkok para matanggal ang bula o hindi na-mix na parte — ang step na ito ang nagbibigay sa custard ng glass-smooth na surface.
Takpan nang mahigpit ang mangkok gamit ang foil o plato para hindi tumulo ang condensation at mag-pit sa surface.

Maghanda ng steamer na may tubig sa gentle simmer, hindi rolling boil, at i-steam ang natatakpang mangkok sa medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes, hanggang mag-set lang ang custard na may slight wobble sa gitna.
Alisin nang maingat ang mangkok at hayaang magpahinga, nakatakip, for 2 minutes.
Alisan ng takip, lagyan ng sesame oil at kaunting light soy sauce, at budburan ng scallion.
Ihain warm, diretso mula sa steaming bowl, with rice.
tips: Panatilihing gentle ang steam, hindi rolling — ang high heat ang dahilan kung bakit nagiging pitted at honeycombed ang texture instead of smooth na custard.
Sampung segundo lang extra ang pag-strain sa egg mixture pero ito ang pinakamalaking difference sa pagitan ng silky na restaurant version at lumpy na sa bahay.
fil.nutritionNote: Low sa taba at easy-to-digest, may protein mula sa itlog at halos walang added oil; i-pair with vegetable stir-fry at kanin para maging complete meal, at gumamit ng low-sodium stock kung ihahain sa mga batang bata.

recipes.title: Cumin Beef Stir-Fry
recipes.description: Thin-sliced beef velveted and seared fast with whole toasted cumin seeds, dried chili and onion until smoky and fragrant — a home-cook take on the Xinjiang lamb skewer stall, built around beef instead.

ingredients.item: flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
dried red chilies, snipped in half

steps: Massage the baking soda into the beef, then mix in the soy sauce, cornstarch and water. Marinate 15 minutes — the baking soda is what keeps thin-sliced flank tender in the short, hot cook.
Toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan over low heat for 1 minute until fragrant; set aside.
Heat a wok over high heat until smoking, add half the oil, and sear the beef in a single layer for 30-45 seconds per side until just browned; remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil, then stir-fry the onion and bell pepper for about 1 minute until starting to soften but still crisp.
Add the garlic, dried chilies, chili flakes and toasted cumin seeds; stir-fry 20-30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the beef to the wok, sprinkle in the ground cumin, sugar and salt, and toss over high heat for 30-45 seconds until everything is well coated.
Scatter with cilantro and serve immediately over rice.
tips: Toasting the cumin seeds before they hit the hot oil doubles their aroma — don't skip straight to raw seeds in the wok.
Keep the sear on the beef fast and the wok hot throughout; cumin beef should taste smoky and charred at the edges, not steamed.
recipes.kidNote: The heat here comes from whole dried chilies and chili flakes rather than numbing Sichuan pepper, but it still runs hot. Cook the kids' portion separately: use half the chili flakes, skip the whole dried chilies entirely, and season with just the cumin, sugar and salt.
recipes.nutritionNote: A protein-forward, vegetable-light stir-fry, so round out the plate with a big side of blanched or stir-fried greens, and go easy on extra salt since the marinade and seasoning already carry sodium.

fil.description: Thin-sliced na baka na na-velvet at mabilis na na-sear with whole toasted cumin seeds, dried chili at sibuyas hanggang maging smoky at mabango — home-cook version ng Xinjiang lamb skewer stall, pero baka ang ginamit.
ingredients: flank steak, hiwaing manipis against the grain
tuyong pulang chilies, guntingin nang pahati
steps: I-massage ang baking soda sa baka, tapos ihalo ang soy sauce, cornstarch at tubig. I-marinate for 15 minutes — ang baking soda ang dahilan kung bakit nananatiling malambot ang thin-sliced flank kahit mabilis at mainit ang pagluluto.
I-toast ang cumin seeds sa dry pan sa low heat for 1 minute hanggang umamoy masarap; itabi muna.
Painitin ang wok sa high heat hanggang umuusok, idagdag ang half ng oil, at i-sear ang baka in a single layer for 30-45 seconds per side hanggang medyo mag-brown lang; alisin at itabi muna.
Idagdag ang natitirang oil, tapos i-stir-fry ang sibuyas at bell pepper for about 1 minute hanggang magsimulang lumambot pero crisp pa rin.
Idagdag ang bawang, dried chilies, chili flakes at toasted cumin seeds; i-stir-fry for 20-30 seconds hanggang umamoy masarap.
Ibalik ang baka sa wok, budburan ng giniling na cumin, asukal at asin, at haluin sa high heat for 30-45 seconds hanggang ma-coat nang maayos ang lahat.
Budburan ng cilantro at ihain agad over rice.
tips: Ang pag-toast sa cumin seeds bago ito idagdag sa mainit na oil ang nagdo-doble sa aroma nito — huwag diretso na lang raw seeds sa wok.
Panatilihing mabilis ang sear sa baka at mainit ang wok throughout; dapat may smoky at charred na lasa ang cumin beef sa gilid, hindi steamed.
fil.kidNote: Galing sa buong dried chilies at chili flakes ang anghang dito instead of numbing na Sichuan pepper, pero anghang pa rin ito. Lutuin nang hiwalay ang portion ng mga bata: half lang ng chili flakes, laktawan nang tuluyan ang whole dried chilies, at timplahan na lang ng cumin, asukal at asin.
fil.nutritionNote: Protein-forward pero konti sa gulay ang stir-fry na ito, kaya kumpletuhin ang plate with malaking side ng blanched o stir-fried greens, at conti-in na lang ang extra asin dahil may sodium na rin ang marinade at seasoning.

recipes.title: Dan Dan Noodles
recipes.description: Wheat noodles topped with a chili-oil-and-sesame sauce, crispy ya cai-spiked ground pork and crushed peanuts, mixed tableside — Sichuan street food's numbing, savory, nutty bowl of noodles.

ingredients.item: ya cai (preserved Sichuan mustard greens), minced

ingredients.note: or well-stirred tahini, thinned with warm water to a pourable paste
for frying the topping and toasting the peanuts

steps: Mix the ground pork with the soy sauce and Shaoxing wine in a bowl, stirring well to loosen it before it hits the pan.
Heat the oil in a wok and toast the crushed peanuts over low heat until golden; remove and set aside.
In the same oil, stir-fry the marinated pork with the ginger and chili flakes until browned, then add the ya cai and stir-fry 1 minute until fragrant; remove from heat.
Whisk the sesame paste with a little warm water until smooth and pourable, then stir in the garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, ground Sichuan pepper, chili oil and sugar to make the sauce.
Divide the sauce between serving bowls.
Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the noodles according to the package; add the bok choy for the final minute to blanch.
Drain the noodles and greens and pile them on top of the sauce in each bowl.
Top with the pork, a scatter of toasted peanuts and the chopped scallion. Mix everything together at the table before eating.
tips: Toast the peanuts low and slow in oil rather than dry — it's faster and gives a rounder flavor than a dry pan.
The sauce should be a thin, pourable paste before it hits the bowl; whisk in warm water a teaspoon at a time until the sesame paste loosens.
recipes.kidNote: Before mixing in the chili oil, ground Sichuan pepper and chili flakes, set aside the kids' portions of noodles and pork with a plain sauce of just soy sauce, vinegar and a little sugar; the numbing peppercorn especially is what makes this an adult dish, not the heat alone.
recipes.nutritionNote: Sesame paste and chili oil bring a lot of fat, and the soy-and-ya-cai topping is salty, so treat this as an occasional dish and serve plain cucumber or blanched greens alongside rather than another salty side.

fil.description: Wheat noodles na tinopan ng chili-oil-and-sesame sauce, crispy ya cai-spiked ground pork at durog na peanuts, hinahalo mismo sa table — ang numbing, savory at malinamnam na mangkok ng noodles ng street food sa Sichuan.
ingredients: ya cai (preserved Sichuan mustard greens), tinadtad
Chinese sesame paste, o well-stirred tahini, pinapanis sa warm water hanggang pourable
neutral oil, para sa pagprito ng topping at pag-toast ng peanuts
steps: Ihalo ang ground pork sa soy sauce at Shaoxing wine sa bowl, haluin nang mabuti bago iprito.
Painitin ang oil sa wok at i-toast ang durog na peanuts sa low heat hanggang golden; alisin at itabi.
Sa parehong oil, i-stir-fry ang marinated pork with luya at chili flakes hanggang browned, tapos idagdag ang ya cai at i-stir-fry 1 minute hanggang mabango; alisin sa apoy.
I-whisk ang sesame paste with kaunting warm water hanggang smooth at pourable, tapos ihalo ang bawang, soy sauce, vinegar, ground Sichuan pepper, chili oil at asukal para gawin ang sauce.
Hatiin ang sauce sa serving bowls.
Pakuluan ang tubig at lutuin ang noodles ayon sa package; idagdag ang bok choy sa final minute para ma-blanch.
I-drain ang noodles at gulay tapos ilagay sa ibabaw ng sauce sa bawat mangkok.
Topan ng pork, kaunting toasted peanuts at tinadtad na scallion. Haluin ang lahat sa table bago kainin.
tips: I-toast ang peanuts nang low and slow sa oil instead of dry — mas mabilis ito at mas round ang lasa kaysa dry pan.
Dapat thin at pourable paste ang sauce bago ito ilagay sa mangkok; i-whisk ng warm water isang teaspoon at a time hanggang lumuwag ang sesame paste.
fil.kidNote: Bago ihalo ang chili oil, ground Sichuan pepper at chili flakes, ihiwalay muna ang portion ng mga bata na noodles at pork with plain sauce na toyo, vinegar at konting asukal lang; ang numbing na peppercorn talaga ang gumagawa nito na adult dish, hindi lang ang anghang.
fil.nutritionNote: Maraming taba galing sa sesame paste at chili oil, at maalat ang soy-and-ya-cai topping, kaya ituring itong occasional dish lang at ihain kasama ng plain cucumber o blanched greens instead of another salty side.

recipes.title: Dry-Fried Green Beans
recipes.localTitle: Gan Bian Si Ji Dou (干煸四季豆)
recipes.description: Green beans seared dry in a scorching wok until the skins blister and wrinkle, then tossed with ground pork, dried chili and preserved mustard greens — a textural Sichuan side that's nothing like a steamed green bean.

ingredients.item: dried red chilies, deseeded and chopped
sui mi ya cai (preserved mustard greens), rinsed

steps: Heat a wok over high heat until lightly smoking. Add the green beans and salt, then immediately lower the heat to medium.

Sear the beans for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the skins blister and show small scorch marks; this dry-searing, not deep-frying, is what gives them their wrinkled texture. Remove and set aside.
Add the oil to the wok over medium-high heat and brown the ground pork, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the garlic and dried chilies; stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the ya cai and stir-fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Return the beans to the wok along with the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil. Toss over high heat for 1 minute until everything is well coated.
Serve hot as a side dish.
tips: The dry-sear is the whole technique: don't add extra oil at this stage, and don't rush past 15 minutes or the beans stay squeaky instead of blistered.
Sui mi ya cai is what makes this taste like a Sichuan restaurant, not a stir-fry improvisation — look for it vacuum-packed at any Chinese grocery.
recipes.kidNote: Pick the dried chili pieces out of the kids' portion before serving — the beans themselves aren't spicy on their own, only the flecks of chili are, so it's an easy fix rather than a reason to skip the dish.
recipes.nutritionNote: One of the lower-oil, higher-fiber dishes in the rotation once you skip deep-frying for the dry-sear method; the ya cai and soy sauce carry sodium, so no extra salt is needed at the table.

fil.description: Green beans na sini-sear dry sa scorching wok hanggang mag-blister at mag-wrinkle ang balat, tapos hinalo with ground pork, dried chili at preserved mustard greens — isang textural Sichuan side na wala talagang kahalintulad sa steamed green bean.
ingredients: dried red chilies, alisan ng buto at tadtarin
sui mi ya cai (preserved mustard greens), banlawan
steps: Painitin ang wok sa high heat hanggang bahagyang umuusok. Idagdag ang green beans at asin, tapos ibaba agad ang heat to medium.

I-sear ang beans for 15-20 minutes, haluin paminsan-minsan, hanggang mag-blister ang balat at may kaunting scorch marks; ang dry-searing na ito — hindi deep-frying — ang nagbibigay sa kanila ng wrinkled texture. Alisin at itabi.
Idagdag ang oil sa wok sa medium-high heat at i-brown ang ground pork, dudurugin habang niluluto.
Idagdag ang bawang at dried chilies; i-stir-fry 30 seconds hanggang mabango.
Idagdag ang ya cai at i-stir-fry 1 minute hanggang mabango.
Ibalik ang beans sa wok kasama ang Shaoxing wine, toyo, asukal at sesame oil. I-toss sa high heat for 1 minute hanggang malagyan nang maayos ang lahat.
Ihain mainit bilang side dish.
tips: Ang dry-sear ang buong technique: huwag magdagdag ng extra oil sa stage na ito, at huwag magmadali bago mag-15 minutes kung hindi mananatiling squeaky ang beans instead of blistered.
Ang sui mi ya cai ang gumagawa nito na parang galing sa Sichuan restaurant, hindi lang basta stir-fry improvisation — hanapin ang vacuum-packed na version sa kahit anong Chinese grocery.
fil.kidNote: Alisin muna ang mga piraso ng dried chili sa portion ng mga bata before ihain — hindi naman maanghang ang beans mismo, ang chili flecks lang, kaya madaling ayusin instead na i-skip na lang ang dish.
fil.nutritionNote: Isa ito sa mas mababa sa oil at mas mataas sa fiber na dishes sa rotation dahil dry-sear method na ginagamit instead of deep-frying; ang ya cai at toyo ang may dalang sodium, kaya hindi na kailangan ng extra salt sa table.

recipes.title: Egg Drop Soup
recipes.description: Chicken stock lightly thickened with cornstarch and swirled with a slow stream of beaten egg until it sets into silky ribbons — the fastest, gentlest soup in the Chinese home-cooking repertoire.
steps: Bring the chicken stock to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Stir in the sesame oil, salt, sugar and white pepper; taste and adjust seasoning.
Mix the cornstarch and water well, since it settles fast, then drizzle it into the simmering stock while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Simmer for a couple of minutes until the soup lightly thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Stir the soup in one direction with a ladle to create a gentle whirlpool, then slowly drizzle in the beaten eggs in a thin stream — the moving broth pulls them into silky ribbons instead of clumps.
Let the eggs set for 10-15 seconds without stirring, then give the soup one final gentle stir.
Ladle into bowls, top with chopped scallion, and serve immediately.
tips: Drizzle the egg in slowly while the broth is moving in a whirlpool — pouring it in all at once or into still broth gives you scrambled clumps instead of ribbons.
Mix the cornstarch slurry again right before adding it; it settles to the bottom of the bowl in under a minute.
recipes.nutritionNote: Light and low in fat on its own — the main thing to watch is sodium from the stock, so use a low-sodium broth or dilute a regular one, and treat this as a starter rather than the only protein at the table.

fil.description: Chicken stock na lightly thickened sa cornstarch at hinaluan ng slow stream ng binitin na itlog hanggang mag-set into silky ribbons — ang pinakamabilis at pinakamalambot na sabaw sa Chinese home-cooking repertoire.
steps: Pakuluan nang bahagya ang chicken stock sa pot.
Isama ang sesame oil, asin, asukal at white pepper; tikman at i-adjust ang seasoning.
Haluin nang mabuti ang cornstarch at tubig, dahil mabilis itong naglalagay, tapos i-drizzle ito sa kumukulong stock habang paulit-ulit na hinahalo para walang lumps.
I-simmer for a couple of minutes hanggang lumapot nang bahagya ang sabaw at ma-coat ang kutsara.

Haluin ang sabaw sa isang direksyon gamit ng laddle para gumawa ng gentle whirlpool, tapos dahan-dahang i-drizzle ang binitin na itlog into thin stream — ang gumagalaw na sabaw ang bumubuo sa silky ribbons instead of clumps.
Hayaang mag-set ang itlog for 10-15 seconds na hindi hinahalo, tapos isang huling gentle stir.
Isalin sa mga mangkok, topan ng tinadtad na scallion, at ihain agad.
tips: I-drizzle nang dahan-dahan ang itlog habang gumagalaw ang broth into whirlpool — kung ibubuhos lahat nang sabay o sa tahimik na broth, magiging scrambled clumps instead of ribbons.
Haluin ulit ang cornstarch slurry bago ito idagdag; nagse-settle ito sa ilalim ng bowl in under a minute.
fil.nutritionNote: Light at mababa sa taba ang sabaw na ito on its own — ang bantayan lang ay ang sodium mula sa stock, kaya gumamit ng low-sodium broth o i-dilute ang regular, at ituring itong starter lang instead of the only protein sa table.

recipes.title: Garlic Eggplant
recipes.localTitle: Yu Xiang Qie Zi (鱼香茄子)
recipes.description: Chinese eggplant fried until silky-soft, then tossed with ground pork in the sweet-sour-spicy "fish fragrant" sauce of doubanjiang, garlic and vinegar — no fish involved, just Sichuan's most famous flavor blend built around a vegetable.

ingredients.item: Chinese or Japanese eggplant, cut into thick batons
doubanjiang (Pixian chili bean paste), finely chopped
scallion, whites and greens separated, chopped

steps: Cut the eggplant into thick batons, toss with the salt, and let sit 10 minutes to draw out moisture; pat dry with paper towels before cooking so it fries instead of steams.
Heat half the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the eggplant in batches, turning occasionally, for 5-6 minutes per batch until soft and lightly browned all over; remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil and brown the ground pork over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until it starts to crisp at the edges.
Push the pork to one side, add the doubanjiang to the cleared space, and stir-fry until the oil turns red, about 1 minute, then mix it through the pork.
Add the garlic, ginger and scallion whites; stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the eggplant to the wok along with the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and stock. Simmer 2 minutes so the eggplant soaks up the sauce.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and toss until the sauce thickens and coats everything glossy.
Scatter with scallion greens and serve hot over rice.
tips: Salting and drying the eggplant before frying keeps it from turning into an oil sponge — skip this step and the dish gets greasy fast.
The sauce should taste balanced between sweet, sour, salty and spicy at once; that combination, not any actual fish, is what "fish fragrant" refers to.
recipes.kidNote: Doubanjiang brings real heat here with no numbing peppercorn involved, but it's still too spicy as written for young kids. Set aside a plain portion of fried eggplant before the doubanjiang goes in, then finish the kids' share with just garlic, a spoon of soy sauce, a little vinegar and sugar.
recipes.nutritionNote: Frying the eggplant adds meaningful oil even after salting and draining, so blot the finished dish with a paper towel if serving small portions, and the doubanjiang and soy sauce both carry sodium, so skip extra salt elsewhere in the meal.

fil.description: Chinese eggplant na pinirito hanggang silky-soft, tapos hinalo with giniling na baboy sa matamis-maasim-maanghang na "fish fragrant" sauce na gawa sa doubanjiang, bawang at suka — walang isda involved, Sichuan's most famous flavor blend lang na naka-base sa gulay.
ingredients: Chinese o Japanese eggplant, hiwain into thick batons
asin, para sa pag-aasin ng eggplant
doubanjiang (Pixian chili bean paste), tadtarin nang pino
scallion, ihiwalay ang puti at berde, tadtarin
steps: Hiwain ang eggplant into thick batons, haluin with asin, at hayaang mag-sit for 10 minutes para lumabas ang moisture; patuyuin gamit ang paper towels bago lutuin para mag-fry instead of mag-steam.

Painitin ang half ng oil sa wok sa medium-high heat at iprito ang eggplant in batches, baliktarin paminsan-minsan, for 5-6 minutes per batch hanggang lumambot at bahagyang mag-brown sa lahat ng parte; alisin at itabi muna.
Idagdag ang natitirang oil at i-brown ang giniling na baboy sa medium-high heat, durugin habang niluluto, hanggang magsimulang mag-crisp sa gilid.
Itulak ang baboy sa isang side, idagdag ang doubanjiang sa blangkong space, at i-stir-fry hanggang mamula ang oil, about 1 minute, tapos ihalo ito sa baboy.
Idagdag ang bawang, luya at puting parte ng scallion; i-stir-fry for 30 seconds hanggang umamoy masarap.
Ibalik ang eggplant sa wok kasama ang toyo, suka, asukal at stock. I-simmer for 2 minutes para masipsip ng eggplant ang sauce.
Ihalo ang cornstarch slurry at haluin hanggang lumapot ang sauce at ma-coat nang glossy ang lahat.
Budburan ng berdeng parte ng scallion at ihain nang mainit over rice.
tips: Ang pag-asin at pagpapatuyo sa eggplant bago iprito ang dahilan kung bakit hindi ito nagiging parang oil sponge — kapag nilaktawan ang step na ito, mabilis maging mamantika ang dish.
Dapat balanced ang lasa ng sauce sa matamis, maasim, maalat at maanghang nang sabay; ang combination na iyon, hindi naman totoong isda, ang tinutukoy ng "fish fragrant".
fil.kidNote: Totoong anghang ang dala ng doubanjiang dito, walang numbing peppercorn involved, pero masyado pa ring maanghang ito para sa mga bata as written. Maglaan ng plain na portion ng fried eggplant bago ilagay ang doubanjiang, tapos tapusin ang share ng mga bata with bawang lang, isang kutsarang toyo, kaunting suka at asukal.
fil.nutritionNote: Nagdadagdag ng meaningful na oil ang pagprito sa eggplant kahit na-asinan at na-drain na, kaya i-blot ng paper towel ang tapos na dish kung maliliit na portions ang ihahain, at pareho may sodium ang doubanjiang at toyo, kaya laktawan na lang ang extra asin sa ibang parte ng meal.

recipes.title: Hot and Sour Soup
recipes.description: A peppery, vinegar-forward broth thickened with cornstarch and loaded with tofu, wood ear mushroom and silky egg ribbons — the sharp, warming soup that opens a Sichuan-style home banquet.

ingredients.item: firm tofu, cut into thin strips
dried wood ear mushrooms, soaked in hot water 20 minutes and sliced
bamboo shoots, sliced into thin strips
lean pork, thinly sliced or shredded

ingredients.note: start with less, add more to taste

steps: Toss the sliced pork with the light soy sauce and cornstarch and let it sit 10 minutes while you prep everything else.
Bring the chicken stock to a simmer in a pot. Add the pork, stirring to separate the pieces, and cook 1-2 minutes until it turns opaque.
Add the tofu, wood ear mushrooms and bamboo shoots; simmer 3-4 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Stir in the vinegar, soy sauce, white pepper and salt; taste and adjust, keeping in mind the pepper's heat builds as it sits.
Give the cornstarch slurry a stir, since it settles fast, then drizzle it into the simmering soup while stirring constantly until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Stir the soup in one direction to create a gentle whirlpool, then slowly drizzle in the beaten eggs in a thin stream; let them set 10-15 seconds before stirring gently once more.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle with sesame oil, and top with sliced scallion.
Serve immediately, while the sourness and pepper are both at their sharpest.
tips: Add the white pepper gradually and taste as you go — it's the ingredient that makes this soup distinct from a plain sour soup, but it's easy to overdo.
Re-stir the cornstarch slurry right before pouring it in; it separates in under a minute sitting in the bowl.
recipes.nutritionNote: Vinegar-forward and naturally low in fat aside from a light drizzle of sesame oil at the end; the soy sauce and stock both add sodium, so use a low-sodium stock and serve smaller bowls as a soup course rather than the main protein.

fil.description: Peppery at vinegar-forward na broth na pinalapot ng cornstarch at puno ng tofu, wood ear mushroom at silky na egg ribbons — ang matalim at warming na soup na nagbubukas sa Sichuan-style home banquet.
ingredients: firm tofu, hiwain into thin strips
dried wood ear mushrooms, ibabad sa mainit na tubig for 20 minutes at hiwain
bamboo shoots, hiwain into thin strips
lean na baboy, hiwaing manipis o tadtarin
light soy sauce, para sa baboy
white pepper, magsimula sa konti, dagdagan to taste
steps: Haluin ang hiniwang baboy with light soy sauce at cornstarch at hayaang mag-sit for 10 minutes habang inihahanda ang iba pa.
Pakuluin ang chicken stock sa pot hanggang mag-simmer. Idagdag ang baboy, haluin para maihiwalay ang mga piraso, at lutuin for 1-2 minutes hanggang maging opaque.
Idagdag ang tofu, wood ear mushrooms at bamboo shoots; i-simmer for 3-4 minutes para maghalo ang lasa.
Ihalo ang suka, toyo, white pepper at asin; tikman at i-adjust, tandaan na lumalakas ang anghang ng pepper habang tumatagal.
Haluin ulit ang cornstarch slurry, dahil mabilis itong mag-settle, tapos ibuhos nang dahan-dahan sa kumukulong soup habang patuloy na hinahalo hanggang lumapot nang sapat para ma-coat ang kutsara.

Haluin ang soup sa isang direksyon para gumawa ng gentle whirlpool, tapos ibuhos nang dahan-dahan ang beaten na itlog nang parang manipis na stream; hayaang mag-set for 10-15 seconds bago haluin ulit nang dahan-dahan.
Isalok sa mangkok, lagyan ng sesame oil, at lagyan ng hiniwang scallion.
Ihain agad, habang pinakamatapang pa ang asim at anghang.
tips: Idagdag nang unti-unti ang white pepper at tikman habang nagdadagdag — ito ang ingredient na nagpapaiba sa soup na ito sa plain sour soup, pero madaling ma-overdo.
Haluin ulit ang cornstarch slurry bago mismo ibuhos; naghihiwalay ito in under a minute sa mangkok.
fil.nutritionNote: Vinegar-forward at naturally low sa taba maliban sa konting sesame oil sa dulo; nagdadagdag ng sodium ang toyo at stock, kaya gumamit ng low-sodium stock at maghain ng mas maliit na mangkok as soup course instead of main protein.

recipes.title: Kung Pao Chicken
recipes.localTitle: Gong Bao Ji Ding (宫保鸡丁)
recipes.description: Diced chicken velveted in cornstarch and Shaoxing wine, stir-fried with whole dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorn until numbing-hot, then finished in a sweet-sour sauce with peanuts — Sichuan's most famous export.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thigh or breast, cut into 1.5cm cubes
scallion, white parts only, cut into chunks
dried red chilies, snipped and deseeded

ingredients.note: mixed with 1 tbsp water or stock

steps: Combine the chicken with salt, light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine and cornstarch; mix well and marinate 15 minutes — this light velveting keeps the chicken juicy in the hot wok.
Snip the dried chilies into 2-3cm pieces and shake out the seeds; slice the garlic and ginger; cut the scallion whites into chunks.
Stir together the sauce ingredients (sugar, cornstarch slurry, dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, black vinegar and sesame oil) in a small bowl.

Heat the peanut oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns and stir-fry until the chilies darken and the oil is fragrant, about 30 seconds — pull off the heat if they start to smoke, or the dish turns bitter.
Turn the heat to high, add the marinated chicken, and stir-fry until the pieces separate and turn opaque, about 2 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and scallion whites; stir-fry until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and stir-fry until it thickens and coats the chicken glossy, about 30 seconds.
Stir in the roasted peanuts, toss once, and serve immediately.
tips: Keep the chilies moving and pull the wok off the heat the moment they darken — scorched chilies turn the whole dish bitter, not just spicy.
Cornstarch in both the marinade and the sauce is what gives the glossy, clinging texture restaurants get.
recipes.kidNote: Kung pao gets its heat from whole dried chilies and its tingle from Sichuan peppercorn — both genuinely upset young kids. Cook the kids' portion as a separate small batch: skip the chilies and peppercorn entirely, stir-fry the chicken with just the garlic, ginger and sauce, then toss with peanuts.
recipes.nutritionNote: The peanuts and frying oil make this calorie-dense and the double soy sauce adds real sodium, so balance the plate with a plain vegetable side and go easy on extra salt elsewhere in the meal.

fil.description: Diced na manok, velveted sa cornstarch at Shaoxing wine, sini-stir-fry with whole dried chilies at Sichuan peppercorn hanggang numbing-hot, tapos fifinish sa sweet-sour sauce with peanuts — ang pinaka-famous export ng Sichuan.
ingredients: boneless chicken thigh o breast, hiwain into 1.5cm cubes
scallion, white parts lang, hiwain into chunks
dried red chilies, gupitin at alisan ng buto
cornstarch, haluin sa 1 tbsp tubig o stock
steps: I-combine ang manok sa asin, light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine at cornstarch; haluin nang mabuti tapos i-marinate for 15 minutes — ito ang light velveting na siyang nagpapanatiling juicy ng manok sa mainit na wok.
Guntingin ang dried chilies into 2-3cm pieces at tanggalin ang buto; hiwain ang bawang at luya; hiwain ang scallion whites into chunks.
Haluin ang sauce ingredients (asukal, cornstarch slurry, dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, black vinegar at sesame oil) sa maliit na bowl.

Painitin ang peanut oil sa wok sa medium heat. Idagdag ang dried chilies at Sichuan peppercorns tapos i-stir-fry hanggang dumilim ang chilies at mabango ang oil, about 30 seconds — alisin agad sa apoy kung nagsimulang umusok, para hindi pumait ang dish.
Taasan ang heat to high, idagdag ang marinated chicken, at i-stir-fry hanggang maghiwalay ang mga piraso at maging opaque, about 2 minutes.
Idagdag ang bawang, luya at scallion whites; i-stir-fry hanggang mabango, about 30 seconds.
Ibuhos ang sauce at i-stir-fry hanggang lumapot at ma-coat nang glossy ang manok, about 30 seconds.
Isama ang roasted peanuts, i-toss once, at ihain agad.
tips: Bantayan ang mga chilies at alisin agad sa apoy ang wok pag nagsimulang dumilim — pag na-scorch ang chilies, pumapait ang buong dish, hindi lang basta maanghang.
Ang cornstarch sa marinade at sa sauce ang nagbibigay ng glossy, clinging texture na ginagawa ng mga restaurant.
fil.kidNote: Ang anghang ng kung pao ay galing sa whole dried chilies at ang tingle naman ay sa Sichuan peppercorn — pareho itong genuinely nakakaabala sa mga bata. Lutuin ang portion ng mga bata bilang separate small batch: skip ang chilies at peppercorn entirely, i-stir-fry ang manok with bawang, luya at sauce lang, tapos toss with peanuts.
fil.nutritionNote: Calorie-dense ito dahil sa peanuts at frying oil, at may real sodium dahil sa double soy sauce, kaya i-balance ng plain vegetable side at bawasan ang extra salt sa iba pang ulam.

recipes.title: Mapo Tofu
recipes.description: Silken tofu simmered in a fiery, numbing sauce of Pixian chili bean paste, fermented black beans and ground meat, finished with a dusting of ground Sichuan pepper — the dish that defines Sichuan's mala flavor.

ingredients.item: soft or silken-firm tofu, cut into 2cm cubes
doubanjiang (Pixian chili bean paste), finely chopped
fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped

steps: Bring a pot of lightly salted water to just below a simmer. Add the tofu cubes and let them sit in the hot water for 10 minutes to firm up and season lightly; drain gently.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium-high heat and brown the ground meat, breaking it up, until crisp at the edges; remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok and stir-fry the doubanjiang over medium heat until the oil turns red, about 1 minute.
Add the black beans, ground chili, garlic and ginger; stir-fry until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, bring to a simmer, then slide in the drained tofu and the browned meat. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, spooning the sauce over the tofu without stirring hard, since it breaks easily.
Add the scallions and season with sugar and a little salt if needed; simmer 1 more minute until the scallions soften.
Drizzle in the cornstarch slurry a little at a time, gently folding, until the sauce clings to the tofu in a silky coat.
Transfer to a serving bowl and finish with a generous dusting of ground Sichuan pepper.
tips: Slide a spatula gently under the tofu instead of stirring — mapo tofu should look rustic and whole, not mashed.
Seek out Pixian doubanjiang specifically; other chili bean pastes are saltier and less complex.
recipes.kidNote: Split the pot before the Sichuan pepper goes on: spoon out the kids' portion first, use half the usual doubanjiang when you build the sauce so their share isn't as salty-spicy, and never dust their bowls with the ground Sichuan pepper — the numbing sensation upsets kids more than the heat itself.
recipes.nutritionNote: Doubanjiang and black beans are both salty ferments and the dish is served over rice, so skip extra soy sauce at the table and add a side of blanched greens since the dish itself has no vegetables besides scallion.

fil.description: Silken tofu na sini-simmer sa fiery at numbing sauce ng Pixian chili bean paste, fermented black beans at ground meat, fifinish ng budbod na ground Sichuan pepper — ang dish na siyang defines mala flavor ng Sichuan.
ingredients: soft o silken-firm tofu, hiwain into 2cm cubes
doubanjiang (Pixian chili bean paste), tinadtad nang pino
fermented black beans, banlawan at tadtarin
ground chili, optional, i-adjust sa panlasa
cornstarch, haluin sa 2 tbsp malamig na tubig
ground roasted Sichuan pepper, para sa paghahain
steps: Pakuluan nang bahagya ang lightly salted na tubig hanggang just below a simmer. Idagdag ang tofu cubes at hayaang maupo sa mainit na tubig for 10 minutes para lumapot at ma-season nang bahagya; i-drain nang dahan-dahan.
Painitin ang 1 tbsp oil sa wok sa medium-high heat at i-brown ang ground meat, dudurugin habang niluluto, hanggang crisp ang edges; alisin at itabi.
Idagdag ang natitirang oil sa wok at i-stir-fry ang doubanjiang sa medium heat hanggang mamula ang oil, about 1 minute.
Idagdag ang black beans, ground chili, bawang at luya; i-stir-fry hanggang mabango, about 1 minute.

Ibuhos ang stock, pakuluin nang bahagya, tapos idagdag ang drained tofu at ang browned meat. I-simmer nang dahan-dahan for 5 minutes, isabog ang sauce sa ibabaw ng tofu na hindi masyadong haluin dahil madaling madurog ito.
Idagdag ang scallions at i-season ng asukal at kaunting asin kung kailangan; i-simmer 1 more minute hanggang lumambot ang scallions.
I-drizzle ang cornstarch slurry nang paunti-unti, i-fold nang dahan-dahan, hanggang mag-cling ang sauce sa tofu into silky coat.
Ilipat sa serving bowl at i-finish ng generous na budbod ng ground Sichuan pepper.
tips: Gumamit ng spatula nang dahan-dahan sa ilalim ng tofu instead of haluin — dapat rustic at buo ang itsura ng mapo tofu, hindi durog.
Hanapin talaga ang Pixian doubanjiang — mas maalat at less complex ang ibang chili bean pastes.
fil.kidNote: Hatiin muna ang pot bago ilagay ang Sichuan pepper: kunin muna ang portion ng mga bata, gamitin ang half ng usual na doubanjiang habang ginagawa ang sauce para hindi masyadong maalat-maanghang ang share nila, at huwag talaga budburan ng ground Sichuan pepper ang mangkok nila — mas nakakaabala sa mga bata ang numbing sensation kaysa sa anghang mismo.
fil.nutritionNote: Parehong salty ferments ang doubanjiang at black beans at inihahain ito over rice, kaya skip na lang ang extra soy sauce sa table at magdagdag ng blanched greens dahil walang gulay ang dish mismo maliban sa scallion.

recipes.title: Red-Braised Pork Belly
recipes.description: Pork belly blanched, caramelized in melted rock sugar, then slow-braised in soy sauce and Shaoxing wine until the fat turns glossy and spoon-tender — Shanghai's signature sweet-savory braise.

ingredients.item: skin-on pork belly, cut into 2cm cubes

ingredients.note: enough to mostly cover the pork; top up as needed

steps: Cut the pork belly into 2cm cubes, cover with water in a pot, and bring to a boil for 1 minute until the surface turns opaque. Drain and rinse to remove impurities.
Wipe out the pot. Over low heat, melt the rock sugar in the oil, swirling gently until it turns a light amber.
Add the blanched pork belly and raise the heat to medium; cook, stirring, until the pieces are lightly browned and coated in caramel.
Reduce the heat to low, pour in the Shaoxing wine, and let it bubble for 2 minutes to cook off the raw alcohol smell.
Stir in the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and enough water to mostly cover the pork.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring every 10 minutes and topping up water if it runs dry, until the pork is fork-tender.
Uncover, raise the heat, and stir constantly until the sauce reduces to a thick, glossy coating on the pork.
Serve hot over steamed rice.
tips: Don't let the sugar go past light amber — burnt caramel turns the whole braise bitter.
Make it a day ahead: the flavor deepens overnight and the fat sets, so you can skim it before reheating.
recipes.nutritionNote: Pork belly is fat-forward and the braise is salt-heavy from two soy sauces, so serve modest portions alongside plain rice and a big plate of steamed or blanched greens to balance it.

fil.description: Pork belly na binlanch muna, tapos ka-caramelize sa melted rock sugar, then slow-braised sa toyo at Shaoxing wine hanggang maging glossy at spoon-tender ang taba — ito ang signature sweet-savory braise ng Shanghai.
ingredients: skin-on pork belly, hiwain into 2cm cubes
tubig, sapat lang para matakpan ang pork; dagdagan kung kailangan
steps: Hiwain ang pork belly into 2cm cubes, takpan ng tubig sa pot, at pakuluan for 1 minute hanggang maging opaque ang surface. I-drain at hugasan para maalis ang mga impurities.
Punasan ang pot. Sa low heat, i-melt ang rock sugar sa oil, i-swirl nang dahan-dahan hanggang maging light amber ang kulay.
Idagdag ang blanched pork belly at taasan ang heat to medium; lutuin, haluin, hanggang lightly browned ang mga piraso at naka-coat sa caramel.
Ibaba ang heat to low, ibuhos ang Shaoxing wine, at hayaang mag-bubble for 2 minutes para maalis ang raw alcohol smell.
Isama ang light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, at sapat na tubig para halos matakpan ang pork.
Takpan at i-simmer sa medium-low heat for 45 minutes to 1 hour, haluin every 10 minutes at dagdagan ng tubig kung natutuyo, hanggang fork-tender na ang pork.
Alisin ang takip, taasan ang heat, at patuloy na haluin hanggang mag-reduce ang sauce into thick, glossy coating sa pork.
Ihain mainit over steamed rice.
tips: Huwag hayaang lumagpas sa light amber ang sugar — burnt caramel makakapapait sa buong braise.
Gawin isang araw before: lalim pa ang lasa overnight at nagse-set ang taba, para ma-skim mo before i-reheat.
fil.nutritionNote: Fat-forward ang pork belly at salty ang braise dahil sa two soy sauces, kaya ihain ng modest portions kasama ng plain rice at malaking plato ng steamed or blanched greens para ma-balance.

recipes.title: Shrimp with Scrambled Egg
recipes.localTitle: Hua Dan Xia Ren (滑蛋虾仁)
recipes.description: Shrimp seared just until pink and folded into soft, glossy scrambled eggs off the heat — a fast Cantonese home-style plate that turns two humble ingredients into something silky.
steps: Peel and devein the shrimp, then pat dry. Season with salt and white pepper, then toss in the cornstarch last so it coats the surface without diluting into the shrimp.
Let the shrimp sit for 10 minutes while you beat the eggs with a little oil, salt and sugar.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and sear the shrimp for about 1 minute per side until just pink and curled; remove and set aside — they'll finish cooking with the eggs.
Wipe out the wok, add a little more oil, and pour in the beaten eggs.
Let the bottom set for about 10 seconds, then use a spatula to fold the cooked layer over so uncooked egg flows underneath; repeat for about 30 seconds total.
Fold the shrimp back into the eggs, turn off the heat, and let the residual heat finish setting the eggs into soft, glossy curds, about 15-20 more seconds.
Scatter with scallion and serve immediately over rice.
tips: Season the shrimp with salt and pepper first and add the cornstarch last — it coats better and gives a cleaner sear than mixing everything at once.
Turn the heat off before the eggs look fully set; they keep cooking in the residual heat of the wok and firm up too much if you wait for that on the stove.
recipes.nutritionNote: A lean, high-protein, low-carb plate on its own, good for balancing out a heavier dish like sweet and sour pork on the same table — just pair with rice or a vegetable side since it has no fiber of its own.

fil.description: Hipon na sini-sear lang hanggang pink at hinalo sa soft at glossy scrambled eggs, patay na ang apoy — mabilis na Cantonese home-style plate na ginagawang silky ang dalawang simpleng ingredients.
ingredients: hipon, balatan at alisan ng ugat
steps: Balatan at alisan ng ugat ang hipon, tapos punasan hanggang matuyo. I-season ng asin at white pepper, tapos idagdag ang cornstarch huling-huli para ma-coat ang surface na hindi lumusaw sa hipon.
Hayaang maupo ang hipon for 10 minutes habang binibitin ang itlog with kaunting oil, asin at asukal.
Painitin ang oil sa wok sa high heat at i-sear ang hipon for about 1 minute per side hanggang just pink at naka-curl; alisin at itabi — matatapos ang pagluluto nila kasama ng itlog.
Punasan ang wok, magdagdag ng kaunting oil, at ibuhos ang binitin na itlog.
Hayaang mag-set ang ilalim for about 10 seconds, tapos gamitin ang spatula para i-fold ang cooked layer para dumaloy ang uncooked egg sa ilalim; ulitin for about 30 seconds total.
I-fold ang hipon pabalik sa itlog, patayin ang apoy, at hayaang tapusin ng residual heat ang pag-set ng itlog into soft at glossy curds, about 15-20 more seconds.
Budburan ng scallion at ihain agad over rice.
tips: I-season muna ng asin at pepper ang hipon tapos idagdag ang cornstarch huli — mas maganda ang coating at mas malinis ang sear kaysa haluin lahat nang sabay.
Patayin ang apoy bago pa fully set ang itlog; tuloy pa rin ang pagluluto nila sa residual heat ng wok at magiging masyadong matigas kung hihintayin mo pa sa kalan.
fil.nutritionNote: Lean, high-protein at low-carb na plate ito on its own, maganda para i-balance ang mas mabigat na dish gaya ng sweet and sour pork sa parehong table — isabay lang sa kanin o vegetable side dahil walang fiber ang dish mismo.

recipes.title: Soy Sauce Chicken
recipes.description: A whole chicken gently poached in a spiced soy sauce master stock until just cooked through, then bathed in the cooling liquid for silky, deeply seasoned meat and glossy amber skin — Cantonese roast-meat-shop cooking at home.

ingredients.note: for brushing the skin at the end

steps: Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking so it isn't cold going into the pot.

Heat the oil in a pot just large enough to hold the chicken. Add the ginger and scallion and cook over medium-low heat until fragrant and lightly caramelized, about 1 minute, then add the star anise and cinnamon.
Pour in the Shaoxing wine and let it bubble 1 minute, then add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar and water. Bring to a simmer and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Lower the whole chicken breast-side down into the simmering sauce; it should be at least two-thirds submerged. Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes.

Flip the chicken breast-side up, cover, and simmer another 15 minutes, then turn off the heat and let the chicken sit in the hot sauce, covered, for 20 minutes to finish cooking through without drying out.
Check doneness by piercing the thickest part of the thigh — the juices should run clear with no pink. Lift the chicken out and brush the skin with sesame oil for shine.
Rest 10 minutes, then chop into pieces and spoon some of the sauce over the top to serve.
Strain and save the remaining sauce; it keeps in the fridge for weeks and can be reused as a master stock for the next batch.
tips: Turning off the heat and letting the chicken finish in the residual heat of the sauce, rather than simmering it the whole time, is what keeps the breast meat silky instead of stringy.
Save the strained master sauce — each reuse gets more complex, and it's the traditional way this dish is made in Cantonese homes.
recipes.nutritionNote: The poaching method needs almost no added fat, but the sauce itself is concentrated soy and salty even diluted with water, so spoon it sparingly over the meat and serve with plain rice and a vegetable side rather than more sauce at the table.

fil.description: Isang whole chicken na dahan-dahang pinoach sa spiced soy sauce master stock hanggang cooked through lang, tapos ibinabad sa cooling liquid para maging silky at deeply seasoned ang karne at glossy amber ang balat — Cantonese roast-meat-shop cooking sa bahay.
ingredients: sesame oil, for brushing sa balat sa dulo
steps: Ilabas ang manok sa fridge 30 minutes bago magluto para hindi malamig kapag inilagay sa pot.

Painitin ang oil sa pot na sapat kalaki para sa manok. Idagdag ang luya at scallion at lutuin sa medium-low heat hanggang umamoy masarap at bahagyang mag-caramelize, about 1 minute, tapos idagdag ang star anise at cinnamon.
Ibuhos ang Shaoxing wine at hayaang mag-bubble for 1 minute, tapos idagdag ang light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar at tubig. I-simmer at haluin hanggang matunaw ang asukal.
Ibaba ang whole chicken nang paharap sa ilalim ang breast sa simmering sauce; dapat two-thirds submerged at least. Takpan at i-simmer nang mahinay for 15 minutes.

Baliktarin ang manok nang paharap sa itaas ang breast, takpan, at i-simmer ulit for 15 minutes, tapos patayin ang apoy at hayaang mag-sit ang manok sa mainit na sauce, nakatakip, for 20 minutes para matapos maluto nang tuluyan nang hindi natutuyo.
I-check ang doneness sa pagtusok sa pinakamakapal na parte ng hita — dapat malinaw ang tumutulong juice, walang pink. Buhatin ang manok at pahiran ang balat ng sesame oil para kumintab.
Ipahinga for 10 minutes, tapos hiwain into pieces at ibuhos ang kaunti sa sauce sa ibabaw bago ihain.
I-strain at itago ang natitirang sauce; tumatagal ito sa fridge for weeks at pwedeng gamitin ulit as master stock for the next batch.
tips: Ang pagpatay ng apoy at pagpapatapos sa manok gamit ang residual heat ng sauce, instead of i-simmer nang buong oras, ang dahilan kung bakit silky ang breast meat imbes na stringy.
Itago ang na-strain na master sauce — mas complex ang lasa kada gamit ulit, at ito ang traditional way ng dish na ito sa mga Cantonese home.
fil.nutritionNote: Halos walang added fat na kailangan ang poaching method, pero concentrated soy at maalat pa rin ang sauce kahit may tubig na, kaya ibuhos nang konti lang over the meat at ihain with plain rice at vegetable side instead of dagdag pang sauce sa table.

recipes.title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallion
recipes.description: A whole fish steamed just until the flesh flakes, doused in a sizzling hot oil over ginger and scallion — the centerpiece of a Cantonese family dinner and proof the simplest method is the hardest to get right.

ingredients.item: whole tilapia or sea bass, cleaned and scored
ginger, half julienned and half sliced

steps: Pat the fish dry and score the thickest part of the flesh a few times so it cooks evenly. Tuck a few ginger slices under the fish on the plate to keep it off the pooling liquid.
Scatter half the julienned ginger and scallion over the fish.

Set up a steamer with plenty of water at a rolling boil. Lower the fish in on its plate, cover, and steam over high heat for 10-12 minutes until the thickest part is opaque and the eyes have turned white.
While the fish steams, combine the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, white pepper, water, sugar and salt in a small saucepan and bring to a brief simmer; keep warm.
Carefully lift the fish out, tilt the plate to drain off the cloudy steaming liquid, and discard it — this liquid tastes fishy and would ruin the sauce.
Top the fish with the remaining fresh ginger, scallion and cilantro, then pour the warm seasoned sauce over it.
Heat the neutral oil and sesame oil in a small pan until just shimmering and starting to smoke, then carefully pour it over the scallions and ginger — it should sizzle loudly and wilt them instantly.
Serve immediately straight from the plate.
tips: Buy the freshest fish you can — with only ginger, scallion and soy sauce, there's nowhere for off flavors to hide.
Don't skip draining the steaming liquid before saucing; it carries the fishy smell and would make the whole plate taste muddy.
recipes.nutritionNote: A lean white fish steamed with almost no added fat until the final oil drizzle — the lightest main in the rotation, so pair it with a starchier side like fried rice to round out the meal.

fil.description: Isang buong isda na sini-steam lang hanggang mag-flake ang laman, binuhusan ng sizzling hot oil sa ibabaw ng luya at scallion — ang centerpiece ng Cantonese family dinner at patunay na ang pinakasimpleng technique ang pinakamahirap gawin nang tama.
ingredients: buong tilapia o sea bass, nilinis at may guhit
luya, half julienned at half hiwain
steps: Punasan ang isda hanggang matuyo at guhitan ang pinakamakapal na parte ng laman nang ilang beses para pantay ang pagkaluto. Ilagay ang ilang hiwa ng luya sa ilalim ng isda sa plato para hindi ito matakpan ng natitirang tubig.
Isabog ang half ng julienned na luya at scallion sa ibabaw ng isda.

Ihanda ang steamer na maraming tubig at nasa rolling boil. Ibaba ang isda kasama ang plato nito, takpan, at i-steam sa high heat for 10-12 minutes hanggang opaque na ang pinakamakapal na parte at puti na ang mata.
Habang niluluto ang isda, i-combine ang light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, white pepper, tubig, asukal at asin sa maliit na saucepan at pakuluan nang bahagya; panatilihing mainit.
Dahan-dahang buhatin ang isda, ikiling ang plato para matanggal ang cloudy steaming liquid, tapos itapon ito — mabaho ito at masisira ang sauce.
Ilagay sa ibabaw ng isda ang natitirang sariwang luya, scallion at cilantro, tapos ibuhos ang mainit na seasoned sauce dito.

Painitin ang neutral oil at sesame oil sa maliit na kawali hanggang shimmering at halos umuusok, tapos dahan-dahang ibuhos ito sa scallions at luya — dapat sumingasing nang malakas at agad malanta ang mga ito.
Ihain agad diretso sa plato.
tips: Bumili ng pinakasariwang isda na makakaya mo — sa ginger, scallion at soy sauce lang, walang matataguan ang off flavors.
Huwag laktawan ang pag-drain ng steaming liquid before i-sauce; mabaho ito at masisira ang lasa ng buong plato.
fil.nutritionNote: Lean white fish na sini-steam with almost no added fat hanggang sa final oil drizzle — ang pinaka-light na main sa rotation, kaya isabay sa starchier side gaya ng fried rice para kumpleto ang meal.

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Bok Choy with Mushrooms
recipes.description: Baby bok choy and shiitake mushrooms stir-fried hot and fast with garlic, then glazed with oyster sauce — the everyday vegetable side that shows up on nearly every Cantonese family dinner table.

ingredients.item: baby bok choy, halved or quartered lengthwise

steps: Wash the bok choy thoroughly, since dirt hides in the base, and halve or quarter each head lengthwise.
Stir together the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar and water or stock in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering, then add the garlic and stir-fry 10 seconds until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and stir-fry 2 minutes until they soften and start to brown at the edges.
Add the bok choy and stir-fry 1-2 minutes until the leaves wilt and the stems turn bright green but stay crisp.
Pour in the sauce, toss for 30 seconds until it reduces to a light glaze coating the vegetables, then drizzle in the sesame oil.
Serve immediately while the bok choy is still crisp-tender.
tips: Cook the bok choy stems and leaves together but keep the total time short — overcooked bok choy turns watery and loses its bite.
Fresh shiitakes give more texture than dried here since the vegetable itself is the point, not a rehydrated mushroom flavor base.
recipes.nutritionNote: A genuinely low-oil, high-fiber vegetable side; the oyster sauce is the only sodium source, so this pairs well alongside a saltier main like char siu or soy sauce chicken without pushing the whole meal over on salt.

fil.description: Baby bok choy at shiitake mushrooms na na-stir-fry nang mabilis at mainit with bawang, tapos na-glaze ng oyster sauce — everyday na vegetable side na lumalabas sa halos lahat ng Cantonese family dinner table.
ingredients: baby bok choy, hatiin o quarter-in nang lengthwise
steps: Hugasan nang mabuti ang bok choy, dahil nagtatago ang dumi sa base, at hatiin o quarter-in ang bawat head nang lengthwise.
Ihalo ang oyster sauce, toyo, asukal at tubig o stock sa maliit na mangkok.
Painitin ang oil sa wok sa high heat hanggang shimmering, tapos idagdag ang bawang at i-stir-fry for 10 seconds hanggang umamoy masarap.
Idagdag ang mushrooms at i-stir-fry for 2 minutes hanggang lumambot at magsimulang mag-brown sa gilid.
Idagdag ang bok choy at i-stir-fry for 1-2 minutes hanggang malanta ang dahon at maging bright green ang tangkay pero crisp pa rin.
Ibuhos ang sauce, haluin for 30 seconds hanggang lumapot into light glaze na coating sa gulay, tapos lagyan ng sesame oil.
Ihain agad habang crisp-tender pa ang bok choy.
tips: Lutuin nang sabay ang tangkay at dahon ng bok choy pero panatilihing maikli ang total time — kapag overcooked ang bok choy, nagiging watery ito at nawawala ang bite.
Mas maraming texture ang fresh shiitakes kaysa sa dried dito dahil ang gulay mismo ang punto, hindi rehydrated na mushroom flavor base.
fil.nutritionNote: Genuinely low-oil at high-fiber na vegetable side; ang oyster sauce lang ang sodium source, kaya maganda itong i-pair with mas maalat na main gaya ng char siu o soy sauce chicken nang hindi masyadong tumataas ang asin ng buong meal.

recipes.title: Sweet and Sour Pork
recipes.description: Pork double-fried until shatteringly crisp, then tossed in a ketchup-and-vinegar sauce simmered slowly with star anise until glossy — the dish that makes even reluctant vegetable-avoiders happy at the table.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder or tenderloin, cut into bite-sized chunks

ingredients.note: reserve 1 tsp for the sauce-thickening slurry
about 1 liter, or enough to submerge the pork

ingredients.item: green bell pepper, cut into 3cm squares

steps: Toss the pork with the marinade (water, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic powder and onion powder) until no liquid remains; set aside for 30 minutes.

Make the sauce base: heat oil in a small saucepan, add the ginger and star anise, and cook until fragrant and lightly caramelized, about 1 minute. Add the ketchup and stir until it darkens slightly, about 2 minutes.
Add the vinegar, sugar and reserved pineapple juice. Simmer uncovered on low heat, stirring occasionally, for about 30 minutes until the sauce is glossy and coats the back of a spoon.
Heat the deep-frying oil to 175°C (350°F). Dredge the marinated pork in the flour-cornstarch mixture, dip in the beaten egg, then dredge again.
Fry the pork in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden and cooked through; drain. Just before serving, re-fry all the pork for 30-60 seconds to make it extra crisp.
Stir-fry the bell pepper and onion in a splash of oil over high heat for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sweet and sour sauce and the pineapple chunks; simmer to thicken, adding a little of the reserved cornstarch mixed with water if it needs to tighten further.
Add the crispy pork, toss quickly to coat without letting it sit in the sauce, and serve immediately so it stays crunchy.
tips: Fry the pork twice: once to cook it through, then a fast second fry right before saucing — that's what keeps it crunchy under the sauce instead of going soggy.
Toss the fried pork into the sauce only right before serving; sauced pork left to sit loses its crunch fast.
recipes.nutritionNote: This is the richest dish in the rotation, deep-fried batter plus a sugar-and-ketchup sauce, so treat it as an occasional treat, serve smaller portions alongside plenty of plain rice and a green vegetable, and skip other fried or sweet dishes at the same meal.

fil.description: Pork na double-fried hanggang shatteringly crisp, tapos hinalo sa ketchup-and-vinegar sauce na sini-simmer nang mabagal with star anise hanggang glossy — ang dish na nagpapasaya kahit sa mga ayaw kumain ng gulay.
ingredients: pork shoulder o tenderloin, hiwain into bite-sized chunks
garlic powder, plus 1/4 tsp onion powder
cornstarch, itabi ang 1 tsp para sa sauce-thickening slurry
green bell pepper, hiwain into 3cm squares
steps: I-toss ang pork sa marinade (tubig, toyo, sesame oil, garlic powder at onion powder) hanggang walang natitirang liquid; itabi for 30 minutes.
