Gawin ang sauce base: painitin ang oil sa maliit na saucepan, idagdag ang luya at star anise, at lutuin hanggang mabango at lightly caramelized, about 1 minute. Idagdag ang ketchup at haluin hanggang bahagyang dumilim, about 2 minutes.

Idagdag ang vinegar, asukal at itinabing pineapple juice. I-simmer nang hindi natatakpan sa low heat, haluin paminsan-minsan, for about 30 minutes hanggang glossy ang sauce at ma-coat ang likod ng kutsara.
Painitin ang deep-frying oil to 175°C (350°F). I-dredge ang marinated pork sa flour-cornstarch mixture, isawsaw sa binitin na itlog, tapos i-dredge ulit.
Iprito ang pork in batches for 2-3 minutes hanggang golden at luto na; i-drain. Bago ihain, i-re-fry ulit ang lahat ng pork for 30-60 seconds para maging extra crisp.
I-stir-fry ang bell pepper at sibuyas sa splash ng oil sa high heat for 30 seconds.
Ibuhos ang sweet and sour sauce at ang pineapple chunks; i-simmer para lumapot, dagdagan ng kaunting itinabing cornstarch mixture na hinaluan ng tubig kung kailangan pang lumapot.
Idagdag ang crispy pork, i-toss agad para ma-coat na hindi tumatagal sa sauce, at ihain agad para manatiling crunchy.
tips: I-prito nang dalawang beses ang pork: una para maluto, tapos fast second fry bago i-sauce — iyon ang gumagawa nito na crunchy pa rin sa ilalim ng sauce instead of soggy.
I-toss lang ang pinaprito na pork sa sauce bago ihain; nawawalan ng crunch agad ang pork kung matagal sa sauce.
fil.nutritionNote: Ito ang pinakamayaman na dish sa rotation, deep-fried batter plus sugar-and-ketchup sauce, kaya ituring itong occasional treat, ihain ng mas maliit na portions kasama ng maraming plain rice at green vegetable, at iwasan ang ibang fried o sweet na dishes sa parehong meal.

recipes.title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
recipes.localTitle: Fan Qie Chao Dan (番茄炒蛋)
recipes.description: Ripe tomatoes stir-fried down into a sweet-savory sauce and folded through soft scrambled eggs — the dish every Chinese kid grows up eating over rice, ready faster than delivery.
steps: Cut the tomatoes into wedges and finely chop the scallions.
Crack the eggs into a bowl with half the salt, the white pepper, sesame oil and Shaoxing wine; beat well for a minute.
Heat a wok over medium heat until smoking, add half the oil, and pour in the eggs. Scramble into large soft curds and remove before fully set; set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok, turn the heat to high, and stir-fry the tomatoes and scallions for 1 minute until they just start to release their juice.
Add the sugar, remaining salt and water; stir to combine.
Return the eggs to the wok, cover, and cook 1-2 minutes until the tomatoes have broken down into a light sauce.
Uncover and stir-fry over high heat until the sauce reaches a loose, saucy consistency that coats rice well.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.
tips: Scramble the eggs until just barely set and pull them early — they finish cooking when folded back in, and overcooked eggs turn rubbery.
Use the ripest, reddest tomatoes you can find; the whole sauce is built from their juice plus a little sugar to round out the acidity.
recipes.nutritionNote: A genuinely balanced weeknight plate with real vegetable content from the tomatoes plus protein from the eggs — just watch the added sugar and oil if serving very small portions.

fil.description: Hinog na kamatis na sini-stir-fry hanggang maging sweet-savory sauce at hinalo sa soft scrambled eggs — ang dish na kinakain ng bawat batang Chinese habang lumalaki over rice, mas mabilis pa kaysa delivery.
steps: Hiwain ang kamatis into wedges at tadtarin nang pino ang scallions.
Basagin ang itlog sa bowl kasama ang half ng asin, white pepper, sesame oil at Shaoxing wine; i-beat nang mabuti for a minute.
Painitin ang wok sa medium heat hanggang umuusok, idagdag ang half ng oil, at ibuhos ang itlog. I-scramble into large soft curds at alisin before fully set; itabi.
Idagdag ang natitirang oil sa wok, taasan ang heat to high, at i-stir-fry ang kamatis at scallions for 1 minute hanggang magsimulang lumabas ang katas nito.
Idagdag ang asukal, natitirang asin at tubig; haluin.
Ibalik ang itlog sa wok, takpan, at lutuin for 1-2 minutes hanggang madurog ang kamatis into light sauce.
Alisin ang takip at i-stir-fry sa high heat hanggang umabot sa loose at saucy consistency na nag-coat nang maayos sa kanin.
Ihain agad over steamed rice.
tips: I-scramble ang itlog hanggang just barely set at alisin agad — matatapos ang pagluluto nila kapag inihalo ulit, at nagiging rubbery ang overcooked na itlog.
Gumamit ng pinakahinog at pinakapulang kamatis — ang buong sauce ay galing sa katas nila plus kaunting asukal para i-balance ang acidity.
fil.nutritionNote: Genuinely balanced na weeknight plate na may real vegetable content mula sa kamatis plus protein mula sa itlog — bantayan lang ang added sugar at oil kung maliliit na portions ang ihahain.

recipes.title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
recipes.description: Day-old rice fried hot and fast with shrimp, char siu, egg, carrot and peas until every grain separates — Yangzhou's answer to leftovers and the fried rice every other version gets compared to.

ingredients.note: cook a day ahead and cool completely

ingredients.item: shrimp, peeled, deveined and halved lengthwise
scallion, white and green parts separated, chopped

steps: Cook the rice with slightly less water than usual so the grains stay firm; spread out and cool completely, ideally a day ahead — wet, fresh rice turns fried rice mushy.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Blanch the carrot and peas for 30-40 seconds, then add the shrimp and cook until just pink, about 2 more minutes. Drain and set aside.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of the salt.
Heat a wok over high heat for a minute, add 1 tablespoon of oil until rippling, then pour in the eggs. Let them set for 10-15 seconds, then add the cold rice directly on top.
Break up the rice clumps and stir-fry for 2.5-3 minutes over high heat until each grain separates and you hear a light crackle.
Lower the heat, add half the salt and the soy sauce, and toss to coat evenly.
Push the rice to the sides of the wok, add the char siu to the center to warm through, then mix it in along with the blanched vegetables, shrimp and scallion whites.
Raise the heat to high, drizzle in the remaining oil for shine, toss everything together, and finish with the scallion greens.
tips: Cold, dry, day-old rice is non-negotiable — fresh rice is too wet and clumps instead of frying into separate grains.
Get the wok smoking hot before the eggs go in; a lukewarm wok is the most common reason home fried rice turns out steamed instead of stir-fried.
recipes.nutritionNote: A complete one-bowl meal with protein from shrimp, egg and char siu already built in, but char siu and soy sauce both bring sodium, so skip extra salt at the table and add a side of blanched vegetables if serving as a whole dinner.

fil.description: Kanin na day-old, sini-stir-fry hot and fast with hipon, char siu, itlog, carrot at gisantes hanggang maghiwalay ang bawat butil — ito ang sagot ng Yangzhou sa leftovers at ang fried rice na pinagkukumparahan ng lahat ng version.
ingredients: tubig, para sa pagluluto ng kanin
hipon, balatan, alisan ng ugat at hiwain into half lengthwise
scallion, white at green parts hiwalayin, tadtarin
steps: Lutuin ang kanin gamit ng kaunti lang na tubig kaysa usual para manatiling matigas ang butil; i-spread out at palamigin nang husto, ideally isang araw before — nagiging mushy ang fried rice kapag basa at bagong-luto ang kanin.
Pakuluan ang tubig. I-blanch ang carrot at peas for 30-40 seconds, tapos idagdag ang hipon at lutuin hanggang just pink, about 2 more minutes. I-drain at itabi.
I-beat ang itlog with pinch ng asin.
Painitin ang wok sa high heat for a minute, idagdag ang 1 tbsp oil hanggang rippling, tapos ibuhos ang itlog. Hayaang mag-set for 10-15 seconds, tapos idagdag ang malamig na kanin diretso sa ibabaw.
Durugin ang mga clumps ng kanin at i-stir-fry for 2.5-3 minutes sa high heat hanggang maghiwalay ang bawat butil at maririnig ang light crackle.
Ibaba ang heat, idagdag ang half ng asin at ang soy sauce, at i-toss para maging pantay ang coating.
Itabi ang kanin sa gilid ng wok, idagdag ang char siu sa gitna para mainitan, tapos ihalo kasama ang blanched vegetables, hipon at scallion whites.
Taasan ang heat to high, i-drizzle ang natitirang oil para sa shine, i-toss ang lahat nang sabay, at i-finish ng scallion greens.
tips: Non-negotiable ang malamig at tuyong day-old na kanin — masyadong basa ang bagong-luto na kanin at nagkukulumpon instead na maghiwalay ang mga butil sa pagpi-fry.
Siguraduhing umuusok na ang wok before ilagay ang itlog; ang pangkaraniwang dahilan kung bakit nagiging steamed instead of stir-fried ang fried rice sa bahay ay lukewarm na wok.
fil.nutritionNote: Complete one-bowl meal ito na may protein na mula sa hipon, itlog at char siu — pero maalat ang char siu at soy sauce, kaya skip na lang ang extra salt sa table at magdagdag ng blanched vegetables kung buong dinner ang ihahain.

recipes.title: Arroz Caldo
recipes.description: A thick, ginger-scented rice porridge with shredded chicken, topped with crispy garlic, egg and scallions — the standard Filipino sick-day and rainy-morning breakfast.

ingredients.note: or a whole chicken cut into pieces
mix half-and-half with regular rice for a looser porridge

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat; sauté the onion, ginger and garlic until softened and fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring, until lightly browned on the outside.
Pour in the fish sauce and cook 1-2 minutes to let the chicken absorb the flavour.
Stir in the rice and cook 1-2 minutes, toasting it lightly in the aromatics.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, and skim off any foam; add the bouillon cubes and stir to dissolve.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer 30-35 minutes, stirring every few minutes so the rice doesn't stick, until the porridge thickens and the chicken is cooked through.
Shred or pull the chicken into bite-sized pieces if you like, then season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls and top with hard-boiled egg, fried garlic and green onions; serve with calamansi and extra fish sauce on the side.
tips: Stir every few minutes once the rice goes in — glutinous rice scorches on the bottom easily.
Fry the garlic bits separately and low and slow; they go from golden to burnt in seconds.
Leftover porridge thickens a lot in the fridge — loosen with a splash of hot water or stock when reheating.
recipes.nutritionNote: A soft, easy-to-digest rice porridge that's fairly plain on its own; the egg and shredded chicken supply protein, so add a side of sautéed vegetables since the dish itself offers little fibre.

fil.description: Makapal, maluyang rice porridge na may shredded chicken, tinopping ng crispy garlic, itlog at scallions — ang standard Filipino sick-day at rainy-morning breakfast.
ingredients: hita at paa ng manok, bone-in
hard-boiled na itlog, hiwain in half
steps: Painitin ang oil sa heavy pot sa medium heat; igisa ang sibuyas, luya at bawang hanggang lumambot at mabango.
Idagdag ang manok at lutuin, haluin, hanggang lightly browned sa labas.
Ibuhos ang patis at lutuin for 1-2 minutes para maabsorb ng manok ang lasa.
Ihalo ang bigas at lutuin for 1-2 minutes, i-toast nang bahagya sa mga aromatics.
Ibuhos ang tubig, pakuluin, at alisin ang foam na lumulutang; idagdag ang bouillon cubes at haluin hanggang matunaw.
Hinaan ang apoy, takpan, at i-simmer for 30-35 minutes, haluin every few minutes para hindi dumikit ang bigas, hanggang lumapot ang lugaw at luto na ang manok.
I-shred o hilahin ang manok into bite-sized pieces kung gusto mo, tapos timplahan ng asin at paminta to taste.
Isalin sa bowl at topping ng hard-boiled egg, fried garlic at green onions; ihain with calamansi at extra patis sa tabi.
tips: Haluin every few minutes once nasa loob na ang bigas — mabilis mag-scorch ang malagkit sa ilalim.
I-fry ang garlic bits separately at low and slow; mabilis lang siyang mag-golden hanggang sunog.
Lumalapot nang husto ang natirang lugaw sa ref — lagyan ng konting mainit na tubig o stock kapag ni-reheat.
fil.nutritionNote: Malambot, madaling matunaw na rice porridge na medyo plain lang mag-isa; ang itlog at shredded chicken ang nagbibigay ng protein, kaya dagdagan ng sautéed vegetables dahil kaunti lang ang fibre ng dish mismo.

recipes.title: Beef Caldereta
recipes.description: Beef chunks braised low and slow in a tomato sauce with potatoes, carrots and bell peppers, enriched with liver spread until glossy and deep red — a special-occasion stew with Spanish roots.

ingredients.item: beef chuck or brisket, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
carrots, peeled and sliced into rounds

ingredients.note: or blended chicken liver as a substitute; adds body and colour
optional, for the classic briny bite

steps: Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a wide pot and pan-fry the potatoes and carrots until the edges lightly brown; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, heat the remaining oil and sear the beef in batches until browned on all sides; set aside with the vegetables.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the same pot until softened and fragrant.
Return the beef to the pot, add the tomato sauce, broth and bay leaves, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer 60-75 minutes, stirring occasionally and topping up liquid if it runs low, until the beef is fork-tender.
Stir in the liver spread until fully dissolved into the sauce, then season with salt and pepper.
Add the browned potatoes, carrots, bell peppers and olives; simmer uncovered 8-10 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Searing the beef and pan-frying the potatoes separately first, rather than dumping everything in together, is what gives caldereta its depth.
Liver spread is the traditional thickener — don't skip it for cheese, which makes a different (and sweeter) dish.
Like most braises, caldereta reheats and often tastes better the next day.
recipes.nutritionNote: A protein-rich, moderately fatty braise; the potatoes and carrots already supply starch and vitamin A, so keep the rice portion normal-sized rather than adding extra sides that pile on more carbohydrate.

fil.description: Beef chunks na ni-braise nang mabagal sa tomato sauce na may patatas, carrots at bell peppers, pinayaman ng liver spread hanggang shiny at deep red — isang special-occasion stew na may Spanish roots.
ingredients: beef chuck o brisket, hiniwa into 1.5-inch cubes
patatas, balatan at hiwain into cubes
carrots, balatan at hiwain into rounds
steps: Painitin ang 1 tablespoon ng mantika sa malapad na pot tapos i-pan-fry ang patatas at carrots hanggang medyo mag-brown ang gilid; alisin tapos itabi.
Sa parehong pot, painitin ang natitirang mantika tapos i-sear ang beef in batches hanggang mag-brown sa lahat ng sides; itabi kasama ng gulay.
Igisa ang sibuyas at bawang sa parehong pot hanggang lumambot at bumango.
Ibalik ang beef sa pot, idagdag ang tomato sauce, broth at bay leaves, tapos pakuluin.
Hinaan ang heat, takpan, tapos i-simmer for 60-75 minutes, hinahalo paminsan-minsan at dinadagdagan ng liquid kung kumokonti, hanggang fork-tender na ang beef.
Ihalo ang liver spread hanggang matunaw nang buo sa sauce, tapos timplahan ng asin at paminta.
Idagdag ang binrown na patatas, carrots, bell peppers at olives; i-simmer uncovered for 8-10 minutes hanggang tender ang gulay at lumapot ang sauce.
Ihain mainit na may steamed rice.
tips: Ang paghiwalay ng pag-sear ng beef at pag-pan-fry ng patatas, sa halip na sabay-sabay ilaga lahat, ang nagbibigay ng depth sa caldereta.
Ang liver spread ang traditional thickener — huwag palitan ng cheese, kasi iba (at mas matamis) ang lasa nito.
Tulad ng ibang braise, mas masarap ang caldereta pag-init kinabukasan.
fil.nutritionNote: Isang protein-rich, medyo mataba na braise; ang patatas at carrots ay may starch at vitamin A na, kaya i-keep normal-sized ang rice portion sa halip na magdagdag pa ng ibang sides na may extra carbs.

recipes.title: Bicol Express
recipes.description: Pork belly simmered in coconut milk with shrimp paste and green chilies until the sauce turns thick and red-orange — the fiery Bicolano dish named after the train that once carried its heat to Manila.

ingredients.note: reduce to 3-4 for a milder pot
optional, for real heat — omit entirely for a family pot

steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the pork and cook, stirring occasionally, 5-7 minutes until lightly browned.
Stir in the shrimp paste and cook 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook uncovered 15-18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pork is tender and the sauce reduces.
Stir in the coconut cream and the green finger chilies; simmer 5 minutes more.
Add the long beans and cook 3-4 minutes until just tender.
Stir in the Thai chilies if using, season with pepper, and simmer 2 minutes more.
Serve hot with plenty of steamed rice.
tips: Slice the chilies rather than leaving them whole if you want the dish properly spicy — whole chilies add only aroma.
The dish thickens as it cools, so loosen leftovers with a splash of coconut milk when reheating.
Balance the shrimp paste's saltiness by tasting before adding extra fish sauce or salt.
recipes.kidNote: Set aside a plain, mild portion of pork and coconut sauce for the kids before adding any sliced chilies — use only whole, uncut long green chilies in their pot for aroma, and keep the Thai chilies strictly for the adult pot.
recipes.nutritionNote: High in saturated fat from both pork belly and coconut milk, so serve smaller portions of sauce over rice, add a plain vegetable side, and avoid pairing it with another coconut-milk dish in the same week.

fil.description: Liempo na sini-simmer sa gata na may bagoong at green chilies hanggang lumapot at mag-red-orange ang sauce — ang maanghang na Bicolano dish na pinangalanan sa tren na dating nagdadala ng init nito papuntang Manila.
steps: Painitin ang mantika sa malapad na kawali over medium heat tapos igisa ang sibuyas at bawang hanggang lumambot.
Idagdag ang baboy tapos lutuin, hinahalo paminsan-minsan, for 5-7 minutes hanggang medyo mag-brown.
Ihalo ang bagoong tapos lutuin for 1-2 minutes hanggang bumango.
Ibuhos ang gata, pakuluin nang dahan-dahan, tapos lutuin uncovered for 15-18 minutes, hinahalo paminsan-minsan, hanggang lumambot ang baboy at lumapot ang sauce.
Ihalo ang kakang gata at ang siling haba; i-simmer for 5 minutes more.
Idagdag ang sitaw tapos lutuin for 3-4 minutes hanggang tender lang.
Ihalo ang siling labuyo kung gagamitin, timplahan ng paminta, tapos i-simmer for 2 minutes more.
Ihain mainit na may sobrang kanin.
tips: Hiwain ang mga sili sa halip na iwan buo kung gusto mo talagang maanghang — ang buong sili aroma lang ang idadagdag.
Lumalapot ang ulam habang lumalamig, kaya patubigan ng kaunting gata kapag nag-i-reheat ng leftovers.
I-balance ang alat ng bagoong sa pagtikim muna bago magdagdag pa ng patis o asin.
fil.kidNote: Maglaan ng plain at mild na portion ng baboy at gata sauce para sa mga bata bago maglagay ng hiniwang sili — buong siling haba lang na hindi hiniwa ang ilagay sa kanilang pot para sa aroma, at ang siling labuyo ay para lang sa adult pot.
fil.nutritionNote: Mataas sa saturated fat galing sa liempo at gata, kaya maglagay ng mas maliit na sauce sa kanin, magdagdag ng plain vegetable side, at iwasang isabay sa isa pang coconut-milk dish sa parehong linggo.

recipes.title: Bistek Tagalog
recipes.description: Thin-sliced beef marinated in calamansi and soy sauce, seared, then simmered with onions until the sauce turns savoury-tangy — a weeknight staple in Tagalog households.

ingredients.item: beef sirloin, thinly sliced against the grain

ingredients.note: or substitute lemon or lime juice

steps: Combine the beef with the calamansi juice, soy sauce, sliced onion, garlic and pepper; massage the marinade into the meat and let sit at least 30 minutes.
Lift the beef out of the marinade, squeezing off excess liquid; reserve the marinade, onions and garlic separately.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat and sear the beef in batches, 1-2 minutes per side, until lightly browned; remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the reserved marinated onions and garlic until softened.
Return the beef to the pan, pour in the reserved marinade and the water, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer uncovered 8-10 minutes until the beef is tender and the sauce has reduced slightly.
Season with salt to taste, then turn off the heat and scatter the raw onion rings over the top; cover for 1-2 minutes so they soften in the residual heat.
Serve hot over steamed rice, spooning the sauce over both.
tips: Slice the beef thinly against the grain — this is what keeps bistek tender without needing a long braise.
The 30-minute marinate is mostly unattended; use the time to prep the rest of dinner.
Don't skip the raw onion rings on top; their bite against the savoury-sour sauce is the dish's signature.
recipes.nutritionNote: Protein-forward and moderately salty from the soy marinade; serve with extra steamed vegetables or a side salad and go easy on additional soy sauce at the table.

fil.description: Manipis na hiwang beef na ni-marinate sa calamansi at toyo, sinear, tapos ni-simmer with onions hanggang maging savory-tangy ang sabaw — weeknight staple ng mga Tagalog household.
ingredients: beef sirloin, hiwain nang manipis against the grain
steps: Pagsamahin ang beef with calamansi juice, toyo, hiwang sibuyas, bawang at paminta; masahin ang marinade sa karne at itabi for at least 30 minutes.
Alisin ang beef sa marinade, pigain ang excess liquid; itabi ang marinade, sibuyas at bawang separately.
Painitin ang oil sa wide pan sa high heat at isear ang beef in batches, 1-2 minutes per side, hanggang lightly browned; alisin at itabi.
Sa parehong pan, igisa ang reserved na marinated onions at bawang hanggang lumambot.
Ibalik ang beef sa pan, ibuhos ang reserved marinade at tubig, at pakuluin.
Hinaan ang apoy at i-simmer uncovered for 8-10 minutes hanggang malambot ang beef at medyo mag-reduce ang sabaw.
Timplahan ng asin to taste, tapos patayin ang apoy at ikalat ang raw onion rings sa ibabaw; takpan for 1-2 minutes para lumambot ang mga ito sa init.
Ihain mainit over steamed rice, budburan ng sabaw ang parehong beef at rice.
tips: Hiwain ang beef nang manipis against the grain — ito ang lihim para maging tender ang bistek kahit hindi matagal ang pag-luto.
Ang 30-minute marinate ay mostly unattended lang; gamitin ang oras para i-prep ang ibang ulam.
Huwag laktawan ang raw onion rings sa ibabaw; ang crunch nito against sa savory-sour sauce ang signature ng dish.
fil.nutritionNote: Protein-forward at medyo maalat dahil sa toyo marinade; ihain with extra steamed vegetables o side salad at bawasan ang extra toyo sa hapag.

recipes.title: Chicken Adobo
recipes.description: Chicken braised in soy sauce, vinegar, garlic and bay leaf until the sauce turns glossy and dark — the everyday dinner every Filipino household makes differently.

ingredients.item: bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks, cut into serving pieces

ingredients.note: cane vinegar is milder; start with less if using distilled white vinegar

steps: Combine the chicken, soy sauce and crushed garlic in a bowl; massage well and marinate at least 1 hour, longer if possible.
Lift the chicken out of the marinade, keeping both the garlicky liquid and the pieces of garlic to use later.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and pan-fry the chicken 2 minutes per side until lightly browned; remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the same pot and sauté the reserved garlic until fragrant and starting to brown.
Return the chicken to the pot with the reserved marinade, peppercorns, bay leaves and water; bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 30 minutes until tender.
Pour in the vinegar and let it boil uncovered, without stirring, for 2 minutes so it loses its raw sharpness.
Stir and simmer uncovered another 15 minutes until the sauce reduces and turns glossy.
Stir in the sugar and salt to taste, then turn off the heat and serve hot with rice.
tips: Do not stir after adding the vinegar until it has boiled for at least 2 minutes, or the sauce tastes raw and sharp.
Marinating overnight (unattended, in the fridge) deepens the flavour more than a rushed 30 minutes.
Adobo tastes better the next day — make it ahead and reheat gently.
recipes.nutritionNote: Salty and rich from soy sauce and rendered chicken fat; balance with steamed vegetables or a fresh tomato-cucumber side and go light on extra rice or soy sauce at the table.

fil.description: Manok na ni-braise sa toyo, suka, bawang at bay leaf hanggang mag-dark and glossy ang sabaw — ang everyday dinner na bawat Pinoy household may sariling bersyon.
ingredients: bone-in na hita at paa ng manok, hiwain into serving pieces
steps: Pagsamahin ang manok, toyo at durog na bawang sa isang bowl; masahin nang mabuti at i-marinate for at least 1 hour, mas matagal kung kaya.
Alisin ang manok sa marinade, itabi ang toyo-garlic na liquid pati na rin ang mga bawang para gamitin mamaya.
Painitin ang 2 tbsp na oil sa heavy pot sa medium-high heat at iprito ang manok 2 minutes per side hanggang lightly browned; alisin at itabi.
Idagdag ang natitirang oil sa parehong pot at igisa ang natirang bawang hanggang mabango at nagsisimulang mag-brown.
Ibalik ang manok sa pot kasama ang reserved marinade, paminta, bay leaves at tubig; pakuluin, tapos takpan at i-simmer for 30 minutes hanggang lumambot.
Ibuhos ang suka at hayaang kumulo nang walang takip, huwag haluin, for 2 minutes para mawala ang matapang na amoy nito.
Haluin at i-simmer uncovered ng isa pang 15 minutes hanggang mag-reduce at maging glossy ang sabaw.
Ihalo ang sugar at asin to taste, tapos patayin ang apoy at ihain mainit with rice.
tips: Huwag haluin pagkatapos ilagay ang suka hangga't hindi pa kumukulo for at least 2 minutes, kung hindi manlalasa ng raw ang sabaw.
Ang overnight marinate (unattended, sa ref) mas nagpapalalim ng lasa kaysa sa mabilisang 30 minutes.
Mas masarap ang adobo kinabukasan — gawin in advance tapos i-reheat gently na lang.
fil.nutritionNote: Maalat at rich dahil sa toyo at rendered chicken fat; i-balance with steamed vegetables o fresh tomato-cucumber side, at bawasan ang extra rice o toyo sa hapag.

recipes.title: Chicken Inasal
recipes.description: Chicken legs marinated in vinegar, calamansi, lemongrass and ginger, basted with golden annatto oil while grilling — the smoky, tangy specialty of Bacolod, sold at every roadside inasalan.

ingredients.item: chicken leg quarters, scored ¼-inch deep
lemongrass, white part only, pounded and chopped

ingredients.note: steeped in the oil to colour it orange; or use 1 tsp annatto powder

steps: Combine the vinegar, calamansi juice, lemongrass, garlic, ginger, sugar and salt in a bowl.
Add the scored chicken, massage the marinade in well, cover and refrigerate 4-24 hours.
Warm the oil over low heat with the annatto seeds for 3-4 minutes until the oil turns deep orange, then strain out the seeds and stir in the melted butter to make the basting sauce.
Prepare a hot charcoal or gas grill and lightly oil the grates.
Lift the chicken from the marinade, letting excess drip off, and grill skin-side down 5-6 minutes until well marked.
Flip and continue grilling, basting regularly with the annatto oil, another 8-10 minutes until fully cooked and lightly charred.
Rest the chicken 3-4 minutes before serving.
Serve hot with garlic rice and a small dish of soy-calamansi dipping sauce.
tips: Scoring the chicken lets the marinade penetrate faster and helps it cook more evenly on the grill.
The overnight marinate is unattended time — do it the night before for a quick weeknight grill session.
No charcoal grill? A hot oven broiler or stovetop grill pan works, though you'll miss the smoke flavour.
recipes.nutritionNote: Grilled rather than fried, so it's leaner than most Filipino chicken dishes; pair with a vegetable side rather than extra oil-basted rice to keep the meal balanced.

fil.description: Chicken legs na ni-marinate sa vinegar, calamansi, lemongrass at luya, binabasted ng golden annatto oil habang nag-gi-grill — ang smoky at maasim na specialty ng Bacolod, binebenta sa bawat roadside inasalan.
ingredients: chicken leg quarters, hiniwa ¼-inch deep
lemongrass, white part lang, dinurog at tinadtad
steps: Ihalo ang vinegar, calamansi juice, lemongrass, bawang, luya, sugar at asin sa isang bowl.
Idagdag ang scored na manok, i-massage nang maigi ang marinade, takpan tapos i-refrigerate for 4-24 hours.
Painitin ang mantika over low heat na may annatto seeds for 3-4 minutes hanggang deep orange na ang mantika, tapos salain ang seeds at ihalo ang tinunaw na butter para gawing basting sauce.
Ihanda ang mainit na charcoal o gas grill tapos lightly i-oil ang grates.
Alisin ang manok sa marinade, patuluin ang excess, tapos i-grill skin-side down for 5-6 minutes hanggang well marked.
I-flip tapos ipagpatuloy ang pag-grill, binabasted regularly ng annatto oil, for 8-10 minutes more hanggang fully cooked at medyo charred.
Pahingahin ang manok for 3-4 minutes bago ihain.
Ihain mainit na may garlic rice at maliit na mangkok ng soy-calamansi dipping sauce.
tips: Ang pag-score sa manok ay nagpapabilis sa pagpasok ng marinade at nakakatulong para maluto nang pantay-pantay sa grill.
Ang overnight marinate ay unattended time lang — gawin na ito the night before para mabilis na weeknight grill session.
Walang charcoal grill? Pwede rin ang mainit na oven broiler o stovetop grill pan, pero mami-miss mo ang smoke flavor.
fil.nutritionNote: Grilled hindi fried, kaya mas leaner kaysa karamihan ng Filipino chicken dishes; isabay sa vegetable side sa halip na extra oil-basted rice para balanced ang meal.

recipes.title: Chicken Tinola
recipes.description: A clear, gingery chicken broth with green papaya and spinach — gentle enough to be the first soup Filipino kids are given when they're sick or just hungry.

ingredients.note: bone-in thigh and leg pieces work well

ingredients.item: green papaya, peeled, seeded and cut into wedges
ingredients.note: or substitute chayote (sayote) if green papaya is unavailable

ingredients.item: fresh spinach or malunggay (moringa) leaves, stems trimmed

steps: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté the onion, garlic and ginger until softened and fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, 5-7 minutes until the outside is lightly browned.
Pour in the fish sauce and cook 1-2 minutes to let the chicken absorb the flavour.
Add the water, bring to a boil, and skim off any foam; lower the heat, cover, and simmer 30-35 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked and tender.
Add the green papaya wedges and cook 3-5 minutes until just tender but still holding their shape.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Push the spinach or malunggay leaves into the broth and cook just until wilted, about 1 minute.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with rice, spooning extra broth over each bowl.
tips: Simmer the chicken low and slow rather than at a hard boil — this is what keeps the broth clean instead of cloudy.
Choose a firm, pale-green, underripe papaya; it holds its shape better than one that's starting to ripen.
recipes.kidNote: Shred the chicken off the bone for the 6-year-old's bowl to avoid small bones; the ginger flavour is mild enough that all three kids usually eat this without complaint.
recipes.nutritionNote: A light, mostly-broth dish that's naturally low in fat; pair with a modest scoop of rice and a side of fruit, since the soup itself is fairly light on calories and fibre beyond the papaya.

fil.description: Malinaw, maluyang chicken broth na may green papaya at spinach — ang unang soup na binibigay sa mga Pinoy kids kapag may sakit o gutom lang.
ingredients: green papaya, balatan, alisin ang buto at hiwain into wedges
spinach o malunggay leaves, putulan ang tangkay
steps: Painitin ang oil sa pot sa medium heat; igisa ang sibuyas, bawang at luya hanggang lumambot at mabango, about 2 minutes.
Idagdag ang manok at lutuin, haluin paminsan-minsan, for 5-7 minutes hanggang lightly browned sa labas.
Ibuhos ang patis at lutuin for 1-2 minutes para maabsorb ng manok ang lasa.
Idagdag ang tubig, pakuluin, at alisin ang foam na lumulutang; hinaan ang apoy, takpan, at i-simmer for 30-35 minutes hanggang luto na at malambot ang manok.
Idagdag ang green papaya wedges at lutuin for 3-5 minutes hanggang tender lang pero hindi nawawala ang hugis.
Timplahan ng asin at paminta to taste.
Ilubog ang spinach o malunggay leaves sa sabaw at lutuin hanggang malanta lang, about 1 minute.
Isalin sa bowl at ihain mainit with rice, dagdagan ng sabaw sa bawat bowl.
tips: I-simmer ang manok nang mahinay imbes na hard boil — ito ang dahilan kung bakit malinaw ang sabaw imbes na malabo.
Pumili ng matigas, pale-green na papaya na hindi pa hinog; mas hindi ito nawawalan ng hugis kompara sa nagsisimula nang mag-hinog.
fil.kidNote: Tanggalin ang buto sa manok ng 6-year-old para iwas sa maliit na buto; hindi masyadong strong ang luya kaya usually kinakain ito ng tatlong bata without complaint.
fil.nutritionNote: Light, mostly-broth na dish na naturally mababa sa taba; i-pair with modest scoop ng rice at fruit sa tabi, dahil medyo light lang sa calories at fibre ang soup mismo bukod sa papaya.

recipes.title: Eggplant Omelet
recipes.description: Whole eggplants charred until smoky, peeled and flattened, then dipped in beaten egg and pan-fried until golden and fluffy — the everyday breakfast omelet Filipino households make with whatever eggplant is on hand.
steps: Grill the whole eggplants directly over an open flame or under a broiler, turning often, 8-10 minutes until the skin is fully charred and blackened and the flesh feels soft.
Let the eggplants cool slightly, then peel off the charred skin under running water, keeping the stem intact.
Flatten each eggplant gently with a fork, leaving the stem attached as a handle.
Season the beaten eggs with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Holding each eggplant by the stem, dip it into the beaten egg, coating both sides well, then lay it in the hot pan.
Spoon a little extra egg over the top of each eggplant, and fry 2-3 minutes per side until golden and set.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve warm with rice, sliced tomato and a dip of soy sauce and calamansi.
tips: Charring the eggplant directly over a flame, not just steaming it, is what gives tortang talong its smoky background flavour.
Keep the stem on while flattening and dipping — it's your handle and helps the omelet hold together.
Work in one pan at a time; adding too much egg-coated eggplant at once cools the oil and makes the coating stick.
recipes.nutritionNote: A quick, protein-and-fibre-friendly vegetable dish; pair with a lean grilled or fried side and a fruit serving, since the eggplant and egg alone are light on the plate.

fil.description: Buong talong na sini-grill hanggang smoky, binalatan at pinipi, tapos isinawsaw sa beaten egg at pinirito hanggang golden at fluffy — ang everyday breakfast omelet na niluluto ng mga Filipino household kahit anong talong ang meron.
steps: I-grill ang buong talong directly sa open flame o sa ilalim ng broiler, palaging binabaligtad, for 8-10 minutes hanggang fully charred at itim ang balat at malambot na ang laman.
Hayaang lumamig nang kaunti ang talong, tapos balatan ang charred skin sa ilalim ng tumatakbong tubig, iniiwan ang tangkay.
Pipiin nang dahan-dahan ang bawat talong gamit ang tinidor, iniiwan ang tangkay para maging hawakan.
Timplahan ang beaten eggs ng asin at paminta.
Painitin ang mantika sa malapad na kawali over medium heat.
Hawakan ang bawat talong sa tangkay, isawsaw sa beaten egg, balutin nang maigi ang dalawang sides, tapos ilagay sa mainit na kawali.
Buhusan ng kaunting extra egg ang ibabaw ng bawat talong, tapos i-fry for 2-3 minutes per side hanggang golden at set.
I-drain nang saglit sa paper towels tapos ihain mainit na may kanin, hiniwang kamatis at sawsawan na toyo at calamansi.
tips: Ang pag-char ng talong directly sa flame, hindi lang pag-steam, ang nagbibigay ng smoky background flavor sa tortang talong.
Panatilihin ang tangkay habang pinipi at isinasawsaw — ito ang hawakan mo at tumutulong para hindi mahiwalay ang omelet.
Isang kawali lang muna sa isang oras; kapag sobra ang egg-coated eggplant na inilagay, lumalamig ang mantika tapos dumidikit ang coating.
fil.nutritionNote: Isang mabilis, protein-and-fibre-friendly na vegetable dish; isabay sa lean grilled o fried side at prutas, dahil light lang ang talong at itlog mag-isa sa plato.

recipes.title: Fish in Coconut Milk
recipes.description: Pan-fried fish simmered in ginger-and-garlic coconut milk with eggplant, bok choy and a whole chili — a rich, warming way to stretch a market-fresh fish into dinner.

ingredients.item: whole galunggong (round scad) or tilapia fillets
ingredients.note: any firm white fish works; ask the market to gut and scale it

ingredients.item: seasoning granules or salt, for the fish
long green chili pepper (siling haba), left whole
ingredients.note: adds aroma more than heat; omit for a milder pot

steps: Season the fish with salt or seasoning granules and let sit 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a pan and lightly fry the eggplant slices, about 2 minutes per side; set aside.
In the same pan, fry the seasoned fish in the remaining oil until golden and crisp on both sides; set aside.
Using about 3 tablespoons of the frying oil in a pot, sauté the ginger, garlic and onion until the onion softens and turns translucent.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle boil, stirring occasionally so it doesn't split.
Add the vinegar and simmer uncovered 3 minutes without stirring.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, then add the chili pepper and the fried fish; cover and simmer 3 minutes to let the fish absorb the sauce.
Add the bok choy, fried eggplant and malunggay leaves; cook 2 minutes more until the greens wilt and the sauce thickens slightly.
Transfer to a serving dish and serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Pan-frying the fish and eggplant first keeps them from falling apart once they hit the simmering coconut milk.
Let the coconut milk come to a boil before adding vinegar — this helps it stay smooth instead of curdling.
Leave the chili whole rather than slicing it if you want the flavour without real heat.
recipes.kidNote: Lift the whole chili pepper out before ladling the kids' portions, and check the fish carefully for small bones before serving it to the 6-year-old.
recipes.nutritionNote: Coconut milk makes this rich in saturated fat, so serve modest portions of the sauce over rice and pair with a plain vegetable side rather than doubling up on coconut-milk dishes in the same week.

fil.description: Pinirito na isda na ni-simmer sa luya-at-bawang coconut milk with talong, pechay at buong sili — rich at warming na paraan para ma-stretch ang market-fresh na isda into dinner.
ingredients: seasoning granules o asin, para sa isda
baby bok choy, hiwain in half
steps: Timplahan ang isda ng asin o seasoning granules at itabi for 10 minutes.
Painitin ang 2 tbsp ng oil sa pan at iprito nang bahagya ang talong, about 2 minutes per side; itabi.
Sa parehong pan, iprito ang tinimplang isda sa natitirang oil hanggang golden at crisp sa dalawang gilid; itabi.
Gamit ang about 3 tbsp ng frying oil sa pot, igisa ang luya, bawang at sibuyas hanggang lumambot at maging translucent ang sibuyas.
Ibuhos ang gata at pakuluin nang bahagya, haluin paminsan-minsan para hindi mag-split.
Idagdag ang suka at i-simmer uncovered for 3 minutes, huwag haluin.
Timplahan ng patis at paminta, tapos idagdag ang sili at ang pinirito na isda; takpan at i-simmer for 3 minutes para maabsorb ng isda ang sabaw.
Idagdag ang pechay, pinirito na talong at malunggay leaves; lutuin ng 2 minutes more hanggang malanta ang mga gulay at slight na lumapot ang sabaw.
Isalin sa serving dish at ihain mainit with steamed rice.
tips: Ang pag-fry muna sa isda at talong ang nagpapanatili sa hugis nila kapag isinabak na sa kumukulong gata.
Hayaang pumakulo muna ang gata bago idagdag ang suka — nakakatulong ito para manatiling smooth imbes na mag-curdle.
Iwan na buo ang sili imbes na hiwain kung gusto mo ng lasa without real heat.
fil.kidNote: Alisin ang buong sili bago i-ladle ang portion ng mga bata, at siguraduhing walang maliit na buto ang isda bago ihain sa 6-year-old.
fil.nutritionNote: Rich sa saturated fat dahil sa gata, kaya ihain ng modest portions ng sabaw over rice at i-pair with plain vegetable side imbes na dobolehin ang gata dishes sa parehong linggo.

recipes.title: Grilled Pork Belly
recipes.description: Pork belly slices marinated in calamansi, soy sauce and garlic, then grilled over charcoal and basted until charred at the edges — classic Filipino weekend backyard fare.

ingredients.item: pork belly, sliced into ½-inch thick slabs

steps: Combine the calamansi juice, fish sauce, garlic, chilies, brown sugar, salt and pepper in a bowl, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pork belly slices and massage the marinade into the meat; cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, or overnight for best flavour.
Meanwhile, mix all the dipping sauce ingredients together in a small bowl and set aside.
Drain the pork, reserving about 1 cup of the marinade; boil the reserved marinade 3-5 minutes to reduce, then stir in the oyster sauce and oil to make the basting sauce.
Prepare a hot charcoal or gas grill and lightly oil the grates; arrange the pork belly and grill 2-3 minutes per side to sear.
Continue grilling, basting regularly with the sauce once the pork loses its pink colour, 4-5 minutes per side more, until fully cooked and lightly charred.
Rest the pork for a few minutes off the heat, then slice into serving pieces.
Serve hot with the spiced vinegar dip and steamed rice.
tips: Marinate overnight if you can — it's unattended time and makes a real difference in flavour.
Keep a cooler part of the grill to move pieces to if the sugar in the marinade starts to burn before the pork is cooked through.
No charcoal grill? A ridged stovetop grill pan or the oven broiler both work — just watch the sugar for scorching.
recipes.kidNote: Set aside a few plain slices of pork belly before adding the chilies to the marinade so the kids get the same smoky-sweet flavour without any heat; keep the spiced vinegar dip strictly for the adults' table.
recipes.nutritionNote: Pork belly is high in fat, so balance the plate with a big side of grilled or steamed vegetables and a smaller rice portion rather than seconds of the meat.

fil.description: Liempo na ni-marinate sa calamansi, toyo at bawang, tapos inihaw sa uling at binastihan hanggang maging charred ang gilid — classic Filipino weekend backyard food.
ingredients: liempo, hiwain into ½-inch thick slabs
steps: Pagsamahin ang calamansi juice, patis, bawang, sili, brown sugar, asin at paminta sa bowl, haluin hanggang matunaw ang sugar.
Idagdag ang liempo at masahin ang marinade sa karne; takpan at i-refrigerate for at least 4 hours, o overnight para mas masarap.
Samantala, ihalo ang lahat ng dipping sauce ingredients sa maliit na bowl at itabi.
I-drain ang liempo, itabi ang about 1 cup ng marinade; pakuluin ang reserved marinade for 3-5 minutes para mag-reduce, tapos ihalo ang oyster sauce at oil para maging basting sauce.
Ihanda ang mainit na charcoal o gas grill at pahiran nang bahagya ng oil ang grates; ilagay ang liempo at ihaw for 2-3 minutes per side para sumear.
Ipagpatuloy ang paghaw, basted regularly with sauce once mawala na ang pink color ng liempo, 4-5 minutes per side more, hanggang luto na at slight na charred.
Ipahinga ang liempo ng ilang minuto off the heat, tapos hiwain into serving pieces.
Ihain mainit with spiced vinegar dip at steamed rice.
tips: I-marinate overnight kung kaya — unattended time lang naman ito at malaking difference sa lasa.
Magtabi ng cooler part sa grill para malipatan ang mga piraso kung nagsisimula nang masunog ang sugar sa marinade bago pa maluto ang liempo.
Walang charcoal grill? Okay lang ang ridged stovetop grill pan o oven broiler — bantayan lang ang sugar para hindi masunog.
fil.kidNote: Magtabi ng ilang plain na piraso ng liempo bago idagdag ang sili sa marinade para makakuha ang mga bata ng parehong smoky-sweet flavor without heat; itago ang spiced vinegar dip strictly para sa mga adults na lang.
fil.nutritionNote: Mataas sa taba ang liempo, kaya i-balance ang plato with malaking side ng grilled o steamed vegetables at mas maliit na rice portion imbes na dagdag pa sa karne.

recipes.title: Kare-Kare
recipes.description: Oxtail simmered for hours until fall-apart tender, then folded into a thick roasted-peanut sauce with eggplant and long beans — a festive stew served with a side of shrimp paste for kick.

ingredients.note: or 3 tbsp regular rice flour toasted dry in a pan until light gold
or substitute a second eggplant if unavailable

ingredients.item: Chinese eggplant, sliced into thick rounds

steps: Rinse the oxtail and place in a large pot with the water; bring to a boil over medium heat, skimming off the scum that rises.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer 2.5-3 hours until the oxtail is easily pierced with a fork, topping up water as needed; strain and reserve the broth, keeping the meat separate.
Blanch the eggplant, long beans and banana blossom in salted boiling water for 1-2 minutes each until just tender-crisp; set aside.
Heat the oil in a large pot and sauté the onion and garlic until softened; add the oxtail and cook, stirring, until lightly browned.
Pour in the fish sauce, then add about 6 cups of the reserved broth and bring to a boil.
Whisk the toasted rice flour with a little water into a smooth slurry, then stir it into the pot to thicken the broth slightly.
Stir in the peanut butter until fully dissolved and the sauce turns thick and creamy; season with salt and pepper.
Add the blanched vegetables and bok choy, folding gently until coated and heated through, then serve hot with rice and sautéed bagoong on the side.
tips: Toasting the rice flour dry in a pan first adds a nutty background note that plain flour doesn't.
The peanut sauce should coat a spoon thickly but still pour — thin it with a splash of reserved broth if it seizes up.
Oxtail is easiest to portion after it's chilled slightly; ask the butcher to pre-cut it if your knife struggles.
recipes.nutritionNote: Rich in fat from both the oxtail and peanut sauce, so serve modest portions of sauce over a normal rice serving and lean on the eggplant, long beans and bok choy for volume and fibre.

fil.description: Buntot ng baka na sini-simmer for hours hanggang malambot na malambot, tapos ihahalo sa isang makapal na roasted-peanut sauce na may talong at sitaw — isang festive na stew na sinasabayan ng bagoong para sa extra kick.
ingredients: buntot ng baka, hiniwa into 2-inch sections
Chinese eggplant, hiniwa into thick rounds
steps: Banlawan ang buntot ng baka tapos ilagay sa malaking pot na may tubig; pakuluin over medium heat, tinatanggal ang bula na lumulutang.
Hinaan ang heat, takpan, tapos i-simmer for 2.5-3 hours hanggang madaling matusok ng tinidor ang buntot, dinadagdagan ng tubig kung kailangan; salain tapos itabi ang sabaw, hiwalay sa karne.
I-blanch ang talong, sitaw at puso ng saging sa maalat na kumukulong tubig for 1-2 minutes each hanggang tender-crisp lang; itabi.
Painitin ang mantika sa malaking pot tapos igisa ang sibuyas at bawang hanggang lumambot; idagdag ang buntot ng baka tapos lutuin, hinahalo, hanggang medyo mag-brown.
Ibuhos ang patis, tapos idagdag ang mga 6 cups ng reserved broth tapos pakuluin.
I-whisk ang toasted rice flour na may kaunting tubig hanggang maging smooth na slurry, tapos ihalo sa pot para lumapot nang kaunti ang sabaw.
Ihalo ang peanut butter hanggang matunaw nang buo at lumapot at lumagkit ang sauce; timplahan ng asin at paminta.
Idagdag ang mga blanched na gulay at pechay, haluin nang dahan-dahan hanggang mabalutan at mainit na, tapos ihain mainit na may kanin at ginisang bagoong sa tabi.
tips: Ang pag-toast ng rice flour dry sa kawali muna ay nagdadagdag ng nutty na lasa na wala sa plain flour.
Dapat makapal ang peanut sauce pero pwede pa ring ibuhos — patubigan ng kaunting reserved broth kung lumapot masyado.
Mas madaling i-portion ang buntot ng baka kapag medyo pinalamig na; pahiwain na lang sa butcher kung ayaw makayanan ng kutsilyo mo.
fil.nutritionNote: Mataas sa taba galing sa buntot ng baka at peanut sauce, kaya maglagay ng katamtamang sauce sa normal na serving ng kanin tapos umasa sa talong, sitaw at pechay para sa volume at fibre.

recipes.title: Laing
recipes.description: Dried taro leaves simmered low and slow in coconut milk with pork, shrimp paste and chili until the leaves turn silky and deep green — a Bicolano classic that rewards patience and a heavy hand off the spoon.

ingredients.note: sold pre-dried in Filipino grocers; do not substitute fresh raw taro leaves, which are toxic uncooked

steps: Combine the coconut milk, pork, onion, garlic, ginger and shrimp paste in a wide pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat.
Simmer uncovered 8-10 minutes until the pork is nearly cooked through.
Lay the dried taro leaves on top of the liquid in an even layer without stirring.
Let the pot simmer undisturbed 20-25 minutes, occasionally pressing the leaves down gently with a spoon so they submerge, until they soften, darken and absorb most of the liquid.
Once the leaves have sunk and softened, gently fold them into the sauce without vigorous stirring, which can turn the dish bitter.
Stir in the coconut cream and chilies, and simmer 5 minutes more until the sauce thickens and clings to the leaves.
Season with pepper to taste, then remove from the heat.
Serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Resist stirring while the leaves cook in the first 20 minutes — disturbing them too early is the most common cause of a bitter, itchy-tasting laing.
Fully dried, packaged taro leaves are both safer and far less likely to cause the throat-itch some fresh leaves can if undercooked.
Leftover laing tastes even better the next day once the coconut oil separates slightly and the flavour deepens.
recipes.kidNote: Taro leaves have a naturally earthy, slightly bitter edge that many kids resist — spoon a portion of sauce and leaves without any chili for the kids, mix it well into their rice, and offer it as a side rather than the main event the first few times.
recipes.nutritionNote: Taro leaves bring iron, calcium and fibre despite the rich coconut sauce; serve smaller portions given the saturated fat content and pair with a plain protein like grilled fish rather than another coconut-based dish.

fil.description: Dried taro leaves na sini-simmer nang mabagal sa gata na may baboy, bagoong at sili hanggang maging silky at deep green ang mga dahon — isang Bicolano classic na kailangan ng pasensya at hindi paghahalo agad.
steps: Ihalo ang gata, baboy, sibuyas, bawang, luya at bagoong sa malapad na pot tapos pakuluin nang dahan-dahan over medium-low heat.
I-simmer uncovered for 8-10 minutes hanggang halos maluto na ang baboy.
Ilagay ang dried taro leaves sa ibabaw ng liquid nang pantay-pantay nang hindi hinahalo.

Hayaang mag-simmer nang hindi ginagalaw for 20-25 minutes, paminsan-minsang idiin nang dahan-dahan ng kutsara ang mga dahon para lumubog, hanggang lumambot, dumilim at masipsip nila ang karamihan sa liquid.
Kapag lumubog at lumambot na ang mga dahon, dahan-dahang ihalo sa sauce nang hindi masyadong hinahalo, dahil pwede itong magpapait sa lasa.
Ihalo ang kakang gata at mga sili, tapos i-simmer for 5 minutes more hanggang lumapot ang sauce at dumikit sa mga dahon.
Timplahan ng paminta, tapos alisin sa heat.
Ihain mainit na may kanin.
tips: Iwasang haluin habang naglulut ang mga dahon sa unang 20 minutes — ang pag-abala dito nang maaga ang pinakakaraniwang dahilan ng mapait, makati na laing.
Ang fully dried, packaged na taro leaves ay mas safe at mas kaunti ang chance na magmakati ang lalamunan kumpara sa fresh leaves na hindi masyadong naluto.
Mas masarap ang leftover laing kinabukasan kapag medyo nag-separate na ang coconut oil at lumalim ang lasa.
fil.kidNote: Ang taro leaves ay may natural na earthy at medyo mapait na lasa na hindi lahat ng bata gusto — maglaan ng portion ng sauce at dahon na walang sili para sa mga bata, ihalo nang maigi sa kanin, tapos ihain bilang side muna sa halip na main dish sa unang ilang beses.
fil.nutritionNote: Ang taro leaves ay may iron, calcium at fibre kahit rich ang gata sauce; maglagay ng mas maliit na portion dahil sa saturated fat, at isabay sa plain protein tulad ng grilled fish sa halip na isa pang coconut-based dish.

recipes.title: Leche Flan
recipes.description: A silky steamed egg custard capped with soft caramel, unmolded glossy-side up — the sweet finale at every Filipino fiesta, birthday and Christmas table.
steps: Divide the sugar among 2-3 llanera moulds (or one large heatproof pan); set over low heat and tilt continuously until it melts into a light golden caramel, then remove from heat and swirl to coat the bottom evenly.
Set the caramel-lined moulds aside to cool and harden while you make the custard.
Whisk the egg yolks gently in a bowl, being careful not to incorporate too much air, since bubbles leave holes in the finished flan.
Stir in the condensed milk, evaporated milk, vanilla and salt, mixing in a slow circular motion until just combined.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into the prepared moulds to remove any stray bits of egg white or membrane.

Cover each mould tightly with foil and steam over gently simmering water for 30-40 minutes, or bake in a water bath at 190°C (375°F) for 50-60 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 2 hours, or overnight, until fully set.
Run a thin knife around the edge and invert onto a plate so the caramel pools on top; slice and serve chilled.
tips: Strain the custard no matter how careful you were whisking — it's the difference between silky and eggy-textured flan.
Steaming over a gentle simmer, not a hard boil, prevents tiny air bubbles from pitting the surface.
Chilling overnight (unattended) firms the custard enough to unmould cleanly; don't rush this step.
recipes.nutritionNote: High in sugar and egg-yolk cholesterol, so treat this as an occasional dessert in modest slices rather than a daily one, and keep the rest of that meal lighter and vegetable-forward.

fil.description: Malutong na steamed egg custard na tinakpan ng soft caramel, binaligtad glossy-side up — ang sweet finale sa bawat Filipino fiesta, birthday at Pasko.
ingredients: egg yolks, mula sa large eggs
steps: Hatiin ang sugar sa 2-3 llanera moulds (o isang malaking heatproof pan); ilagay sa low heat at i-tilt nang tuloy-tuloy hanggang matunaw into light golden caramel, tapos alisin sa apoy at i-swirl para mabalutan nang pantay ang ilalim.
Itabi ang caramel-lined moulds hanggang lumamig at tumigas habang ginagawa ang custard.
I-whisk nang bahagya ang egg yolks sa bowl, mag-ingat na huwag masyadong pumasok ang hangin, dahil nagbibigay ng holes sa finished flan ang bubbles.
Ihalo ang condensed milk, evaporated milk, vanilla at asin, i-mix sa slow circular motion hanggang just combined lang.
I-strain ang mixture through fine sieve papunta sa prepared moulds para alisin ang anumang stray na piraso ng egg white o membrane.

Takpan nang mahigpit ang bawat mould ng foil at i-steam over gently simmering water for 30-40 minutes, o i-bake sa water bath sa 190°C (375°F) for 50-60 minutes, hanggang lumabas na malinis ang toothpick na isinuksok sa gitna.
Palamigin sa room temperature, tapos i-refrigerate for at least 2 hours, o overnight, hanggang fully set na.
Lagyan ng thin knife ang gilid at baligtarin sa plato para mapunta sa ibabaw ang caramel; hiwain at ihain chilled.
tips: I-strain ang custard kahit gaano pa kaingat ang pag-whisk mo — ito ang difference between silky at eggy-textured flan.
Ang pag-steam over gentle simmer, hindi hard boil, ay pumipigil sa tiny air bubbles na sumira sa surface.
Ang overnight chilling (unattended) ang nagpapatigas nang tama sa custard para lumabas nang maayos sa mould; huwag magmadali sa step na ito.
fil.nutritionNote: Mataas sa sugar at egg-yolk cholesterol, kaya treat this as occasional dessert sa modest slices imbes na araw-araw, at panatilihing lighter at vegetable-forward ang ibang bahagi ng meal na iyon.

recipes.title: Lumpiang Shanghai
recipes.description: Hand-rolled pork and vegetable spring rolls fried until crackling-crisp — the fixture of every Filipino birthday table and a favourite baon (packed lunch) treat.

ingredients.note: or ground chicken for a lighter version

ingredients.item: water chestnuts, drained and finely chopped
ingredients.note: 8 oz can; adds crunch, can omit if unavailable
thaw fully if frozen and keep covered with a damp cloth while working

steps: Combine the ground pork, green onions, water chestnuts, carrot, garlic, soy sauce, salt and pepper in a bowl and mix until evenly distributed.
Lay one spring roll wrapper on a flat surface with a corner pointing toward you, like a diamond.
Spoon about 1 heaping tablespoon of filling near the bottom corner and shape it into a thin log.
Fold the bottom corner over the filling, tuck and roll once, then fold in the side corners and continue rolling into a tight cylinder; seal the top corner with a dab of water.
Repeat with the remaining filling and wrappers, then cut each roll crosswise into 2-3 shorter pieces if you like.
Heat about 2 inches of oil in a deep pan to 165°C (330°F); fry the lumpia in batches, turning occasionally, 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crisp.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack.
Serve hot with sweet chilli sauce or banana ketchup for dipping.
tips: Roll tightly but don't overfill — an over-stuffed lumpia bursts open in the oil.
Uncooked rolls freeze well on a tray, then bag once solid; fry straight from frozen, adding a minute or two to the cook time.
Keep the oil at a steady medium heat; too hot browns the wrapper before the filling cooks through.
recipes.nutritionNote: Deep-fried and rich, so treat it as a portion-controlled side or party food rather than a main; pair with a vinegar-based dip instead of sweet sauce and add a vegetable soup or salad to the meal.

fil.description: Hand-rolled na baboy at gulay spring rolls na pinirito hanggang crackling-crisp — ang laging nasa Filipino birthday table at paboritong baon.
ingredients: water chestnuts, i-drain at tadtarin nang pino
steps: Pagsamahin ang giniling na baboy, green onions, water chestnuts, carrot, bawang, toyo, asin at paminta sa bowl at haluin hanggang pantay-pantay.
Ilatag ang isang lumpia wrapper sa flat na surface na nakaturo ang sulok sayo, parang diamond.
Maglagay ng about 1 heaping tbsp na filling malapit sa ibabang sulok at hubugin into thin log.
I-fold ang ibabang sulok papunta sa filling, tuck at i-roll once, tapos i-fold ang mga side corners at ipagpatuloy ang pag-roll into tight cylinder; i-seal ang top corner gamit ang kaunting tubig.
Ulitin sa natitirang filling at wrappers, tapos hiwain ang bawat roll crosswise into 2-3 shorter pieces kung gusto mo.
Painitin ang about 2 inches ng oil sa deep pan sa 165°C (330°F); iprito ang lumpia in batches, i-turn paminsan-minsan, for 3-4 minutes hanggang golden brown at crisp.
Hanguin gamit ang slotted spoon at i-drain sa wire rack.
Ihain mainit with sweet chili sauce o banana ketchup for dipping.
tips: I-roll nang mahigpit pero huwag over-fill — sumasabog ang over-stuffed na lumpia sa oil.
Nag-fi-freeze nang maayos ang uncooked rolls sa tray, tapos i-bag once solid na; iprito straight from frozen, dagdagan ng isa o dalawang minuto ang cook time.
Panatilihin ang oil sa steady medium heat; kapag masyadong mainit mag-bro-brown ang wrapper bago pa maluto ang filling.
fil.nutritionNote: Deep-fried at rich, so treat as portion-controlled side o party food imbes na main dish; i-pair with vinegar-based dip imbes na sweet sauce at dagdagan ng vegetable soup o salad ang meal.

recipes.title: Mung Bean Soup
recipes.description: Mung beans simmered until creamy, sautéed with tomato and garlic, and finished with pork cracklings and spinach — the humble Friday dinner Filipino families grew up on.

ingredients.item: dried mung beans (munggo), sorted and rinsed

ingredients.note: or crispy fried pork belly bits; omit and add a little extra oil for a vegetarian version

ingredients.item: fresh spinach or malunggay leaves, stems trimmed

steps: Sort through the mung beans, discarding any discoloured beans or debris, then rinse until the water runs clear.
Combine the beans and water in a pot; bring to a boil over medium heat, skimming off the foam that rises.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer 45-50 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are soft and starting to burst, topping up water if it drops much below 4 cups.
In a separate pan, heat the oil and sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant and softened.
Add the tomato and mash it into the mixture with a spoon until it breaks down into a light sauce.
Stir in the fish sauce and cook 1-2 minutes, then pour in the cooked mung beans with their liquid; bring back to a boil.
Add the chicharon and simmer a few minutes until it softens slightly in the broth; season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in the spinach, turn off the heat, and cover for 1-2 minutes until just wilted, then serve hot with rice.
tips: No need to soak the mung beans first — they cook through in under an hour from dry.
Add the chicharon just before serving if you want it to stay a bit crunchy rather than fully softened.
Mash a few extra spoonfuls of the cooked beans against the pot for a creamier, thicker soup.
recipes.nutritionNote: A genuinely balanced one-pot meal — mung beans bring plant protein, iron and fibre — so this is a good night to serve a smaller rice portion and let the beans and greens carry the plate.

fil.description: Munggo na ni-simmer hanggang creamy, ginisa with kamatis at bawang, at tinopping ng chicharon at spinach — ang simpleng Friday dinner na kinalakihan ng maraming Pinoy family.
ingredients: spinach o malunggay leaves, putulan ang tangkay
steps: I-sort ang munggo, alisin ang mga discolored na buto o dumi, tapos hugasan hanggang malinaw na ang tubig.
Pagsamahin ang munggo at tubig sa pot; pakuluin sa medium heat, alisin ang foam na lumulutang.
Hinaan ang apoy, takpan, at i-simmer for 45-50 minutes, haluin paminsan-minsan, hanggang malambot at nagsisimulang pumutok ang munggo, dagdagan ng tubig kung bababa nang husto sa 4 cups.
Sa hiwalay na pan, painitin ang oil at igisa ang sibuyas at bawang hanggang mabango at lumambot.
Idagdag ang kamatis at dikdikin gamit ang kutsara hanggang maging light na sauce.
Ihalo ang patis at lutuin for 1-2 minutes, tapos ibuhos ang lutong munggo kasama ang sabaw nito; pakuluin ulit.
Idagdag ang chicharon at i-simmer ng ilang minuto hanggang bahagyang lumambot sa sabaw; timplahan ng asin at paminta to taste.
Ihalo ang spinach, patayin ang apoy, at takpan for 1-2 minutes hanggang malanta lang, tapos ihain mainit with rice.
tips: Hindi na kailangang ibabad ang munggo — naluluto naman ito nang mabilis sa loob ng isang oras mula pagka-dry.
Idagdag ang chicharon bago ihain kung gusto mo itong crunchy pa rin imbes na fully softened na.
Dikdikin ang ilang extra sandok ng lutong munggo laban sa pot para maging mas creamy at makapal ang sabaw.
fil.nutritionNote: Genuinely balanced na one-pot meal — nagbibigay ang munggo ng plant protein, iron at fibre — kaya okay ang mas maliit na rice portion ngayong gabi at hayaan ang munggo at gulay ang mag-carry ng plato.

recipes.title: Pancit Bihon
recipes.description: Rice noodles stir-fried with pork, shrimp and vegetables in a light soy broth until every strand is coated — the noodle dish served at birthdays for long life and luck.

ingredients.item: pork tenderloin or shoulder, thinly sliced

steps: Bring the chicken stock and soy sauce to a boil; add the rice noodles and soak off the heat for 1-2 minutes until softened, then drain, reserving the liquid.
Heat 1 teaspoon of the oil in a wok over medium-high heat; stir-fry the shrimp 1-2 minutes until pink, then remove and set aside.
Add the pork to the same wok and cook until lightly browned; remove and set aside with the shrimp.
Heat the remaining oil and sauté the onion and garlic until softened and fragrant.
Add the carrot and celery; stir-fry 30-40 seconds, then add the cabbage and cook until just tender-crisp.
Return the pork and shrimp to the wok, then add the softened noodles along with the reserved stock in splashes, tossing gently between additions.
Continue tossing until the noodles have absorbed the liquid and everything is evenly combined; season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer to a platter, scatter with green onions, and serve with calamansi halves for squeezing over.
tips: Add the stock to the noodles gradually, not all at once, so they finish tender rather than soggy or clumped.
Cut every vegetable to roughly the same thin size so the stir-fry cooks evenly in just a few minutes.
recipes.nutritionNote: Carb-heavy from the noodles with modest protein from pork and shrimp; load in extra cabbage and carrots and serve fruit on the side rather than additional rice.

fil.description: Bihon na ginisa with baboy, hipon at gulay sa light na sabaw ng toyo hanggang mabalutan ang bawat strand — ang pancit na hain sa birthday para sa long life and luck.
ingredients: hipon, balatan at alisin ang ugat
pork tenderloin o kasim, hiwain nang manipis
steps: Pakuluin ang chicken stock at toyo; idagdag ang bihon at ibabad off the heat for 1-2 minutes hanggang lumambot, tapos i-drain, itabi ang liquid.
Painitin ang 1 tsp ng oil sa wok sa medium-high heat; i-stir-fry ang hipon for 1-2 minutes hanggang pumink, tapos alisin at itabi.
Idagdag ang baboy sa parehong wok at lutuin hanggang lightly browned; alisin at itabi kasama ng hipon.
Painitin ang natitirang oil at igisa ang sibuyas at bawang hanggang lumambot at mabango.
Idagdag ang carrot at kintsay; i-stir-fry for 30-40 seconds, tapos idagdag ang repolyo at lutuin hanggang tender-crisp lang.
Ibalik ang baboy at hipon sa wok, tapos idagdag ang malambot na bihon kasama ang reserved stock in splashes, i-toss gently sa bawat dagdag.
Ipagpatuloy ang pag-toss hanggang maabsorb ng bihon ang liquid at pantay-pantay ang timpla; timplahan ng asin at paminta to taste.
Isalin sa platter, budburan ng green onions, at ihain with calamansi halves para pigain sa ibabaw.
tips: Idagdag ang stock sa bihon nang paunti-unti, huwag lahat sabay, para maging tender ang resulta imbes na soggy o clumped.
Hiwain ang lahat ng gulay sa parehong manipis na size para pantay ang pagkaluto sa loob lang ng ilang minuto.
fil.nutritionNote: Carb-heavy dahil sa noodles with modest protein mula sa baboy at hipon; dagdagan ang repolyo at carrot at ihain ng fruit sa tabi imbes na extra rice.

recipes.title: Pancit Palabok
recipes.description: Rice noodles smothered in a thick orange annatto-shrimp sauce and topped with crumbled pork, boiled egg, chicharon and scallions — a party noodle dish built in layers rather than tossed together.

ingredients.item: shrimp, peeled and deveined, shells reserved

ingredients.note: simmer the reserved shrimp shells in water 10 minutes, then strain; or use fish or chicken stock
or 3 tbsp oil steeped with 2 tbsp annatto seeds, strained
or extra crushed chicharon if unavailable

steps: Soak the rice noodles in room-temperature water 15-20 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the noodles 1-2 minutes until just tender; drain and divide among serving plates.
Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant, then add the ground pork and cook until browned.
Add the shrimp and cook 1-2 minutes until pink; lift out half the shrimp and pork mixture to use as a topping later, leaving the rest in the pan.
Pour in the shrimp stock and annatto powder, stirring until the broth turns deep orange, then bring to a simmer.
Stir in the fish sauce, then slowly add the cornstarch slurry, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens into a loose, clingy gravy; season with salt and pepper.
Ladle the hot sauce generously over the noodles on each plate.
Arrange the reserved pork-shrimp mixture, sliced egg, chicharon, tinapa flakes and green onions on top, and serve immediately with calamansi halves for squeezing.
tips: Add the cornstarch slurry gradually and stop as soon as the sauce coats the back of a spoon — it thickens further as it sits.
Keep the noodles, sauce and toppings separate until the table is ready; palabok goes gummy if it sits assembled too long.
Making your own shrimp stock from the shells is a small extra step that noticeably deepens the sauce's flavour.
recipes.nutritionNote: A carb-forward party dish with good protein from pork, shrimp and egg; go light on the chicharon topping and add a vegetable side or soup to round out the meal.

fil.description: Rice noodles na binuhusan ng makapal na orange annatto-shrimp sauce at tinuktukan ng durog na baboy, boiled egg, chicharon at scallions — isang party noodle dish na ginagawa in layers sa halip na i-toss lang.
ingredients: hipon, balatan at nilinis, itinabi ang balat
steps: Ibabad ang rice noodles sa room-temperature na tubig for 15-20 minutes hanggang malambot, tapos i-drain.
Pakuluin ang isang pot ng tubig tapos i-blanch ang noodles for 1-2 minutes hanggang tender lang; i-drain tapos hatiin sa mga serving plates.
Painitin ang mantika sa kawali tapos igisa ang sibuyas at bawang hanggang bumango, tapos idagdag ang ground pork at lutuin hanggang mag-brown.
Idagdag ang hipon tapos lutuin for 1-2 minutes hanggang maging pink; alisin ang kalahati ng pork-shrimp mixture para gamiting topping mamaya, iiwan ang natitira sa kawali.
Ibuhos ang shrimp stock at annatto powder, hinahalo hanggang maging deep orange ang broth, tapos pakuluin nang dahan-dahan.
Ihalo ang patis, tapos dahan-dahang idagdag ang cornstarch slurry, hinahalo palagi, hanggang lumapot at maging loose na gravy ang sauce; timplahan ng asin at paminta.
Buhusan nang sagana ang mainit na sauce sa noodles sa bawat plato.
Ayusin ang natitirang pork-shrimp mixture, hiniwang itlog, chicharon, tinapa flakes at green onions sa ibabaw, tapos ihain agad na may calamansi halves na pwedeng pigain.
tips: Idagdag nang gradual ang cornstarch slurry tapos itigil kapag nababalutan na ng sauce ang likod ng kutsara — lalapot pa ito habang naghihintay.
Panatilihing hiwalay ang noodles, sauce at toppings hanggang handa na sa mesa; nagiging gummy ang palabok kapag matagal nang naka-assemble.
Ang paggawa ng sarili mong shrimp stock galing sa balat ay maliit na extra step na malaking tulong sa lasa ng sauce.
fil.nutritionNote: Isang carb-forward na party dish na may magandang protein galing sa baboy, hipon at itlog; bawasan ang chicharon topping tapos magdagdag ng vegetable side o soup para mas balanced ang meal.

recipes.title: Pinakbet
recipes.description: Squash, eggplant, okra, long beans and bitter gourd simmered with a little pork and shrimp paste — the vegetable dish every Ilocano and Tagalog table has its own version of.

ingredients.note: or bagoong isda (fermented fish) for the more traditional Ilocano version

ingredients.item: kalabasa (squash), peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the pork and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned at the edges.
Stir in the shrimp paste and cook 1-2 minutes until it deepens in colour and smells toasty.
Add the tomatoes and mash them into the mixture with the back of a spoon until softened and juicy.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer 15-20 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the squash and cook about 2 minutes until almost tender.
Add the long beans and cook until tender-crisp, then add the bitter gourd, eggplant and okra.
Cook 4-5 minutes more until the vegetables are tender yet still hold their shape; season with salt and pepper and serve hot with rice.
tips: Add the vegetables in stages, hardest first, and stop cooking while they still have bite — overcooked pinakbet turns mushy and grey.
Salting the sliced ampalaya and rinsing it before cooking mellows its bitterness.
Resist stirring too often once the vegetables are in; a gentle toss keeps them from breaking apart.
recipes.kidNote: Bitter gourd is the vegetable most kids push aside — load each child's portion heavier on squash, long beans and eggplant, with just a token piece or two of ampalaya so they get used to the flavour without a full plate of it.
recipes.nutritionNote: An excellent fibre-rich, vegetable-forward dish that's lower in rice-displacing starch than most Filipino mains; the pork and shrimp paste add sodium, so skip extra patis or soy sauce at the table tonight.

fil.description: Kalabasa, talong, okra, sitaw at ampalaya na ni-simmer with kaunting baboy at bagoong — ang vegetable dish na bawat Ilocano at Tagalog family may sariling version.
ingredients: kalabasa, balatan at hiwain into chunks
ampalaya, alisin ang buto at hiwain
steps: Painitin ang oil sa pot sa medium heat; igisa ang sibuyas at bawang hanggang lumambot.
Idagdag ang baboy at lutuin, haluin paminsan-minsan, hanggang lightly browned ang gilid.
Ihalo ang bagoong at lutuin for 1-2 minutes hanggang tumingkad ang kulay at mag-amoy toasty.
Idagdag ang kamatis at dikdikin gamit ang likod ng kutsara hanggang lumambot at maging juicy.
Ibuhos ang tubig, pakuluin, tapos hinaan ang apoy, takpan at i-simmer for 15-20 minutes hanggang malambot ang baboy.
Idagdag ang kalabasa at lutuin about 2 minutes hanggang halos malambot na.
Idagdag ang sitaw at lutuin hanggang tender-crisp, tapos idagdag ang ampalaya, talong at okra.
Lutuin ng 4-5 minutes more hanggang malambot pero hindi nawawala ang hugis ng gulay; timplahan ng asin at paminta at ihain mainit with rice.
tips: Idagdag ang gulay in stages, matigas muna, at itigil ang pagluluto habang may bite pa — nagiging mushy at kulay-abo ang overcooked pinakbet.
Ang pag-aasin ng hiniwang ampalaya at paghuhugas nito bago lutuin ay nagpapabawas ng pait.
Iwasan ang sobrang haluin pag nasa loob na ang gulay; gentle toss lang para hindi masira ang hugis.
fil.kidNote: Ang ampalaya ang pinaka-itinatabi ng mga bata sa plato — dagdagan ang portion nila ng kalabasa, sitaw at talong, tapos konting piraso lang ng ampalaya para masanay sila sa lasa nang hindi puno ang plato nito.
fil.nutritionNote: Excellent fibre-rich at vegetable-forward na dish na mas mababa sa starch kompara sa ibang Filipino mains; ang baboy at bagoong ay nagdadagdag ng sodium, kaya laktawan na muna ang extra patis o toyo sa hapag ngayong gabi.

recipes.title: Pineapple Chicken
recipes.description: Chicken braised with pineapple chunks and juice, carrots and bell pepper in a lightly creamy sauce — a sweet, kid-favourite spin on the everyday chicken stew.

ingredients.note: 20 oz / 567 g can; separate the chunks from the juice

steps: Marinate the chicken pieces in the reserved pineapple juice for 20-30 minutes.
Lift the chicken out, reserving the marinade, and pat it dry.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat and sear the chicken until lightly browned on both sides; set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion and garlic until softened, then return the chicken to the pot.
Pour in the reserved pineapple marinade and enough water to nearly cover the chicken; bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and simmer 20-25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the pineapple chunks and carrot; simmer 5 minutes until the carrot is just tender.
Stir in the evaporated milk and fish sauce, and simmer uncovered 3-4 minutes until the sauce lightly thickens.
Add the bell pepper, season with pepper to taste, and cook 2 minutes more until just tender; serve hot with rice.
tips: Use the canned pineapple juice as the marinade rather than discarding it — it tenderizes the chicken and seasons the sauce at the same time.
Add the bell pepper last so it keeps some crunch instead of going limp.
recipes.nutritionNote: A milder, lower-sodium chicken dish thanks to the fruit sweetness carrying much of the flavour; balance the natural sugar from the pineapple with a smaller rice portion and a side of leafy greens.

fil.description: Manok na ni-braise na may pineapple chunks at juice, carrots at bell pepper sa isang light creamy sauce — isang matamis, paboritong ulam ng mga bata na spin sa everyday chicken stew.
steps: I-marinate ang manok sa reserved pineapple juice for 20-30 minutes.
Alisin ang manok, i-reserve ang marinade, tapos i-pat dry.
Painitin ang mantika sa pot over medium-high heat tapos i-sear ang manok hanggang medyo mag-brown sa dalawang sides; itabi.
Sa parehong pot, igisa ang sibuyas at bawang hanggang lumambot, tapos ibalik ang manok sa pot.
Ibuhos ang reserved pineapple marinade at sapat na tubig para halos matakpan ang manok; pakuluin, tapos hinaan ang heat, takpan, at i-simmer for 20-25 minutes hanggang maluto ang manok.
Idagdag ang pineapple chunks at carrot; i-simmer for 5 minutes hanggang tender lang ang carrot.
Ihalo ang evaporated milk at patis, tapos i-simmer uncovered for 3-4 minutes hanggang medyo lumapot ang sauce.
Idagdag ang bell pepper, timplahan ng paminta, tapos lutuin for 2 minutes more hanggang tender lang; ihain mainit na may kanin.
tips: Gamitin ang canned pineapple juice bilang marinade sa halip na itapon lang — pinapalambot nito ang manok at nagbibigay lasa sa sauce nang sabay.
Idagdag ang bell pepper sa dulo para may crunch pa, hindi nalalanta.
fil.nutritionNote: Mas mild at mababa sa sodium na chicken dish dahil sa natural na tamis ng prutas na nagdadala ng flavor; balansehin ang natural na sugar ng pineapple sa mas maliit na rice portion at side ng gulay.

recipes.title: Pork Menudo
recipes.description: Pork and liver simmered in a tomato sauce with potatoes, carrots, garbanzo beans and raisins — a hearty stew with a faint sweetness that shows up at Filipino gatherings and Sunday lunches alike.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into small cubes
pork liver, cut into small cubes
ingredients.note: or omit and add extra pork shoulder for a milder version

steps: Combine the pork with the soy sauce and calamansi juice; marinate 10-15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot and pan-fry the potatoes and carrots until lightly browned at the edges; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion and garlic until softened, then add the marinated pork and cook until browned.
Add the tomatoes and cook, mashing them into the pork, until they break down into a sauce.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and simmer 25-30 minutes until the pork is tender.
Stir in the liver and cook 3-4 minutes, just until it loses its raw colour.
Add the fried potatoes and carrots, garbanzo beans and raisins; simmer 8-10 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the bell pepper and fish sauce, season with salt and pepper, and cook 2-3 minutes more before serving hot with rice.
tips: Adding the liver later, rather than browning it with the pork, keeps it from turning grainy.
Pan-frying the potatoes and carrots first helps them hold their shape through the simmer instead of turning mushy.
Menudo freezes and reheats well, making it a good make-ahead dish for a crowd.
