recipes.nutritionNote: A balanced one-pot meal with protein, iron-rich liver and vegetables built in; the raisins add natural sugar, so a normal rice portion without extra sweet sides keeps the meal in balance.

fil.description: Baboy at atay na sini-simmer sa tomato sauce na may patatas, carrots, garbanzos at raisins — isang hearty stew na may kaunting tamis na lumalabas sa mga Filipino gatherings at Sunday lunch.
ingredients: pork shoulder, hiniwa into small cubes
pork liver, hiniwa into small cubes
patatas, balatan at hiwain into cubes
carrots, balatan at hiwain into cubes
steps: Ihalo ang baboy sa toyo at calamansi juice; i-marinate for 10-15 minutes.
Painitin ang mantika sa pot tapos i-pan-fry ang patatas at carrots hanggang medyo mag-brown ang gilid; alisin tapos itabi.
Sa parehong pot, igisa ang sibuyas at bawang hanggang lumambot, tapos idagdag ang na-marinate na baboy at lutuin hanggang mag-brown.
Idagdag ang kamatis tapos lutuin, dinidiin papasok sa baboy, hanggang maging sauce.
Ibuhos ang tubig, pakuluin, tapos hinaan ang heat, takpan, at i-simmer for 25-30 minutes hanggang lumambot ang baboy.
Ihalo ang atay tapos lutuin for 3-4 minutes, hanggang mawala lang ang raw color nito.
Idagdag ang pinritong patatas at carrots, garbanzo beans at raisins; i-simmer for 8-10 minutes hanggang tender ang gulay.
Ihalo ang bell pepper at patis, timplahan ng asin at paminta, tapos lutuin for 2-3 minutes more bago ihain mainit na may kanin.
tips: Ang pagdagdag ng atay sa dulo, sa halip na i-brown kasama ng baboy, ay pumipigil dito na maging grainy.
Ang pag-pan-fry ng patatas at carrots muna ay tumutulong para hindi maging mushy sa simmer.
Ang menudo ay pwedeng i-freeze at reheat nang maayos, kaya magandang make-ahead dish para sa maraming tao.
fil.nutritionNote: Isang balanced na one-pot meal na may protein, iron-rich na atay at gulay na kasama na; nagdadagdag ng natural sugar ang raisins, kaya normal na rice portion lang nang walang extra sweet sides ang magpapanatili sa balance.

recipes.title: Pork Sinigang
recipes.description: Pork ribs and vegetables simmered in a sour tamarind broth — the pucker-inducing soup Filipinos crave on rainy days and reach for when someone's under the weather.

ingredients.item: pork spare ribs, cut into 2-inch pieces

ingredients.note: adds aroma, not real heat; leave out entirely for a milder pot
or 15 pieces fresh tamarind pods, boiled soft and strained, for a more traditional sour base

steps: Rinse the pork ribs and place in a large pot; cover with the water and bring to a boil over medium heat, skimming off the scum that rises.
Once the broth runs clear, add the tomatoes, onion and fish sauce; lower the heat and simmer 45-60 minutes, covered, until the pork is fork-tender.
Add the taro and cook 5-6 minutes until it starts to soften and lightly thickens the broth.
Stir in the tamarind soup base until dissolved, then taste — the broth should be assertively sour.
Add the radish and chilies; simmer 3 minutes.
Add the long beans, eggplant and okra; cook 3-4 minutes until just tender but not mushy.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then add the bok choy and cook 1 minute more, just until wilted.
Remove from the heat right away, since bok choy overcooks fast, and serve hot in bowls with steamed rice.
tips: Parboil-and-discard the first pork water for a cleaner, less cloudy broth if you have the time.
Add vegetables in order of cook time — roots first, leafy greens last — so nothing turns to mush.
The broth should taste sour before you add salt; sinigang is meant to pucker slightly.
recipes.kidNote: Ladle the kids' broth before adding the whole chilies, and go a little lighter on the tamarind base in their portion if they're sensitive to sour — pork, taro and soft vegetables over rice is usually an easy sell.
recipes.nutritionNote: A vegetable-packed, comparatively lean soup once you skim the fat; the broth alone is fairly low in carbohydrate, so a normal rice portion alongside is well balanced and the vegetables cover fibre and vitamin C.

fil.description: Pork ribs at gulay na pinakuluan sa maasim na tamarind broth — ang paborito ng mga Pinoy tuwing umuulan at go-to kapag may masama ang pakiramdam sa bahay.
ingredients: pork spare ribs, hiwain into 2-inch pieces
gabi, balatan at hiwain in half
steps: Hugasan ang pork ribs at ilagay sa malaking pot; takpan ng tubig at pakuluin sa medium heat, alisin ang dumi na lumulutang.
Kapag malinaw na ang sabaw, idagdag ang kamatis, sibuyas at patis; hinaan ang apoy at i-simmer for 45-60 minutes, covered, hanggang malambot na ang baboy.
Idagdag ang gabi at lutuin for 5-6 minutes hanggang magsimulang lumambot at slight na lumapot ang sabaw.
Ihalo ang sinigang mix hanggang matunaw, tapos tikman — dapat maasim talaga ang sabaw.
Idagdag ang labanos at sili; i-simmer for 3 minutes.
Idagdag ang sitaw, talong at okra; lutuin for 3-4 minutes hanggang tender-crisp lang, huwag hanggang malambot na malambot.
Timplahan ng asin at paminta to taste, tapos idagdag ang pechay at lutuin ng 1 minute more, hanggang lang malanta.
Alisin agad sa apoy dahil mabilis mag-overcook ang pechay, at ihain mainit with rice.
tips: I-parboil muna at itapon ang unang sabaw ng baboy para mas malinis at hindi malabo ang broth, kung meron kang time.
Ilagay ang gulay ayon sa cook time — ugat muna, dahon last — para walang mag-mushy.
Dapat maasim na ang sabaw bago pa lagyan ng asin; talagang mangangalasa ang sinigang.
fil.kidNote: I-ladle muna ang sabaw para sa bata bago idagdag ang buong sili, at bawasan ang sinigang mix sa portion nila kung sensitive sa asim — baboy, gabi at malambot na gulay with rice ay usually okay lang sa kanila.
fil.nutritionNote: Maraming gulay at medyo lean na soup kapag naalisan ng fat; mababa sa carbs ang sabaw lang, kaya okay lang ang normal na rice portion at ang gulay na naman ang bahala sa fibre at vitamin C.

recipes.title: Sweet and Sour Fish
recipes.description: Fried whole fish drenched in a glossy sweet-and-sour sauce with bell peppers, carrots and ginger — a bright, tangy way to turn an everyday market fish into a dinner-table centerpiece.

ingredients.item: whole tilapia or lapu-lapu, cleaned and scored
ingredients.note: or use firm fillets cut into large pieces

ingredients.item: red bell pepper, sliced into strips

steps: Season the fish with salt inside and out, then dredge lightly in cornstarch, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and fry the fish 4-5 minutes per side until golden and crisp; drain on paper towels.
Pour off most of the oil, leaving about 1 tablespoon, and sauté the ginger, garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the carrot and cook 1-2 minutes, then add the bell pepper and stir-fry until just tender-crisp.
Pour in the vinegar, sugar, water and soy sauce; bring to a boil and let it bubble 1-2 minutes without stirring.
Stir the cornstarch slurry into the sauce and cook, stirring, until it thickens into a glossy glaze.
Place the fried fish on a serving platter and pour the hot sweet-sour sauce and vegetables over the top.
Serve immediately while the fish is still crisp, with steamed rice.
tips: Fry the fish until genuinely crisp — the hot sauce will soften it slightly, so it needs a head start.
Boil the vinegar briefly before thickening the sauce to cook off its raw sharpness.
Pour the sauce over just before serving so the fish doesn't sit and go soggy.
recipes.kidNote: Check the fried fish carefully for small bones before serving to the 6-year-old, or serve deboned fillets instead of the whole fish for the kids' plates.
recipes.nutritionNote: A lean protein dish once you account for the light frying; the carrot and bell pepper add vitamin A and C, and the sauce's sugar is balanced out by a normal, not oversized, rice portion.

fil.description: Pinritong buong isda na binuhusan ng makintab na sweet-and-sour sauce na may bell peppers, carrots at luya — isang maliwanag at maasim na paraan para gawing dinner-table centerpiece ang ordinaryong isda sa palengke.
ingredients: whole tilapia o lapu-lapu, nilinis at hiniwa
red bell pepper, hiniwa into strips
steps: Timplahan ang isda ng asin sa loob at labas, tapos i-dredge nang manipis sa cornstarch, alisin ang excess.
Painitin ang mantika sa malapad na kawali over medium-high heat tapos i-fry ang isda for 4-5 minutes per side hanggang golden at malutong; i-drain sa paper towels.
Ibuhos ang karamihan sa mantika, iiwan lang ng mga 1 tablespoon, tapos igisa ang luya, bawang at sibuyas hanggang bumango.
Idagdag ang carrot tapos lutuin for 1-2 minutes, tapos idagdag ang bell pepper at i-stir-fry hanggang tender-crisp lang.
Ibuhos ang vinegar, sugar, tubig at toyo; pakuluin tapos hayaang kumulo for 1-2 minutes nang hindi hinahalo.
Ihalo ang cornstarch slurry sa sauce tapos lutuin, hinahalo, hanggang lumapot at maging makintab.
Ilagay ang pinritong isda sa serving platter tapos ibuhos ang mainit na sweet-sour sauce at gulay sa ibabaw.
Ihain agad habang malutong pa ang isda, may kanin.
tips: I-fry ang isda hanggang talagang malutong — palalambutin ito nang kaunti ng mainit na sauce, kaya kailangan ng head start.
Pakuluin muna ang vinegar bago lapotin ang sauce para maalis ang raw na asim nito.
Ibuhos ang sauce bago mismo ihain para hindi malanta ang isda.
fil.kidNote: Suriin nang maigi ang pinritong isda para sa maliliit na buto bago ihain sa 6-year-old, o gumamit ng deboned fillets sa halip na buong isda para sa plato ng mga bata.
fil.nutritionNote: Isang lean protein dish kahit may light frying; ang carrot at bell pepper ay may vitamin A at C, at ang sugar ng sauce ay nababalanse ng normal, hindi sobrang laki, na rice portion.

recipes.title: Aloo Gobi
recipes.description: Potatoes and cauliflower pan-fried golden, then tossed through a cumin tempering with dry spices — genuinely spicy-hot bite for bite since there's no gravy to dilute the heat, not just heavily spiced.
steps: Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a wide pan and shallow-fry the cauliflower florets in batches until golden at the edges; drain and set aside.
In the same oil, fry the potato cubes until golden and crisp; drain and set aside.
Wipe out the pan, heat the remaining oil and add the cumin seeds and dried fenugreek leaves; let them sizzle until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until soft and lightly browned.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilli and saute for a minute.
Lower the heat and stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder with a splash of water so they don't scorch.
Add the tomato and cook until it softens and the raw smell disappears.
Gently fold in the fried potatoes and cauliflower, coating them in the masala without breaking them up.
Sprinkle over the amchur and garam masala, toss once more, and garnish with coriander leaves.
tips: Frying the cauliflower and potatoes separately before adding the masala is what keeps this sabzi dry rather than mushy.
Fold, don't stir, once the vegetables go back in — cauliflower breaks apart easily.
recipes.kidNote: Because there's no gravy to dilute the spice, the heat lands harder bite for bite — set aside the kids' portion before adding the slit green chilli and use only a pinch of chilli powder in their share, finishing with a little extra coriander instead. The cumin-fenugreek tempering still comes through for flavour.
recipes.nutritionNote: A fibre- and vitamin-C-rich vegetable side that's genuinely low in fat once you go easy on the frying oil; pair with a dal or rajma for the protein this dish doesn't provide on its own.

fil.description: Patatas at cauliflower na pan-fried hanggang golden, tapos hinalo sa cumin tempering with dry spices — tunay na maanghang bite by bite dahil walang gravy na magpapabawas ng init, hindi lang heavily spiced.
steps: Painitin ang 3 tbsp oil sa wide pan at shallow-fry ang cauliflower florets in batches hanggang golden sa gilid; i-drain at itabi muna.
Sa parehong oil, iprito ang patatas hanggang golden at crisp; i-drain at itabi muna.
Punasan ang pan, painitin ang natitirang oil at ilagay ang cumin seeds at dried fenugreek leaves; hayaang mag-sizzle hanggang bumango.
Idagdag ang sibuyas at lutuin hanggang malambot at light brown.
Idagdag ang ginger-garlic paste at green chilli at igisa for a minute.
Hinaan ang apoy tapos ihalo ang turmeric, chilli powder at coriander powder with a splash of water para hindi masusunog.
Idagdag ang kamatis at lutuin hanggang lumambot at mawala ang raw smell.
Ihalo nang mahinay ang fried potatoes at cauliflower, pahiran ng masala na hindi nadudurog.
Budburan ng amchur at garam masala, haluin ulit, at garnish ng wansoy leaves.
tips: Ang paghiwalay ng pagprito ng cauliflower at patatas bago idagdag ang masala ang nagpapanatili sa sabzi na dry sa halip na mushy.
I-fold, huwag haluin, kapag nabalik na ang gulay — madaling madurog ang cauliflower.
fil.kidNote: Dahil walang gravy na magpapabawas ng init, mas matindi ang anghang bite by bite — ikuha muna ang share ng mga bata bago ilagay ang slit green chilli at gumamit lang ng kaunting chilli powder sa share nila, tapos dagdagan na lang ng extra wansoy sa halip. Mararamdaman pa rin ang cumin-fenugreek tempering para sa lasa.
fil.nutritionNote: Isang fibre- at vitamin-C-rich na vegetable side na mababa talaga sa fat kung bawasan ang frying oil; isabay sa dal o rajma para sa protein na wala sa dish na ito.

recipes.title: Baingan Bharta
recipes.description: A whole eggplant charred over an open flame until the skin blisters and the flesh turns smoky-soft, then mashed and cooked down with onion, tomato and ginger — properly spicy-hot, letting the char come through rather than burying it in cream.
steps: Pierce the eggplant a few times with a knife, rub lightly with oil, and roast it directly over an open gas flame (or under a hot grill), turning occasionally, for 12-15 minutes until the skin is blackened and blistered all over and a knife slides through the flesh easily.
Let the eggplant cool, then peel off the charred skin under running water and discard the stem; roughly mash the smoky flesh with a fork.
Heat the oil in a pan and add the cumin seeds; let them sizzle until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook over medium heat until golden brown.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilli, and saute for a minute.
Add the tomato and cook, stirring often, until it softens and turns pulpy.
Lower the heat and stir in the turmeric and chilli powder with a splash of water so they bloom without scorching.
Add the mashed eggplant and salt, and cook uncovered over medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until the mixture dries out and no longer tastes raw.
Sprinkle over the garam masala, mix, and finish with coriander leaves.
tips: Charring the eggplant directly over a flame is what makes bharta taste smoky — an oven-roasted eggplant cooks through but misses that flavour, so finish it briefly under the broiler if that's your only option.
Cook the mashed eggplant uncovered until it visibly dries and thickens; a wet bharta tastes unfinished.
recipes.kidNote: Skip the green chilli and use half the red chilli powder in the batch for the kids, and stir their portion in a minute earlier so it spends less time over direct heat — the smoky char and cumin-onion base still carry the dish without the sharp heat.
recipes.nutritionNote: Eggplant is naturally low in calories and a decent source of fibre; this version uses no cream, so it's one of the lighter vegetable sides here — good to pair with a protein-rich dal or rajma.

fil.description: Isang buong eggplant na ni-char sa open flame hanggang mag-blister ang balat at maging smoky-soft ang laman, tapos dinikdik at niluto with onion, kamatis at luya — talagang spicy-hot, hinahayaang lumabas ang char kesa itago sa cream.
steps: Butasan ang eggplant ng ilang beses gamit ang kutsilyo, pahiran nang bahagya ng oil, at i-roast directly over open gas flame (o under hot grill), i-turn paminsan-minsan, for 12-15 minutes hanggang mag-itim at mag-blister ang balat all over at madaling makapasok ang kutsilyo sa laman.
Palamigin ang eggplant, tapos alisin ang charred skin under running water at itapon ang tangkay; dikdikin nang bahagya ang smoky flesh gamit ang fork.
Painitin ang oil sa pan at idagdag ang cumin seeds; hayaang mag-sizzle hanggang bumango.
Idagdag ang onion at lutuin sa medium heat hanggang golden brown.
Idagdag ang ginger-garlic paste at green chilli, at igisa for a minute.
Idagdag ang kamatis at lutuin, haluin nang madalas, hanggang lumambot at maging pulpy.
Hinaan ang apoy at ihalo ang turmeric at chilli powder with splash of water para mag-bloom without masunog.
Idagdag ang mashed eggplant at asin, at lutuin nang bukas sa medium heat for 8-10 minutes, haluin nang madalas, hanggang matuyo ang mixture at wala nang lasang raw.
Budburan ng garam masala, haluin, at finish with coriander leaves.
tips: Ang pag-char sa eggplant directly over flame ang nagbibigay sa bharta ng smoky taste — kapag oven-roasted lang, maluluto pero mawawala ang flavor na iyon, kaya i-finish nang bahagya under the broiler kung wala talagang open flame.
Lutuin ang mashed eggplant nang bukas hanggang halatang matuyo at lumapot; parang hindi tapos ang lasa ng basang bharta.
fil.kidNote: Laktawan ang green chilli at gumamit ng kalahati lang ng red chilli powder sa batch para sa mga bata, at ihalo ang share nila nang isang minuto earlier para mas kaunti ang oras nito sa direct heat — nandiyan pa rin ang smoky char at cumin-onion base para dalhin ang dish without the sharp heat.
fil.nutritionNote: Naturally low in calories ang eggplant at decent source ng fibre; walang cream ang version na ito, kaya isa ito sa mas light na vegetable sides dito — magandang i-pair with protein-rich na dal o rajma.

recipes.title: Beans Poriyal
recipes.description: Finely chopped green beans stir-fried with a mustard-seed and urad dal tempering, then tossed with fresh grated coconut — a dry, mild South Indian vegetable side that keeps its crunch and bright colour.
steps: Heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and add the mustard seeds; let them splutter.
Add the urad dal, dried red chillies and curry leaves, and fry until the dal turns golden.
Add the chopped beans, turmeric and salt, and toss well to coat in the tempering.
Add a splash of water, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are just tender but still bright green.
Uncover and cook a minute longer over higher heat to evaporate any remaining moisture, so the poriyal stays dry rather than steamed.
Stir in the grated coconut, toss for a minute to warm it through, and serve.
tips: Chop the beans small and even so they cook through in the same time without turning mushy.
Add the coconut right at the end off the heat if serving later — it stays freshest that way.
recipes.nutritionNote: A fibre- and vitamin-rich vegetable side that's naturally low in fat; the coconut is used sparingly as a finish rather than a sauce, so it pairs well even on days you're serving a richer curry.

fil.description: Green beans na tinadtad nang pino at ginisa sa mustard-seed at urad dal tempering, tapos hinalo sa fresh grated coconut — dry at mild na South Indian vegetable side na hindi nawawalan ng crunch at bright na kulay.
steps: Painitin ang coconut oil sa wide pan at idagdag ang mustard seeds; hayaang mag-splutter.
Idagdag ang urad dal, dried red chillies at curry leaves, at i-fry hanggang golden ang dal.
Idagdag ang chopped beans, turmeric at asin, at i-toss nang maigi para mabalutan sa tempering.
Magdagdag ng splash ng tubig, takpan, at lutuin sa low-medium heat for 8-10 minutes, haluin paminsan-minsan, hanggang lumambot lang ang beans pero manatiling bright green pa rin.
Buksan at lutuin pa ng isang minuto sa mas mataas na apoy para mag-evaporate ang natitirang moisture, para manatiling dry ang poriyal kesa steamed.
Ihalo ang grated coconut, i-toss for a minute para uminit, at ihain.
tips: Tadtarin ang beans nang maliit at pantay para maluto sabay without maging mushy.
Idagdag ang coconut right at the end, off the heat, kung ihahain later — mas fresh ito nang ganon.
fil.nutritionNote: Fiber- at vitamin-rich na vegetable side na naturally low in fat; sparingly lang ginamit ang coconut as finish kesa sauce, kaya bagay ito kahit may mas richer curry ka nang iho-hain.

recipes.title: Butter Chicken
recipes.description: Tandoori-marinated chicken simmered in a velvety butter-tomato-cashew gravy, finished with cream and kasuri methi — mildly spiced, the restaurant classic that wins over spice-shy eaters.
steps: Mix the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, garam masala, kasuri methi and salt; marinate at least 1 hour, ideally overnight in the fridge.
Boil the tomatoes and cashews together in 1 cup water for 12-15 minutes until soft, then blend to a smooth puree.
Pan-sear the marinated chicken in a splash of butter over medium-high heat until charred at the edges but not cooked through; set aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the same pan and add the cinnamon, cardamom and cloves; let them sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the chilli powder and garam masala so the ground spices bloom in the residual heat without scorching.
Pour in the tomato-cashew puree, return to the heat and simmer 12-15 minutes, stirring, until the fat separates at the edges.
Add the seared chicken, sugar and enough water to loosen the gravy; cover and simmer 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the cream and crushed kasuri methi off the heat, then serve.
tips: Marinating the chicken overnight is what makes it tender — do not skip past the 1-hour minimum.
Simmer the tomato puree until the butter visibly separates at the edges; that's the sign the raw tomato taste is gone.
recipes.nutritionNote: Rich in protein from the chicken but heavy in butter and cream — balance the plate with a cucumber-onion salad and go light on naan if rice is also on the table.

fil.description: Tandoori-marinated na manok na sinimmer sa velvety butter-tomato-cashew gravy, finished with cream at kasuri methi — mild lang ang spice, ang restaurant classic na kinakain kahit ng ayaw sa maanghang.
ingredients: hinog na kamatis, hiniwa sa apat
steps: Ihalo ang manok sa yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, garam masala, kasuri methi at asin; i-marinate for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight sa ref.
Pakuluan ang kamatis at cashew sa 1 cup water for 12-15 minutes hanggang lumambot, tapos i-blend hanggang maging smooth puree.
I-sear ang na-marinate na manok sa konting butter sa medium-high heat hanggang mag-char sa gilid pero hindi pa fully cooked; itabi muna.
Tunawin ang natitirang butter sa parehong pan tapos ilagay ang cinnamon, cardamom at cloves; hayaang mag-sizzle for 30 seconds hanggang bumango.
Alisin ang pan sa apoy tapos ihalo ang chilli powder at garam masala para mag-bloom ang mga powdered spices sa residual heat na hindi nasusunog.
Ibuhos ang tomato-cashew puree, ibalik sa apoy at i-simmer for 12-15 minutes, haluin, hanggang mag-separate ang fat sa gilid.
Idagdag ang seared chicken, asukal at sapat na tubig para maluwagan ang gravy; takpan at i-simmer for 10 minutes hanggang ma-cook through ang manok.
Ihalo ang cream at dinurog na kasuri methi off the heat, tapos ihain.
tips: Ang overnight marinate ang gumagawa sa manok na malambot — huwag laktawan ang 1-hour minimum.
I-simmer ang tomato puree hanggang makitang nag-separate ang butter sa gilid; yun ang sign na wala nang raw tomato taste.
fil.nutritionNote: Mataas sa protein galing sa manok pero heavy sa butter at cream — balansehin ang plato ng cucumber-onion salad at bawasan ang naan kung may rice na rin sa table.

recipes.title: Chana Masala
recipes.description: Chickpeas simmered in a deeply bhuna'd onion-tomato masala with whole spices and green chillies — tangy, robust and properly spicy-hot rather than just heavily spiced, classic chole.
steps: Drain the soaked chickpeas and pressure-cook with the cinnamon, cloves, black cardamom, bay leaf and fresh water for 15 minutes until completely tender.
Heat the oil in a pan and add the carom seeds; let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Add the onion and saute over medium heat until golden brown.
Add the ginger paste and garlic paste and cook for a minute until the raw smell disappears.
Lower the heat and stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and garam masala with a splash of water so the powders don't scorch.
Add the tomato and green chillies and cook, stirring often, for 8-10 minutes until the masala turns glossy and the oil separates.
Add the cooked chickpeas with their stock, the amchur and salt; simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the gravy.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.
tips: Soak the chickpeas at least 8 hours; they roughly double in size and cook more evenly.
Cooking the masala until it turns glossy and the oil visibly separates is the real test that the raw tomato taste is gone.
recipes.kidNote: Hold back the slit green chillies and use only half a teaspoon of chilli powder in the batch you'll serve the kids, then finish their bowls with a spoonful of yogurt on the side to cool it down — the whole spices (cinnamon, cloves, cardamom) stay in for aroma without any heat.
recipes.nutritionNote: Chickpeas are a strong plant protein and fibre source, especially paired with rice or roti for a complete meal; the dish itself is low in fat, so it's a good counterbalance on days you've served something buttery.

fil.description: Chickpeas na sinimmer sa maigting na bhuna'd onion-tomato masala with whole spices at green chillies — tangy, robust at tunay na maanghang, hindi lang heavily spiced, ang classic chole.
steps: I-drain ang naibabad na chickpeas at pressure-cook kasama ang cinnamon, cloves, black cardamom, bay leaf at fresh water for 15 minutes hanggang completely tender.
Painitin ang oil sa pan at ilagay ang carom seeds; hayaang mag-sizzle for a few seconds.
Idagdag ang sibuyas at igisa sa medium heat hanggang golden brown.
Idagdag ang ginger paste at garlic paste at lutuin for a minute hanggang mawala ang raw smell.
Hinaan ang apoy tapos ihalo ang turmeric, chilli powder at garam masala with a splash of water para hindi masusunog ang powders.
Idagdag ang kamatis at green chillies at lutuin, haluin often, for 8-10 minutes hanggang maging glossy ang masala at mag-separate ang oil.
Idagdag ang lutong chickpeas kasama ang stock nito, ang amchur at asin; i-simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, dinudurog ang ilang chickpeas para lumapot ang gravy.
Garnish ng wansoy leaves at ihain mainit.
tips: I-soak ang chickpeas for at least 8 hours; halos doble ang laki nito at mas even ang pagkaluto.
Ang pagluto ng masala hanggang maging glossy at makitang nag-separate ang oil ang tunay na test na wala nang raw tomato taste.
fil.kidNote: Ikuha muna ang share ng mga bata bago ilagay ang slit green chillies at gumamit lang ng kalahating tsp na chilli powder sa batch nila, tapos tapusin ng kutsarang yogurt sa tabi para pumalamig — mananatili ang whole spices (cinnamon, cloves, cardamom) para sa bango na walang init.
fil.nutritionNote: Ang chickpeas ay strong na plant protein at fibre source, lalo na kapag isinabay sa rice o roti para maging complete meal; mababa sa fat ang dish mismo, kaya magandang counterbalance sa araw na may naihain kang mamantika.

recipes.title: Chapati
recipes.description: Whole-wheat dough rolled thin and puffed straight over an open flame until it balloons with steam — the plain, unspiced everyday flatbread that shows up at almost every Indian meal.

ingredients.item: extra whole wheat flour, for dusting

steps: Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl, then add the water gradually, bringing the dough together as you go.
Knead for 5-7 minutes until the dough is soft, smooth and no longer sticky; cover and rest for 20-30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 12 equal balls and roll each one out on a floured surface into a thin, even circle.
Heat a tawa or flat griddle over medium-high heat; lay a rolled circle on it and cook for about 20 seconds until small bubbles appear.
Flip and cook the second side for about 30 seconds until light brown spots form.
Using tongs, lift the roti and place it directly over an open flame for a few seconds until it puffs up like a balloon; flip once to puff the other side.
Remove from the flame, brush lightly with ghee if using, and stack in a cloth-lined container to keep soft.
Repeat with the remaining dough, rolling the next roti while the previous one cooks.
tips: Resting the dough for at least 20 minutes relaxes the gluten and makes the rotis easier to roll thin and round.
No open flame at home — press the roti firmly with a folded cloth on the tawa instead; it will puff from the trapped steam just the same.
recipes.nutritionNote: A whole-grain carbohydrate that's naturally low in fat — the healthiest bread option on the table next to naan or paratha, and an easy way to get whole grains into the kids without them noticing.

fil.description: Whole-wheat dough na ginulong nang manipis at pinapuffed diretso sa open flame hanggang mamaga sa steam — ang plain, unspiced everyday flatbread na laging nasa halos bawat Indian meal.
steps: Ihalo ang harina at asin sa malaking mangkok, tapos ilagay nang paunti-unti ang tubig, hanguin ang dough habang tumatagal.
I-knead for 5-7 minutes hanggang malambot, makinis at hindi na malengkit ang dough; takpan at pahingahin for 20-30 minutes.
Hatiin ang dough sa 12 pantay na bola at igulong ang bawat isa sa flour-dusted na surface hanggang maging manipis at pantay na bilog.
Painitin ang tawa o flat griddle sa medium-high heat; ilagay ang ginulong na bilog dito at lutuin for about 20 seconds hanggang lumitaw ang maliliit na bula.
Ibaligtad at lutuin ang kabilang side for about 30 seconds hanggang lumitaw ang light brown spots.
Gamit ang tongs, buhatin ang roti at ilagay diretso sa ibabaw ng open flame for a few seconds hanggang mamaga na parang balloon; ibaligtad para mapaga rin ang kabilang side.
Alisin sa flame, pahiran nang bahagya ng ghee kung gagamitin, at i-stack sa cloth-lined na container para manatiling malambot.
Ulitin sa natitirang dough, iginulong ang susunod na roti habang niluluto ang isa.
tips: Ang pagpapahinga ng dough for at least 20 minutes ang nagre-relax sa gluten at nagpapadali sa pag-roll ng manipis at maayos na hugis na roti.
Walang open flame sa bahay — pindutin nang mahigpit ang roti gamit ang tiklop na tela sa tawa; mamamaga pa rin ito dahil sa trapped steam.
fil.nutritionNote: Whole-grain carb na naturally mababa sa fat — ang pinaka-healthy na bread option sa table kumpara sa naan o paratha, at madaling paraan para makapasok ang whole grains sa mga bata na hindi man lang nila mamamalayan.

recipes.title: Chicken Biryani
recipes.description: Marinated chicken layered with part-cooked basmati and dum-steamed under a sealed lid — heavily spiced with whole garam masala but only a moderate chilli warmth, a special-occasion one-pot rice dish.

ingredients.item: aged basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 30 minutes
thinly sliced onion, fried until golden
warm milk with a pinch of saffron

steps: Mix the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, garam masala and lemon juice; marinate at least 1 hour, ideally overnight in the fridge.
Rinse the basmati rice until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes, then drain.
Heat the ghee in a heavy pot and add the bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon and star anise; let them sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the fried onions back in with the marinated chicken and saute over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Cover and cook on low heat for 12-15 minutes until the chicken is just cooked through, then spread it in an even layer at the bottom of the pot.
Meanwhile, boil the soaked rice in plenty of salted water for 5-6 minutes until it is about 70% cooked — still firm at the core — then drain.
Spread the part-cooked rice over the chicken, scatter the mint leaves and drizzle over the saffron milk.
Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid, sealing the edge with a strip of dough or foil if it isn't airtight, and cook on the lowest possible heat for 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the pot rest, still sealed, for 10 minutes before opening.
Fluff gently from the bottom up so the chicken and rice mix in layers, and serve with raita.
tips: Par-boiling the rice to just 70% is the key step — it finishes cooking in the sealed pot on the chicken's steam and stays separate instead of turning mushy.
Resting the sealed pot off the heat for 10 minutes lets the layers settle before you open it.
recipes.kidNote: Set aside a portion of the marinated chicken without the chilli powder before it goes into the pot, and layer it separately (or in a small foil packet inside the same pot) so the kids get the whole-spice aroma of the biryani without the heat — serve with plain yogurt on the side to cool any stray heat from the rice near the main chicken layer.
recipes.nutritionNote: A filling one-pot meal with protein from the chicken and carbohydrates from the rice, but the ghee and fried onions add up — serve with a cooling cucumber raita rather than extra fried sides to keep the meal balanced.

fil.description: Marinated na manok na inilayer with part-cooked basmati at dum-steamed sa sealed lid — heavily spiced with whole garam masala pero moderate lang ang chilli warmth, special-occasion na one-pot rice dish.
ingredients: aged basmati rice, banlawan at naibabad for 30 minutes
sibuyas, hiniwa ng manipis, pinriton hanggang golden
warm milk na may pinch ng saffron
steps: Ihalo ang manok sa yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, garam masala at lemon juice; i-marinate for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight sa ref.
Banlawan ang basmati rice hanggang malinaw ang tubig at i-soak for 30 minutes, tapos i-drain.
Painitin ang ghee sa heavy pot at ilagay ang bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon at star anise; hayaang mag-sizzle for 30 seconds hanggang bumango.
Ibalik ang fried onions kasama ang na-marinate na manok at igisa sa medium heat for 5 minutes.
Takpan at lutuin sa low heat for 12-15 minutes hanggang ma-cook through ang manok, tapos ikalat nang pantay sa ilalim ng pot.
Samantala, pakuluan ang na-soak na rice sa maraming salted water for 5-6 minutes hanggang mga 70% luto lang — matigas pa rin sa core — tapos i-drain.
Ikalat ang part-cooked rice sa ibabaw ng manok, budburan ng mint leaves at patakan ng saffron milk.
Takpan ang pot ng tight-fitting lid, selyuhan ang gilid ng strip ng dough o foil kung hindi airtight, at lutuin sa pinakamababang apoy for 20 minutes.
Patayin ang apoy at hayaang magpahinga ang pot, sealed pa rin, for 10 minutes bago buksan.
I-fluff nang mahinay mula sa ilalim pataas para maghalo ang manok at rice sa layers, at ihain with raita.
tips: Ang par-boiling ng rice hanggang 70% lang ang key step — natatapos itong maluto sa sealed pot gamit ang steam ng manok at nananatiling separate sa halip na maging mushy.
Ang pagpapahinga ng sealed pot off the heat for 10 minutes ang nagpapaayos sa layers bago ito buksan.
fil.kidNote: Ikuha muna ang bahagi ng na-marinate na manok na walang chilli powder bago ito ilagay sa pot, at ilayer nang hiwalay (o sa maliit na foil packet sa loob ng parehong pot) para maranasan ng mga bata ang whole-spice aroma ng biryani na walang init — ihain with plain yogurt sa tabi para pumalamig kung may stray na init mula sa rice malapit sa main chicken layer.
fil.nutritionNote: Isang filling na one-pot meal na may protein mula sa manok at carbs mula sa rice, pero dumadami ang ghee at fried onions — ihain with cooling cucumber raita sa halip na dagdag na fried sides para mapanatiling balanced ang meal.

recipes.title: Chicken Chettinad
recipes.description: Chicken simmered in a coarse, freshly roasted masala of coriander, fennel, star anise and dried red chillies — genuinely spicy-hot from the Chettinad region of Tamil Nadu, not just heavily spiced, with a deep roasted aroma.

ingredients.note: reduce to 2 for a milder batch

steps: Dry roast the coriander seeds, dried red chillies, cumin, fennel, peppercorns, cinnamon, cloves and star anise in a pan over low heat for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Add the grated coconut to the same pan and roast a further 1-2 minutes until it turns light golden, then cool and grind everything to a coarse paste with a splash of water.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan, add the curry leaves and onion, and cook over medium heat until the onion turns golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and saute for a minute until the raw smell disappears.
Add the chicken and sear on medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes until it changes colour on all sides.
Lower the heat, add the ground masala paste and turmeric, and cook, stirring often, for 5-6 minutes until the oil starts to separate — this roasted masala catches easily, so keep the heat low.
Add the tomato and salt, cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Uncover and simmer a few minutes more to thicken the gravy to a coating consistency, then finish with coriander leaves.
tips: Roast the whole spices and coconut low and slow — pushed too far they turn bitter instead of nutty.
Cook the ground masala on low heat until the oil visibly separates; that's the sign the raw spice taste is gone.
recipes.kidNote: Halve the dried red chillies (or drop to two) in the batch you'll serve the kids and skip any extra pepper, then finish their bowls with a spoonful of coconut milk or yogurt stirred through — the roasted coriander, fennel and cinnamon still carry the Chettinad flavour without the heat.
recipes.nutritionNote: A good source of lean protein from the chicken; the roasted-spice masala uses less added fat than a cream-based curry, so it pairs well with plain rice without tipping the meal too rich.

fil.description: Manok na ni-simmer sa coarse at freshly roasted masala ng coriander, fennel, star anise at dried red chillies — talagang spicy-hot mula sa Chettinad region ng Tamil Nadu, hindi lang heavily spiced, na may malalim na roasted aroma.
steps: I-dry roast ang coriander seeds, dried red chillies, cumin, fennel, peppercorns, cinnamon, cloves at star anise sa pan sa low heat for 2-3 minutes hanggang bumango at medyo dumilim.
Idagdag ang grated coconut sa parehong pan at i-roast pa for 1-2 minutes hanggang mag-light golden, tapos palamigin at gilingin lahat into coarse paste with splash of water.
Painitin ang oil sa heavy pan, idagdag ang curry leaves at onion, at lutuin sa medium heat hanggang mag-golden ang onion.
Idagdag ang ginger-garlic paste at igisa for a minute hanggang mawala ang raw smell.
Idagdag ang manok at i-sear sa medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes hanggang magbago ng kulay all sides.

Hinaan ang apoy, idagdag ang ground masala paste at turmeric, at lutuin, haluin nang madalas, for 5-6 minutes hanggang magsimulang humiwalay ang oil — mabilis masunog itong roasted masala, kaya panatilihing mahinay ang apoy.
Idagdag ang kamatis at asin, takpan at i-simmer for 15-18 minutes hanggang lumambot ang manok.
Buksan at i-simmer pa ng ilang minuto para lumapot ang gravy to coating consistency, tapos finish with coriander leaves.
tips: I-roast ang whole spices at coconut nang mahinay — kapag sobrang tinulak, mapapait ito instead na maging nutty.
Lutuin ang ground masala sa low heat hanggang halatang humiwalay ang oil; yun ang sign na wala nang raw spice taste.
fil.kidNote: Bawasan ng kalahati ang dried red chillies (o dalawa na lang) sa batch para sa mga bata at wag nang magdagdag ng extra pepper, tapos lagyan ang mangkok nila ng kutsarang coconut milk o yogurt na hinalo — nandiyan pa rin ang roasted coriander, fennel at cinnamon para dalhin ang Chettinad flavor without the heat.
fil.nutritionNote: Magandang source ng lean protein ang manok; mas kaunti ang added fat ng roasted-spice masala kumpara sa cream-based curry, kaya bagay ito sa plain rice without tipping the meal too rich.

recipes.title: Dal Tadka
recipes.description: Split pigeon pea lentils simmered soft and finished with a sizzling ghee tempering of garlic, cumin and dried red chilli — the everyday, mildly warm lentil dal that anchors a home thali.
steps: Pressure-cook the dal with the onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger, turmeric and 3 cups water for 8-10 minutes until the lentils are soft and mushy.
Once the pressure releases, whisk the dal smooth, adjust the consistency with hot water, and stir in the garam masala and salt; simmer 5 minutes.
For the tadka, heat the ghee in a small pan over medium heat and add the cumin seeds; let them sizzle until they turn golden.
Add the chopped garlic and dried red chillies and fry until the garlic turns light brown and the chillies darken slightly — do not let the garlic burn.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the Kashmiri chilli powder so it blooms in the residual heat rather than scorching.
Pour the whole sizzling tadka over the simmering dal and stir through, or let it float on top for the table.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice or roti.
tips: Whisk the dal well before adding the tadka — a lumpy dal never feels 'restaurant style'.
The garlic in the tadka should turn honey-brown, not deep brown; it turns bitter past that point.
recipes.nutritionNote: An excellent plant protein and fibre source when paired with rice for a complete amino acid profile; light on fat except for the ghee tempering, which can be halved without losing much flavour.

fil.description: Split pigeon pea lentils na sinimmer hanggang lumambot at tinapusan ng sizzling ghee tempering ng bawang, cumin at dried red chilli — ang everyday, mildly warm na lentil dal na anchor ng home thali.
steps: Pressure-cook ang dal kasama ang sibuyas, kamatis, green chilli, luya, turmeric at 3 cups water for 8-10 minutes hanggang lumambot at maging mushy ang lentils.
Pagkalabas ng pressure, i-whisk ang dal hanggang smooth, i-adjust ang consistency ng hot water, at ihalo ang garam masala at asin; i-simmer for 5 minutes.
Para sa tadka, painitin ang ghee sa maliit na pan sa medium heat at ilagay ang cumin seeds; hayaang mag-sizzle hanggang golden.
Idagdag ang tinadtad na bawang at dried red chillies at iprito hanggang light brown ang bawang at medyo dumilim ang chillies — huwag hayaang masunog ang bawang.
Alisin ang pan sa apoy tapos ihalo ang Kashmiri chilli powder para mag-bloom sa residual heat sa halip na masunog.
Ibuhos ang buong sizzling tadka sa simmering dal at haluin, o hayaang lumutang sa ibabaw para sa table.
Garnish ng wansoy leaves at ihain mainit with rice o roti.
tips: I-whisk nang maayos ang dal bago idagdag ang tadka — hindi kailanman 'restaurant style' ang lumpy dal.
Dapat honey-brown lang ang bawang sa tadka, hindi deep brown; napapait ito lampas doon.
fil.nutritionNote: Magandang plant protein at fibre source kapag isinabay sa rice para sa complete amino acid profile; mababa sa fat maliban sa ghee tempering, na puwedeng i-half kahit konti lang mawala sa lasa.

recipes.title: Egg Curry
recipes.description: Boiled eggs pan-fried until blistered, then simmered in a robust dhaba-style onion-tomato masala — genuinely spicy-hot, not just heavily spiced, and a quick protein-packed curry for meatless days.
steps: Prick the boiled, peeled eggs a few times with a fork so they don't burst while frying.
Heat the ghee in a nonstick pan and shallow-fry the eggs, turning, until golden and blistered all over; set aside.
Heat the oil in the same pan and add the bay leaf, cinnamon and cardamom; let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook over medium heat, stirring often, until deep golden brown.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and saute for a minute until the raw smell disappears.
Add the tomato and cook until soft and pulpy, then lower the heat and stir in the chilli powder, turmeric and half the garam masala with a splash of water so they bloom without catching.
Cook until the oil separates at the edges, about 3-4 minutes, then add the water and salt and bring to a simmer.
Slide the fried eggs into the gravy, cover and simmer 5 minutes so they soak up the masala.
Sprinkle over the remaining garam masala and coriander leaves before serving.
tips: Frying the boiled eggs first is what gives dhaba-style egg curry its blistered skin that grabs onto the gravy.
Cook the masala until the oil visibly separates — that's the cue the tomatoes are fully cooked down.
recipes.kidNote: Halve the chilli powder and skip any extra green chilli in the batch of gravy you'll serve the kids, and cut their eggs in half so the masala coats more surface with less punch per bite — the whole garam masala (cinnamon, cardamom, bay leaf) still gives it that home-style aroma.
recipes.nutritionNote: Eggs are a complete protein and a useful stand-in on days without meat or fish; the dish is moderate in fat from the frying step, so pair it with a lighter dal or plain rice rather than another rich curry.

fil.description: Boiled na itlog na pan-fried hanggang blistered, tapos sinimmer sa robust dhaba-style onion-tomato masala — tunay na maanghang, hindi lang heavily spiced, at mabilis na protein-packed curry para sa mga araw na walang karne.
steps: Tusukin ang luto at balat nang itlog ng ilang beses gamit ang tinidor para hindi ito sumabog habang pinipriton.
Painitin ang ghee sa nonstick pan at shallow-fry ang itlog, ibaligtad, hanggang golden at blistered sa lahat ng gilid; itabi muna.
Painitin ang oil sa parehong pan at ilagay ang bay leaf, cinnamon at cardamom; hayaang mag-sizzle for 30 seconds.
Idagdag ang sibuyas at lutuin sa medium heat, haluin often, hanggang deep golden brown.
Idagdag ang ginger-garlic paste at igisa for a minute hanggang mawala ang raw smell.

Idagdag ang kamatis at lutuin hanggang lumambot at maging pulpy, tapos hinaan ang apoy at ihalo ang chilli powder, turmeric at kalahati ng garam masala with a splash of water para mag-bloom na hindi masusunog.
Lutuin hanggang mag-separate ang oil sa gilid, mga 3-4 minutes, tapos idagdag ang tubig at asin at pakuluin.
Idulas ang fried eggs papasok sa gravy, takpan at i-simmer for 5 minutes para maabsorb nila ang masala.
Budburan ng natitirang garam masala at wansoy leaves bago ihain.
tips: Ang pagprito muna ng boiled eggs ang nagbibigay sa dhaba-style egg curry ng blistered skin na kumakapit sa gravy.
Lutuin ang masala hanggang makitang nag-separate ang oil — yun ang cue na lutong-luto na ang kamatis.
fil.kidNote: Bawasan ng kalahati ang chilli powder at laktawan ang extra green chilli sa batch ng gravy na ihahain sa mga bata, at hatiin sa dalawa ang itlog nila para mas madaming surface ang nababalutan ng masala pero mas kaunti ang tama per bite — mararamdaman pa rin ang whole garam masala (cinnamon, cardamom, bay leaf) para sa home-style aroma.
fil.nutritionNote: Ang itlog ay complete protein at magandang panghalili sa araw na walang karne o isda; moderate lang sa fat ang dish dahil sa frying step, kaya isabay sa mas light na dal o plain rice sa halip na isa pang mayamang curry.

recipes.title: Keema Matar
recipes.description: Mutton or beef mince bhuna-fried with whole garam masala, onions and tomatoes, then simmered with peas — warmly spiced with a real but manageable kick, not fiery, ready in half an hour.

ingredients.note: traditionally mutton; beef mince works well too

steps: Heat the ghee in a heavy pan and add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom; fry for 30 seconds until they sizzle and smell fragrant.
Add the onion and cook over medium heat, stirring often, until deep golden brown, about 8 minutes.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilli and saute for a minute until the raw smell disappears.
Add the mince and break it up with the back of the spoon; cook on medium heat for 4-5 minutes until it changes colour.
Lower the heat and stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and half the garam masala with a splash of water so the powders bloom without catching.
Add the tomato puree and salt, cover and cook on low heat for 10 minutes until the mince is tender and the oil starts to separate.
Stir in the peas and simmer uncovered for 6-8 minutes until the peas are cooked and the curry is semi-dry.
Finish with the remaining garam masala, mint and coriander, then serve hot.
tips: Breaking up the mince fully before it browns keeps it from clumping into hard balls.
For a drier keema to stuff into parathas, simmer a few extra minutes uncovered at the end.
recipes.kidNote: Spoon out the kids' portion before the green chilli and second hit of garam masala go in, and stir a spoonful of yogurt or a pinch of sugar through it to round out the spice — the whole garam masala aromatics stay in for flavour without heat.
recipes.nutritionNote: A good source of iron and protein from the mince, though it carries meat's saturated fat — pair with a fibre-rich side like a cucumber-tomato salad or dal and go easy on the ghee if serving it often.

fil.description: Mutton o beef mince na bhuna-fried with whole garam masala, sibuyas at kamatis, tapos sinimmer with peas — may tunay na kick pero manageable, hindi apoy-apoy, ready in half an hour.
steps: Painitin ang ghee sa heavy pan at ilagay ang bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves at cardamom; iprito for 30 seconds hanggang mag-sizzle at bumango.
Idagdag ang sibuyas at lutuin sa medium heat, haluin often, hanggang deep golden brown, mga 8 minutes.
Idagdag ang ginger-garlic paste at green chilli at igisa for a minute hanggang mawala ang raw smell.
Idagdag ang mince at durugin gamit ang likod ng kutsara; lutuin sa medium heat for 4-5 minutes hanggang magbago ang kulay.
Hinaan ang apoy tapos ihalo ang turmeric, chilli powder at kalahati ng garam masala with a splash of water para mag-bloom ang powders na hindi masusunog.
Idagdag ang tomato puree at asin, takpan at lutuin sa low heat for 10 minutes hanggang lumambot ang mince at magsimulang mag-separate ang oil.
Ihalo ang peas at i-simmer uncovered for 6-8 minutes hanggang maluto ang peas at maging semi-dry ang curry.
Tapusin ng natitirang garam masala, mint at wansoy, tapos ihain mainit.
tips: Ang pagdurog ng mince nang husto bago ito mag-brown ang nagpapaiwas sa pagiging clumpy nito na parang matigas na bola.
Para sa mas tuyong keema na isstuff sa paratha, i-simmer ng ilang extra minutes uncovered sa dulo.
fil.kidNote: Ikuha muna ang share ng mga bata bago ilagay ang green chilli at second hit ng garam masala, tapos haluan ng kutsarang yogurt o kaunting asukal para mabawasan ang anghang — mananatili ang whole garam masala aromatics para sa lasa na walang init.
fil.nutritionNote: Magandang source ng iron at protein galing sa mince, pero may saturated fat rin dahil karne — isabay sa fibre-rich na side gaya ng cucumber-tomato salad o dal at bawasan ang ghee kung madalas itong iniluluto.

recipes.title: Kerala Fish Curry
recipes.description: Firm fish steaks simmered in a tangy coconut-milk gravy soured with kudampuli and finished with a mustard-curry-leaf tempering — coastal Kerala's everyday curry, properly spicy-hot, not just heavily spiced.

ingredients.item: firm fish steaks (kingfish or pomfret), cut into pieces

steps: Soak the kudampuli pieces in a quarter cup of hot water for 10 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a clay pot or wide pan and add the crushed ginger, garlic, shallots and green chillies; saute for 6-7 minutes until softened.
Add the crushed tomato and cook for 4-5 minutes until it breaks down.
Lower the heat and stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder with a splash of water so the ground spices bloom without burning.
Add the soaked kudampuli with its soaking water, half the coconut milk and enough water to cover; bring to a boil and simmer 3-4 minutes.
Slide the fish pieces into the gravy, cover and cook 10 minutes without stirring hard, just swirling the pot so the fish doesn't break.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, season with salt and simmer uncovered 5 minutes until the fish is just cooked through.
For the tempering, heat the coconut oil in a small pan, add the mustard seeds and let them sputter, then add the dried red chillies and curry leaves and fry until crisp.
Pour the sizzling tempering over the curry and let it rest 10 minutes before serving — this curry tastes even better the next day.
tips: This curry actually improves overnight in the fridge as the tamarind and chilli mellow into the fish — traditionally made a day ahead.
Swirl the pot instead of stirring with a spoon once the fish goes in, or the pieces will break apart.
recipes.kidNote: The chilli and kudampuli make this a proper spicy-hot curry, not just a heavily spiced one, so it isn't a safe one to serve straight to the kids. Set aside a portion of fish before the chilli powder goes in, poach it separately in a little of the coconut milk with just turmeric and salt, and spoon a little of that mellow coconut gravy over their rice instead of the full curry.
recipes.nutritionNote: An excellent source of omega-3s and lean protein from the fish, though the coconut milk adds saturated fat — balance the meal with plain rice and a cucumber salad rather than another coconut-based side.

fil.description: Firm na fish steaks na sinimmer sa tangy coconut-milk gravy na inasiman ng kudampuli at tinapusan ng mustard-curry-leaf tempering — everyday curry ng coastal Kerala, tunay na maanghang, hindi lang heavily spiced.
ingredients: firm fish steaks (kingfish o pomfret), hiniwa
steps: I-soak ang kudampuli pieces sa quarter cup na hot water for 10 minutes.
Painitin ang coconut oil sa clay pot o wide pan at ilagay ang dinurog na luya, bawang, shallots at green chillies; igisa for 6-7 minutes hanggang lumambot.
Idagdag ang dinurog na kamatis at lutuin for 4-5 minutes hanggang mawasak.
Hinaan ang apoy tapos ihalo ang turmeric, chilli powder at coriander powder with a splash of water para mag-bloom ang powdered spices na hindi masusunog.
Idagdag ang na-soak na kudampuli kasama ang soaking water nito, kalahati ng coconut milk at sapat na tubig para matakpan; pakuluin at i-simmer for 3-4 minutes.
Idulas ang isda papasok sa gravy, takpan at lutuin for 10 minutes nang hindi masyadong hinahalo, i-swirl lang ang pot para hindi madurog ang isda.
Ibuhos ang natitirang coconut milk, timplahan ng asin at i-simmer uncovered for 5 minutes hanggang ma-cook through ang isda.
Para sa tempering, painitin ang coconut oil sa maliit na pan, ilagay ang mustard seeds at hayaang mag-sputter, tapos idagdag ang dried red chillies at curry leaves at iprito hanggang crisp.
Ibuhos ang sizzling tempering sa curry at hayaang magpahinga for 10 minutes bago ihain — mas masarap talaga ang curry na ito sa susunod na araw.
tips: Umiimprove talaga ang curry na ito overnight sa ref habang naghahalo ang tamarind at chilli sa isda — traditionally ginagawa ito isang araw bago ihain.
I-swirl ang pot sa halip na haluin ng kutsara kapag nasa loob na ang isda, para hindi madurog ang mga piraso.
fil.kidNote: Dahil sa chilli at kudampuli, tunay itong maanghang na curry, hindi lang heavily spiced, kaya hindi ito safe na ihain nang diretso sa mga bata. Ikuha muna ang bahagi ng isda bago ilagay ang chilli powder, i-poach ito nang hiwalay sa konting coconut milk na may turmeric at asin lang, tapos ibuhos ang kaunting mellow coconut gravy sa rice nila sa halip na full curry.
fil.nutritionNote: Magandang source ng omega-3 at lean protein galing sa isda, pero may dagdag saturated fat ang coconut milk — balansehin ang meal ng plain rice at cucumber salad sa halip na isa pang coconut-based side.

recipes.title: Lemon Rice
recipes.description: Cooled cooked rice tossed through a crackling mustard-seed, peanut and curry-leaf tempering with a generous squeeze of lemon — a mildly tangy South Indian rice dish that travels well in a lunchbox.
steps: Cook the rice ahead of time and spread it out to cool completely, fluffing the grains apart so they stay separate rather than clumping.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the peanuts until crunchy; remove and set aside.
In the same oil, add the mustard seeds; once they splutter, add the urad dal and chana dal and fry until golden.
Add the dried red chilli, green chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida, and fry for a few seconds.
Add the turmeric powder and stir through.
Add the cooled rice and salt, and toss gently with a wide spatula to coat evenly without mashing the grains.
Take the pan off the heat, squeeze in the lemon juice, and toss again, tasting and adjusting salt or lemon as needed.
Garnish with the roasted peanuts and coriander leaves before serving.
tips: Day-old, fully cooled rice works best — warm rice turns gummy the moment the lemon juice hits it.
Add the lemon juice off the heat; direct heat mutes its fresh tang.
recipes.nutritionNote: A light carbohydrate base with a modest lift of protein and healthy fat from the peanuts; it's a plain rice dish on its own, so serve alongside a dal, poriyal or curry rather than as the whole meal.

fil.description: Lutong rice na pinalamig, hinalo sa crackling mustard-seed, peanut at curry-leaf tempering na may generous squeeze ng lemon — mildly tangy na South Indian rice dish na okay dalhin sa lunchbox.
steps: Lutuin ang rice ahead of time at ikalat para lumamig nang tuluyan, i-fluff ang mga butil para hindi magdikit-dikit.
Painitin ang oil sa pan at i-fry ang peanuts hanggang crunchy; alisin at itabi.
Sa parehong oil, idagdag ang mustard seeds; once mag-splutter, idagdag ang urad dal at chana dal at i-fry hanggang golden.
Idagdag ang dried red chilli, green chilli, curry leaves at asafoetida, at i-fry for a few seconds.
Idagdag ang turmeric powder at ihalo.
Idagdag ang cooled rice at asin, at i-toss nang bahagya gamit ang wide spatula para mabalutan evenly without madurog ang mga butil.
Alisin ang pan sa apoy, pigain ang lemon juice, at i-toss ulit, tikman at ayusin ang asin o lemon kung kailangan.
Garnishan ng roasted peanuts at coriander leaves bago ihain.
tips: Mas maganda ang day-old, fully cooled rice — magiging gummy ang warm rice the moment tamaan ito ng lemon juice.
Idagdag ang lemon juice off the heat; nawawala ang fresh tang nito sa direct heat.
fil.nutritionNote: Light na carbohydrate base with modest na boost ng protein at healthy fat mula sa peanuts; plain rice dish lang ito, kaya ihain kasama ng dal, poriyal o curry kesa buong meal na mag-isa.

recipes.title: Matar Paneer
recipes.description: Paneer cubes and green peas simmered in a dhaba-style onion-tomato gravy built from separately fried onions and boiled tomatoes — mildly warm, quick weeknight comfort food without any cream or cashews.
steps: Boil the tomato in a little water for 5-6 minutes until soft, then cool and blend to a smooth puree.
Shallow-fry the onion in a tablespoon of the oil until deep golden, then cool and grind to a smooth paste.
Heat the remaining oil in a pan and add the cumin seeds and bay leaf; let them sizzle until fragrant.
Add the onion paste and cook over medium heat, stirring, for 3-4 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and saute for a minute until the raw smell disappears.
Lower the heat and stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder with a splash of water so the powders bloom without catching.
Add the tomato puree and cook, stirring often, for 7-8 minutes until it thickens and the oil separates again.
Add enough water to loosen the gravy, then add the peas and simmer 6-8 minutes until tender.
Add the paneer, garam masala, kasuri methi and salt; simmer 2-3 minutes just to warm the paneer through, then finish with coriander leaves.
tips: Grinding the fried onion and boiled tomato separately, instead of cooking them together raw, is what gives this gravy its dhaba-style depth.
Add the paneer right at the end and don't let it boil hard, or it turns rubbery.
recipes.nutritionNote: Paneer and peas together bring protein, calcium and fibre, and this version skips cream entirely, keeping the fat mostly to the tempering oil — a good vegetarian main to pair with a lighter dal-and-rice night.

fil.description: Paneer cubes at green peas na ni-simmer sa dhaba-style onion-tomato gravy mula sa hiwalay na pinrito na onions at pinakuluang tomatoes — mildly warm at mabilis na weeknight comfort food na walang cream o cashews.
steps: Pakuluin ang kamatis sa kaunting tubig for 5-6 minutes hanggang lumambot, tapos palamigin at i-blend into smooth puree.
I-shallow-fry ang onion sa tablespoon ng oil hanggang deep golden, tapos palamigin at gilingin into smooth paste.
Painitin ang natitirang oil sa pan at idagdag ang cumin seeds at bay leaf; hayaang mag-sizzle hanggang bumango.
Idagdag ang onion paste at lutuin sa medium heat, haluin, for 3-4 minutes hanggang humiwalay ang oil.
Idagdag ang ginger-garlic paste at igisa for a minute hanggang mawala ang raw smell.
Hinaan ang apoy at ihalo ang turmeric, chilli powder at coriander powder with splash of water para mag-bloom ang powders without masunog.
Idagdag ang tomato puree at lutuin, haluin nang madalas, for 7-8 minutes hanggang lumapot at humiwalay ulit ang oil.
Magdagdag ng sapat na tubig para lumusaw ang gravy, tapos idagdag ang peas at i-simmer for 6-8 minutes hanggang lumambot.
Idagdag ang paneer, garam masala, kasuri methi at asin; i-simmer for 2-3 minutes lang para uminit ang paneer, tapos finish with coriander leaves.
tips: Ang paggiling ng fried onion at boiled tomato nang hiwalay, kesa lutuin sabay nang raw, ang nagbibigay dito ng dhaba-style depth.
Idagdag ang paneer right at the end at wag hayaang pakuluan nang malakas, kundi magiging rubbery ito.
fil.nutritionNote: Nagdadala ang paneer at peas ng protein, calcium at fibre nang magkasama, at nilaktawan ng version na ito ang cream, kaya nanatili ang taba mostly sa tempering oil lang — magandang vegetarian main to pair with lighter dal-and-rice night.

recipes.title: Palak Paneer
recipes.description: Fresh spinach blanched, shocked and pureed into a silky green gravy, tempered with cumin and simmered with soft paneer and a swirl of cream — mild enough for the whole table to share.
steps: Blanch the spinach in boiling salted water for 1 minute, then plunge immediately into ice water to stop the cooking and keep the colour bright.
Drain the spinach and blend it with the green chilli, ginger and garlic to a smooth puree; set aside.
Heat the ghee in a pan and add the cumin seeds and bay leaf; let them sizzle until the cumin turns golden.
Add the onion and saute until soft and light golden.
Add the chopped garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then add the tomato and cook until it softens and the oil starts to separate.
Lower the heat and stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and garam masala with a splash of water so they bloom without burning.
Add the spinach puree and a little water to loosen it, then simmer 6-7 minutes until the raw spinach smell is gone.
Add the paneer cubes, simmer 2 minutes to warm through, then take off the heat and stir in the cream and kasuri methi.
tips: Shocking the spinach in ice water immediately after blanching is what keeps palak paneer bright green instead of khaki.
Add the paneer right at the end — boiling it too long turns it rubbery.
recipes.nutritionNote: Spinach brings iron and folate and paneer brings calcium and protein, making this one of the more nutrient-dense vegetarian mains here — go light on the cream if it's a frequent weeknight dish.

fil.description: Fresh spinach na blanched, shocked at pinureed hanggang maging silky green gravy, tinempera ng cumin at sinimmer with soft paneer at swirl ng cream — mild na kayang ibahagi ng buong table.
steps: I-blanch ang spinach sa boiling salted water for 1 minute, tapos isawsaw kaagad sa ice water para mahinto ang pagluto at manatiling bright ang kulay.
I-drain ang spinach at i-blend kasama ang green chilli, luya at bawang hanggang smooth puree; itabi muna.
Painitin ang ghee sa pan at ilagay ang cumin seeds at bay leaf; hayaang mag-sizzle hanggang golden ang cumin.
Idagdag ang sibuyas at igisa hanggang malambot at light golden.
Idagdag ang tinadtad na bawang at lutuin for 30 seconds, tapos idagdag ang kamatis at lutuin hanggang lumambot at magsimulang mag-separate ang oil.
Hinaan ang apoy tapos ihalo ang turmeric, chilli powder at garam masala with a splash of water para mag-bloom na hindi masusunog.
Idagdag ang spinach puree at kaunting tubig para maluwagan, tapos i-simmer for 6-7 minutes hanggang mawala ang raw spinach smell.
Idagdag ang paneer cubes, i-simmer for 2 minutes hanggang uminit, tapos alisin sa apoy at ihalo ang cream at kasuri methi.
tips: Ang pag-shock ng spinach sa ice water kaagad pagkatapos i-blanch ang nagpapanatili sa palak paneer na bright green sa halip na khaki.
Idagdag ang paneer sa pinakadulo lang — nagiging rubbery ito kung masyadong matagal pinakuluan.
fil.nutritionNote: Ang spinach ay may iron at folate at ang paneer naman ay may calcium at protein, kaya isa ito sa pinaka nutrient-dense na vegetarian main dito — bawasan ang cream kung madalas itong ihain sa weeknight.

recipes.title: Poha
recipes.description: Flattened rice rinsed soft and tossed through a mustard-seed tempering with potatoes, peanuts and curry leaves — Maharashtra's gently spiced, favourite quick breakfast, ready before the chai brews.
steps: Place the poha in a colander and rinse gently under running water twice, just until softened — do not soak or it will turn mushy.
Sprinkle the turmeric, sugar and salt over the rinsed poha, toss gently to coat, and set aside.
Dry-roast the peanuts in a pan until crunchy, then set aside.
Heat the oil in the same pan and shallow-fry the potato cubes until golden and just tender; remove and set aside.
Add the mustard seeds to the hot oil; once they splutter, add the cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add the onion and saute until translucent, then add the curry leaves, green chilli and roasted peanuts.
Add the softened poha and the fried potatoes, and toss gently over low heat until everything is warmed through and evenly coated.
Cover and let it steam for 2 minutes on low heat, then garnish with coriander leaves and serve with lemon wedges.
tips: Rinse, don't soak, the poha — a quick rinse under running water softens the flakes without turning them into paste.
Toss gently with a wide spatula rather than stirring hard; poha flakes break easily.
recipes.nutritionNote: Flattened rice is light and easy to digest, and the peanuts and potato round it out with some protein and energy — a good low-oil breakfast option, just watch the peanuts if there are nut allergies in the mix.

fil.description: Flattened rice na binanlawan hanggang malambot at hinalo sa mustard-seed tempering with patatas, mani at curry leaves — ang gently spiced, paboritong quick breakfast ng Maharashtra, ready pa bago maluto ang chai.
ingredients: patatas, balatan at cubed nang maliit
steps: Ilagay ang poha sa colander at banlawan nang bahagya sa running water twice, hanggang lumambot lang — huwag ibabad para hindi maging mushy.
Budburan ng turmeric, asukal at asin ang binanlawang poha, haluin nang bahagya para mabalutan, at itabi muna.
Dry-roast ang mani sa pan hanggang crunchy, tapos itabi muna.
Painitin ang oil sa parehong pan at shallow-fry ang patatas hanggang golden at just tender; alisin at itabi muna.
Idagdag ang mustard seeds sa mainit na oil; kapag nag-splutter na, idagdag ang cumin seeds at hayaang mag-crackle.
Idagdag ang sibuyas at igisa hanggang translucent, tapos idagdag ang curry leaves, green chilli at roasted na mani.
Idagdag ang malambot na poha at fried potatoes, at haluin nang bahagya sa low heat hanggang uminit at pantay ang pagkabalot ng lahat.
Takpan at hayaang mag-steam for 2 minutes sa low heat, tapos garnish ng wansoy leaves at ihain with lemon wedges.
tips: Banlawan lang, huwag ibabad, ang poha — ang mabilis na banlaw sa running water ang lumalambot sa flakes na hindi ito naging paste.
Haluin nang bahagya gamit ang wide spatula sa halip na haluing malakas; madaling madurog ang poha flakes.
fil.nutritionNote: Magaan at madaling matunaw ang flattened rice, at ang mani at patatas ang nagbibigay ng konting protein at energy — magandang low-oil breakfast option, bantayan lang ang mani kung may nut allergy sa bahay.

recipes.title: Prawn Masala
recipes.description: Prawns simmered in a ground coconut-and-whole-spice masala with onion and tomato — a coastal Konkan-style curry, tangy and properly spicy-hot, distinct from a coconut-milk fish curry since the coconut here is ground into the base, not poured in.

ingredients.note: reduce to 2 for a milder batch

steps: Toss the prawns with turmeric, salt and lemon juice, and set aside to marinate for 15 minutes.

Dry roast the coriander seeds, dried red chillies, cumin, fennel, cinnamon and cloves in a pan for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then cool and grind with the grated coconut and a little water to a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a pan and add the curry leaves and onion; cook over medium heat until golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and saute for a minute until the raw smell disappears.
Add the ground coconut masala paste and cook, stirring often, over low heat for 5-6 minutes until the oil starts to separate.
Add the tomato and cook until it softens and breaks down.
Add enough water to bring the gravy to a curry consistency, bring to a simmer, and cook 5 minutes for the flavours to meld.
Slide in the marinated prawns and cook for 4-5 minutes, just until they turn pink and curl — do not overcook or they turn rubbery.
Sprinkle over the garam masala and finish with coriander leaves.
tips: Prawns cook fast — pull them off the heat the moment they curl into a tight 'C' shape, or they turn tough.
Roasting the whole spices before grinding is what separates this from a plain coconut-milk curry; don't skip it.
recipes.kidNote: The ground dried-chilli masala makes this a proper spicy-hot curry rather than a mild one, so it isn't a safe one to serve straight to the kids. Set aside a few plain-poached prawns (simmered separately in a little of the tomato-onion base with just turmeric and salt) and spoon a little of that milder gravy over their rice instead.
recipes.nutritionNote: Prawns are a lean, high-protein seafood option; ground coconut adds some saturated fat but far less than a coconut-milk-based curry, so this pairs well with plain rice and a vegetable side.

fil.description: Prawns na ni-simmer sa ground coconut-and-whole-spice masala na may onion at kamatis — coastal Konkan-style curry, tangy at talagang spicy-hot, iba sa coconut-milk fish curry kasi dito, ginigiling ang coconut papunta sa base, hindi lang binubuhos.
ingredients: prawns, binalatan at inalisan ng ugat
steps: Ihalo ang prawns sa turmeric, asin at lemon juice, at itabi para mag-marinate for 15 minutes.

I-dry roast ang coriander seeds, dried red chillies, cumin, fennel, cinnamon at cloves sa pan for 1-2 minutes hanggang bumango, tapos palamigin at gilingin with grated coconut at kaunting tubig into smooth paste.
Painitin ang oil sa pan at idagdag ang curry leaves at onion; lutuin sa medium heat hanggang golden.
Idagdag ang ginger-garlic paste at igisa for a minute hanggang mawala ang raw smell.
Idagdag ang ground coconut masala paste at lutuin, haluin nang madalas, sa low heat for 5-6 minutes hanggang magsimulang humiwalay ang oil.
Idagdag ang kamatis at lutuin hanggang lumambot at mag-breakdown.
Magdagdag ng sapat na tubig para maging curry consistency ang gravy, pakuluin nang mahinay, at lutuin for 5 minutes para maghalo ang flavors.
Ilagay ang marinated prawns at lutuin for 4-5 minutes, hanggang mag-pink at mag-curl lang — wag i-overcook kundi magiging rubbery ito.
Budburan ng garam masala at finish with coriander leaves.
tips: Mabilis maluto ang prawns — alisin agad sa apoy the moment mag-curl sila into tight 'C' shape, kundi magiging tough ito.
Ang pag-roast ng whole spices bago gilingin ang siyang nagpapaiba nito sa plain coconut-milk curry; wag laktawan ito.
fil.kidNote: Dahil sa ground dried-chilli masala, talagang maanghang ang curry na ito kaysa mild lang, kaya hindi ito safe ipakain nang diretso sa mga bata. Maglaan ng ilang plain-poached prawns (i-simmer nang hiwalay sa kaunting tomato-onion base na may turmeric at asin lang) at ibuhos na lang ang mas mildong gravy sa rice nila instead.
fil.nutritionNote: Lean, high-protein seafood option ang prawns; nagdadagdag ng kaunting saturated fat ang ground coconut pero mas kaunti pa rin kaysa coconut-milk-based curry, kaya bagay ito sa plain rice at side ng gulay.

recipes.title: Rajma Masala
recipes.description: Red kidney beans simmered low and slow in an onion-tomato masala until the gravy turns thick and clingy — mild, homely Punjabi comfort food eaten spooned over steamed rice.

ingredients.item: dried red kidney beans (rajma), soaked overnight

steps: Drain the soaked kidney beans and pressure-cook with fresh water for 15-20 minutes until completely soft and easily mashed between fingers.
Heat the butter and oil in a pan and add the cumin seeds; let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Add the onion and cook over medium heat until deep golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the crushed garlic, ginger and green chilli and saute for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomato and cook until soft and pulpy, then lower the heat and stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder with a splash of water so they don't catch.
Cook the masala until the oil separates at the edges, about 5 minutes.
Add the cooked beans along with their cooking liquid and salt; simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
Stir in the garam masala and cream, simmer for a minute, and finish with coriander leaves.
tips: Soak the rajma for at least 8 hours or overnight — unsoaked beans stay tough even after pressure-cooking.
Mashing a spoonful of beans into the gravy is what gives rajma its signature thick, clingy texture.
recipes.nutritionNote: Kidney beans plus rice form a complete protein and are high in fibre — this is one of the most balanced meals in the rotation; just watch the added cream and butter if serving it often.

fil.description: Red kidney beans na sinimmer nang mahinay sa onion-tomato masala hanggang lumapot at kumapit ang gravy — mild at homely Punjabi comfort food na kinakain with steamed rice.
ingredients: dried red kidney beans (rajma), naibabad overnight
steps: I-drain ang naibabad na kidney beans at pressure-cook with fresh water for 15-20 minutes hanggang completely soft at madaling madurog sa pagitan ng daliri.
Painitin ang butter at oil sa pan at ilagay ang cumin seeds; hayaang mag-sizzle for a few seconds.
Idagdag ang sibuyas at lutuin sa medium heat hanggang deep golden brown, mga 8-10 minutes.
Idagdag ang dinurog na bawang, luya at green chilli at igisa for 30 seconds hanggang bumango.
Idagdag ang kamatis at lutuin hanggang lumambot at maging pulpy, tapos hinaan ang apoy at ihalo ang turmeric, chilli powder at coriander powder with a splash of water para hindi masusunog.
Lutuin ang masala hanggang mag-separate ang oil sa gilid, mga 5 minutes.
Idagdag ang lutong beans kasama ang cooking liquid nito at asin; i-simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, dinudurog ang ilang beans sa gilid ng pan para lumapot ang gravy.
Ihalo ang garam masala at cream, i-simmer for a minute, at tapusin ng wansoy leaves.
tips: I-soak ang rajma for at least 8 hours o overnight — matigas pa rin ang unsoaked beans kahit pressure-cooked na.
Ang pagdurog ng isang kutsarang beans papasok sa gravy ang nagbibigay sa rajma ng signature thick at clingy texture nito.
fil.nutritionNote: Ang kidney beans plus rice ay complete protein at mataas sa fibre — isa ito sa pinaka-balanced na meal sa rotation; bantayan lang ang cream at butter kung madalas itong ihain.

recipes.title: Rava Dosa
recipes.description: A thin, lacy, instant semolina crepe with no fermentation needed — crisp at the edges, studded with cumin and curry leaves, South India's quick-fix breakfast dosa served with coconut chutney and sambar.
steps: Whisk the semolina, rice flour, maida and salt together in a large bowl.
Add the water gradually, whisking out any lumps, until the batter is thin and watery — much runnier than a regular dosa batter.
Rest the batter for 20-30 minutes so the semolina fully absorbs the water, then stir well again before cooking.
Stir in the cumin seeds, crushed pepper, ginger, green chilli, curry leaves, coriander leaves and onion if using.
Heat a flat dosa tawa or nonstick pan over medium-high heat until a drop of batter sizzles on contact.
Stir the batter again, then pour it from a height in a circular motion from the outer edge inward, leaving natural lacy gaps — do not spread it with a ladle like a regular dosa.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until the dosa turns golden and crisp and lifts easily off the pan, 2-3 minutes.
Fold into a half-moon or quarter and serve immediately with coconut chutney and sambar; repeat with the remaining batter, stirring it each time since the flours settle.
tips: A thin, watery batter is what gives rava dosa its lacy holes — thick batter turns it into a pancake instead.
Cook these one at a time straight from the heat; unlike regular dosa, rava dosa doesn't hold well once made ahead.
recipes.nutritionNote: Lighter than a rice-and-lentil dosa since it skips fermentation, though it's still a refined-carbohydrate breakfast — round it out with a vegetable-forward sambar or coconut chutney rather than a second fried side.

fil.description: Manipis, lacy, instant semolina crepe na walang fermentation kailangan — crisp sa gilid, may cumin at curry leaves, ang mabilis na fix-breakfast dosa ng South India na iniihain with coconut chutney at sambar.
steps: Ihalo ang semolina, rice flour, maida at asin sa large bowl.
Idagdag ang tubig nang paunti-unti, alisin ang lumps, hanggang manipis at watery ang batter — mas runny pa kaysa regular na dosa batter.
Patahimikin ang batter for 20-30 minutes para ma-absorb nang tuluyan ng semolina ang tubig, tapos haluin ulit nang maigi bago lutuin.
Ihalo ang cumin seeds, crushed pepper, luya, green chilli, curry leaves, coriander leaves at onion kung gagamitin.
Painitin ang flat dosa tawa o nonstick pan sa medium-high heat hanggang mag-sizzle ang isang patak ng batter kapag nahulog.
Haluin ulit ang batter, tapos ibuhos mula sa taas in a circular motion mula sa outer edge papunta sa gitna, iwanan ang natural lacy gaps — wag i-spread gamit ang ladle tulad ng regular na dosa.
I-drizzle ng kaunting oil sa gilid at lutuin hanggang mag-golden at crisp ang dosa at maalis nang madali sa pan, 2-3 minutes.
I-fold into half-moon o quarter at ihain agad with coconut chutney at sambar; ulitin with natitirang batter, haluin ito bawat time kasi nagse-settle ang flours.
tips: Ang thin at watery na batter ang nagbibigay sa rava dosa ng lacy holes nito — pag makapal ang batter, magiging pancake na lang ito.
Lutuin ito isa-isa straight from the heat; hindi tulad ng regular na dosa, hindi maganda i-hold ang rava dosa once naluto na.
fil.nutritionNote: Mas light kaysa rice-and-lentil dosa kasi walang fermentation, pero refined-carbohydrate pa rin ang breakfast na ito — kumpletuhin with vegetable-forward na sambar o coconut chutney kesa dagdag pang fried side.

recipes.title: Rogan Josh
recipes.description: Bone-in mutton or beef braised low and slow in whisked yogurt with fennel, dry ginger powder and Kashmiri chilli for its signature deep red colour — no onion or garlic, warmly spiced rather than fiery, with a rich, clingy gravy.

ingredients.item: bone-in mutton or beef stew pieces

steps: Heat the mustard oil in a heavy pot until it just starts to smoke, then let it cool for a minute to lose its raw sharpness.
Add the bay leaf, black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves and cinnamon, and let them sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the meat and sear on high heat, turning occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until browned on all sides.
