Lower the heat and stir in the asafoetida and Kashmiri chilli powder with a splash of water so the powder blooms without scorching.
Add the whisked yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring constantly over low heat so it doesn't split, until it's fully incorporated.
Stir in the fennel powder, dry ginger powder and salt.
Add the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the meat is fork-tender and the gravy has thickened.
Uncover and simmer a few minutes more if the gravy needs reducing, then serve hot.
tips: Add the yogurt off direct high heat and stir constantly — this is the step that prevents the gravy from curdling.
Letting the smoking mustard oil cool slightly before the spices go in keeps its pungency from turning bitter.
recipes.kidNote: Use the lower end of the Kashmiri chilli powder (or halve it) for the portion you'll serve the kids — it's a mild variety used mostly for colour, but a lighter hand keeps their share properly gentle — and stir a spoonful of extra yogurt through their gravy. The whole spices stay in for aroma without any real heat.
recipes.nutritionNote: A protein- and iron-rich meat braise; the gravy relies on yogurt rather than cream for body, which keeps the saturated fat lower than a butter-based curry — pair with rice or roti and a green vegetable side.

fil.description: Mutton o beef na may buto, ni-braise nang mahinay sa whisked yogurt na may fennel, dry ginger powder at Kashmiri chilli para sa signature deep red na kulay nito — walang onion o bawang, warmly spiced kesa fiery, may rich at clingy na gravy.
ingredients: mutton o beef stew pieces, may buto
steps: Painitin ang mustard oil sa heavy pot hanggang magsimulang mag-usok, tapos palamigin for a minute para mawala ang raw sharpness.
Idagdag ang bay leaf, black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves at cinnamon, at hayaang mag-sizzle for 30 seconds hanggang bumango.
Idagdag ang karne at i-sear sa high heat, i-turn paminsan-minsan, for 8-10 minutes hanggang mag-brown all sides.
Hinaan ang apoy at ihalo ang asafoetida at Kashmiri chilli powder with splash of water para mag-bloom ang powder without masunog.
Idagdag ang whisked yogurt isang spoonful at a time, haluin nang patuloy sa low heat para hindi mag-split, hanggang ma-incorporate nang lahat.
Ihalo ang fennel powder, dry ginger powder at asin.
Idagdag ang tubig, pakuluin, tapos takpan at i-simmer sa low heat for 45-60 minutes, haluin paminsan-minsan, hanggang fork-tender ang karne at lumapot ang gravy.
Buksan at i-simmer pa ng ilang minuto kung kailangan pang ma-reduce ang gravy, tapos ihain mainit.
tips: Idagdag ang yogurt off direct high heat at haluin nang patuloy — ito ang step na pumipigil sa gravy na mag-curdle.
Ang pagpapalamig nang kaunti sa smoking mustard oil bago ilagay ang spices ay pumipigil sa pungency nito na maging bitter.
fil.kidNote: Gamitin ang mas kaunting Kashmiri chilli powder (o kalahatiin) sa share na ipapakain sa mga bata — mild variety naman ito na mostly para sa kulay, pero mas maganda kung konti lang para talagang gentle ang share nila — at haluin ang extra spoonful ng yogurt sa gravy nila. Nandiyan pa rin ang whole spices for aroma without any real heat.
fil.nutritionNote: Protein- at iron-rich na meat braise; umaasa ang gravy sa yogurt kesa cream for body, kaya mas mababa ang saturated fat kumpara sa butter-based curry — i-pair with rice o roti at side ng green vegetable.

recipes.title: Sooji Halwa
recipes.description: Semolina roasted in ghee until fragrant, then bloomed with warm sugar syrup and cardamom until glossy and soft — a quick, saffron-tinted festival sweet studded with fried cashews and raisins.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons of the ghee in a pan and fry the cashews and raisins until the cashews turn golden and the raisins plump up; remove and set aside.
Add the remaining ghee to the same pan and add the semolina; roast over low-medium heat, stirring constantly, for 8-10 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden — do not let it brown.
Meanwhile, warm the water with the sugar and saffron in a separate pot, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Slowly pour the warm sugar water into the roasted semolina while stirring continuously with the other hand — it will bubble and splutter, so add it carefully in a thin stream.
Stir in the cardamom powder, then cover and cook on low heat for 2-3 minutes until all the liquid is absorbed and the semolina turns soft and glossy.
Fold in the fried cashews and raisins, and finish with an extra drizzle of ghee before serving warm.
tips: Pour the liquid in slowly and keep stirring — dumping it in fast causes hard lumps that never soften.
Roast the semolina only until fragrant and pale gold; over-roasting makes the finished halwa taste dry and dense.
recipes.nutritionNote: A ghee- and sugar-rich sweet best kept to an occasional treat rather than a daily dessert; the cashews add a little protein and healthy fat, but portion it small alongside a lighter main meal.

fil.description: Semolina na ni-roast sa ghee hanggang bumango, tapos hinalo sa warm sugar syrup at cardamom hanggang glossy at soft — mabilis at saffron-tinted na festival sweet na may fried cashews at raisins.
steps: Painitin ang 2 tablespoons ng ghee sa pan at i-fry ang cashews at raisins hanggang mag-golden ang cashews at mag-plump ang raisins; alisin at itabi.
Idagdag ang natitirang ghee sa parehong pan at idagdag ang semolina; i-roast sa low-medium heat, haluin nang patuloy, for 8-10 minutes hanggang bumango at mag-light golden — wag hayaang mag-brown.
Samantala, painitin ang tubig with sugar at saffron sa ibang pot, haluin hanggang matunaw ang sugar.
Dahan-dahang ibuhos ang warm sugar water sa roasted semolina habang haluin nang patuloy gamit ang kabilang kamay — mag-bubble at mag-splutter ito, kaya ibuhos nang maingat in a thin stream.
Ihalo ang cardamom powder, tapos takpan at lutuin sa low heat for 2-3 minutes hanggang ma-absorb lahat ng liquid at maging soft at glossy ang semolina.
Ihalo ang fried cashews at raisins, at finish with extra drizzle ng ghee bago ihain mainit.
tips: Ibuhos ang liquid nang dahan-dahan at panatilihing haluin — kapag binuhos nang bigla, magkakaroon ng hard lumps na hindi na lalambot.
I-roast ang semolina hanggang lang bumango at mag-pale gold; kapag over-roasted, magiging dry at dense ang lasa ng finished halwa.
fil.nutritionNote: Ghee- at sugar-rich na sweet na mas mainam ilaan for occasional treat lang kesa daily dessert; nagdadagdag ang cashews ng kaunting protein at healthy fat, pero i-portion nang maliit kasama ng mas light na main meal.

recipes.title: Upma
recipes.description: Roasted semolina tempered with mustard seeds, lentils, cashews and curry leaves, then cooked soft and fluffy in hot water — a mild, quick South Indian breakfast that's on the table in under 20 minutes of actual cooking.
steps: Dry roast the semolina in a wide pan over low-medium heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring constantly, until it smells nutty but stays pale; set aside.
In the same pan, heat the ghee and add the mustard seeds; once they splutter, add the urad dal, chana dal and cashews and fry until golden.
Add the curry leaves, green chilli and ginger, and saute for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook until translucent.
Add the water and salt, and bring to a rolling boil.
Lower the heat and slowly stream in the roasted semolina with one hand while stirring continuously with the other to prevent lumps.
Cover and cook on low heat for 2-3 minutes until all the water is absorbed and the semolina is soft and fluffy.
Fluff with a fork, drizzle over the lemon juice, and garnish with coriander leaves before serving.
tips: Streaming the rava in slowly while stirring is the only way to avoid lumps — dumping it in all at once guarantees them.
Roast the semolina just until fragrant; over-roasted rava turns the finished upma dry and grainy.
recipes.nutritionNote: A light, quickly digested breakfast; the lentils and cashews add a little protein and the onion some fibre, but it's low in vegetables overall, so pair with fruit or a side of yogurt to round out the meal.

fil.description: Roasted semolina na ni-temper sa mustard seeds, lentils, cashews at curry leaves, tapos niluto nang soft at fluffy sa mainit na tubig — mild at mabilis na South Indian breakfast na matatapos sa loob ng 20 minutes ng actual cooking.
steps: I-dry roast ang semolina sa wide pan sa low-medium heat for 4-5 minutes, haluin nang patuloy, hanggang bumango pero manatiling pale ang kulay; itabi.
Sa parehong pan, painitin ang ghee at idagdag ang mustard seeds; once mag-splutter, idagdag ang urad dal, chana dal at cashews at i-fry hanggang golden.
Idagdag ang curry leaves, green chilli at luya, at igisa for 30 seconds.
Idagdag ang onion at lutuin hanggang translucent.
Idagdag ang tubig at asin, at pakuluin nang malakas.
Hinaan ang apoy at dahan-dahang isalin ang roasted semolina gamit ang isang kamay habang haluin nang patuloy ng kabilang kamay para hindi mag-lumps.
Takpan at lutuin sa low heat for 2-3 minutes hanggang ma-absorb lahat ng tubig at maging soft at fluffy ang semolina.
I-fluff gamit ang fork, i-drizzle ang lemon juice, at garnishan ng coriander leaves bago ihain.
tips: Ang dahan-dahang pagsalin ng rava habang haluin lang ang only way para maiwasan ang lumps — pag binuhos lahat nang sabay, sigurado magkaka-lumps.
I-roast ang semolina hanggang lang bumango; pag over-roasted, magiging dry at grainy ang finished upma.
fil.nutritionNote: Light at mabilis ma-digest na breakfast; nagdadagdag ang lentils at cashews ng kaunting protein at ang onion ng fibre, pero mababa sa gulay overall, kaya i-pair with fruit o side ng yogurt para kumpleto ang meal.

recipes.title: Agedashi Tofu
recipes.description: Starch-dusted tofu deep-fried until the outside is crisp and the inside stays custardy, served in a warm dashi-soy-mirin sauce with grated daikon and ginger — an izakaya starter that's simple enough for a weeknight.

ingredients.note: pressed 15 minutes to remove excess water
or 2 cups hot water plus 2 tsp instant dashi powder

ingredients.item: daikon radish (about 8cm piece), grated and squeezed

steps: Wrap the tofu blocks in paper towels, set a light weight on top, and press 15 minutes to remove excess water.
Combine dashi, soy sauce and mirin in a small saucepan, bring to a gentle simmer, then remove from heat and keep warm.
Grate the daikon and ginger, squeezing excess liquid from the daikon; slice the scallion.
Cut each pressed tofu block into 4 pieces and dust thoroughly on all sides with potato starch, shaking off the excess.
Heat oil in a heavy pot to 170°C (340°F) and fry the tofu in batches 2-3 minutes, turning once, until the coating is crisp and pale golden.
Drain briefly on a rack, then arrange in bowls.
Pour the warm sauce around, not over, the tofu so the crust stays crisp, and top with grated daikon, ginger, scallion and katsuobushi.
Serve immediately, mixing the tofu into the sauce bite by bite.
tips: Pour the sauce around the tofu rather than over it, and serve right away — the starch coating softens fast once it sits in liquid.
recipes.nutritionNote: A lighter, plant-protein alternative to a fried meat dish; the sauce is only moderately salty, so it works well as a side without needing extra vegetables to balance it.

fil.description: Starch-dusted na tofu na pinirito hanggang malutong sa labas pero custardy pa rin sa loob, ihinain sa mainit na dashi-soy-mirin sauce na may grated daikon at luya — isang izakaya starter na simple pa rin kahit weeknight.
ingredients: daikon radish (mga 8cm piece), grated at piniga
steps: Balutin ang tofu blocks sa paper towels, lagyan ng magaan na timbang sa ibabaw, tapos idiin for 15 minutes para maalis ang excess na tubig.
Ihalo ang dashi, toyo at mirin sa maliit na saucepan, pakuluin nang dahan-dahan, tapos alisin sa heat at panatilihing mainit.
I-grate ang daikon at luya, piniga ang excess liquid ng daikon; hiwain ang scallion.
Hiwain ang bawat pressed na tofu block into 4 pieces tapos budburan nang maigi sa lahat ng sides ng potato starch, alisin ang excess.
Painitin ang mantika sa heavy pot to 170°C (340°F) tapos i-fry ang tofu in batches for 2-3 minutes, binabaligtad once, hanggang malutong at pale golden ang coating.
I-drain nang saglit sa rack, tapos ayusin sa mga mangkok.
Ibuhos ang mainit na sauce sa paligid, hindi sa ibabaw, ng tofu para manatiling malutong ang crust, tapos tuktukan ng grated daikon, luya, scallion at katsuobushi.
Ihain agad, hinahalo ang tofu sa sauce bite by bite.
tips: Ibuhos ang sauce sa paligid ng tofu sa halip na sa ibabaw nito, tapos ihain agad — mabilis lumambot ang starch coating kapag naiwan sa liquid.
fil.nutritionNote: Mas magaan na plant-protein na alternative sa fried meat dish; katamtaman lang ang alat ng sauce, kaya gumagana ito bilang side nang hindi na kailangan ng extra gulay para i-balance.

recipes.title: Chawanmushi
recipes.description: A silky savoury egg custard steamed with chicken, shrimp, shiitake and fish cake tucked inside — a restaurant-course dish that's actually simple to make at home with a steamer and a fine sieve.

ingredients.note: or 2.5 cups hot water plus 2.5 tsp instant dashi powder, cooled
or regular soy sauce, using slightly less

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thigh, diced small
ingredients.note: marinate briefly in a splash of soy sauce and sake

ingredients.item: medium shrimp, peeled, deveined and tails removed
mitsuba or baby spinach leaves, for garnish

steps: Toss the diced chicken with a splash of soy sauce and sake and set aside to marinate briefly.
Whisk the eggs gently in a bowl without incorporating air, then stir in the cooled dashi, soy sauce, mirin and salt.
Strain the egg mixture through a fine sieve into a jug for a silky, bubble-free custard.
Divide the chicken, shrimp, shiitake and kamaboko evenly among 4 heatproof cups or chawanmushi bowls.
Pour the strained egg mixture over the fillings, filling each cup about three-quarters full, and skim off any surface bubbles with a spoon.
Cover each cup loosely with foil and set in a steamer or a wide pot with 2cm of simmering water; steam over low heat with the lid slightly ajar for 15-18 minutes.
Check doneness by inserting a skewer into the centre — it should come out with clear liquid, not raw egg.
Garnish with mitsuba or a small spinach leaf and serve hot, straight from the cup.
tips: Steam gently, never at a rolling boil, or the custard turns pocked and rubbery instead of silky — keep the lid cracked to let excess steam escape.
recipes.kidNote: Dice the shrimp and chicken small before steaming and check each cup for stray shell bits — the mild custard itself is an easy sell for all three kids.
recipes.nutritionNote: A gentle, low-sodium way to serve egg and protein together (just 1 tbsp soy sauce across the whole pot); good to balance a saltier main like tonjiru or saba misoni in the same meal.

fil.description: Isang silky at savory na egg custard na sini-steam kasama ng manok, hipon, shiitake at fish cake sa loob — isang restaurant-course na dish na madali palang gawin sa bahay gamit lang ang steamer at fine sieve.
ingredients: medium shrimp, balatan, nilinis at tinanggalan ng tail
mitsuba o baby spinach leaves, pang-garnish
steps: Ihalo ang dinicing na manok sa kaunting toyo at sake tapos itabi para mag-marinate nang saglit.
I-whisk nang dahan-dahan ang itlog sa bowl nang hindi nagpapasok ng hangin, tapos ihalo ang pinalamig na dashi, toyo, mirin at asin.
Salain ang egg mixture sa fine sieve papunta sa jug para maging silky at walang bula ang custard.
Hatiin ang manok, hipon, shiitake at kamaboko nang pantay-pantay sa 4 na heatproof cups o chawanmushi bowls.
Ibuhos ang sinalang egg mixture sa ibabaw ng mga laman, punuin ang bawat cup mga three-quarters full, tapos alisin ang anumang bula sa ibabaw gamit ang kutsara.
Takpan nang maluwag ang bawat cup ng foil tapos ilagay sa steamer o malapad na pot na may 2cm na kumukulong tubig; i-steam over low heat na medyo bukas ang takip for 15-18 minutes.
Suriin kung luto na sa pagturok ng skewer sa gitna — dapat lumabas ito na may malinaw na liquid, hindi raw na itlog.
Tuktukan ng mitsuba o maliit na spinach leaf tapos ihain mainit, diretso galing sa cup.
tips: I-steam nang dahan-dahan, huwag kailanman sa rolling boil, dahil ang custard ay magiging pocked at rubbery sa halip na silky — panatilihing medyo bukas ang takip para makalabas ang excess steam.
fil.kidNote: I-dice nang maliit ang hipon at manok bago i-steam tapos suriin ang bawat cup para sa stray shell bits — madaling matikman ng tatlong bata ang mild na custard mismo.
fil.nutritionNote: Isang gentle at low-sodium na paraan para ihain ang itlog at protein nang sabay (1 tbsp na toyo lang para sa buong pot); magandang i-balance sa mas maalat na main tulad ng tonjiru o saba misoni sa parehong meal.

recipes.title: Chicken Karaage
recipes.description: Bite-sized chicken thigh marinated in ginger, garlic, soy and sake, then double-fried in potato starch for a shatter-crisp crust and juicy centre — Japan's favourite fried chicken.

ingredients.item: boneless, skin-on chicken thighs, cut into 2-inch pieces

ingredients.note: enough for 3-4cm depth in the pot

steps: Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Add the grated ginger, garlic, soy sauce, sake and sesame oil; toss to coat and marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Set out separate piles of flour and potato starch; dredge each piece of chicken first in flour, then in potato starch, shaking off the excess.
Heat oil in a heavy pot to 160°C (325°F) and fry the chicken in small batches for 90 seconds until pale gold; drain on a wire rack.
Raise the oil temperature to 180°C (350°F) and fry each batch again for 45 seconds until deep golden and crisp.
Drain well and serve hot with lemon wedges, Kewpie mayonnaise and shichimi togarashi.
tips: The 30-minute marinade is worth the wait — it's what actually seasons the meat instead of just coating the outside.
The double fry is the trick: a lower first fry cooks the chicken through, and a hotter, quicker second fry crisps the crust without drying the meat.
recipes.kidNote: Keep the shichimi togarashi off the kids' portions and let them dip plain karaage in ketchup or mayo instead — it's naturally kid-approved without any spice.
recipes.nutritionNote: Deep-fried, so treat it as the weekend or party dish rather than a weeknight regular; balance the plate with a vegetable side and go light on the mayo dip.

fil.description: Bite-sized na hita ng manok na ni-marinate sa luya, bawang, toyo at sake, tapos double-fried sa potato starch para sa shatter-crisp na crust at juicy sa loob — paborito ng Japan na fried chicken.
ingredients: boneless na hita ng manok na may balat, hiniwa nang 2-inch
steps: Budburan ng asin at paminta ang manok.
Idagdag ang kinudkod na luya, bawang, toyo, sake at sesame oil; i-toss para mabalutan at i-marinate sa fridge for 30 minutes.
Maghanda ng hiwalay na pile ng flour at potato starch; i-dredge ang bawat piraso ng manok sa flour muna, tapos sa potato starch, ipagpag ang sobra.
Painitin ang oil sa heavy pot sa 160°C (325°F) at iprito ang manok nang paka-batch for 90 seconds hanggang pale gold; i-drain sa wire rack.
Taasan ang oil temperature sa 180°C (350°F) at iprito ulit ang bawat batch for 45 seconds hanggang deep golden at crisp.
I-drain nang maigi at ihain mainit na may lemon wedges, Kewpie mayonnaise at shichimi togarashi.
tips: Sulit ang 30-minute marinade — ito ang talagang nagtitimpla sa karne, hindi lang nagko-coat sa labas.
Ang double fry ang trick: mas mababang first fry ang magluluto sa manok, at mas mainit, mas mabilis na second fry ang mag-crisp sa crust nang hindi natutuyo ang karne.
fil.kidNote: Ilayo muna ang shichimi togarashi sa portion ng mga bata at ipa-dip na lang sa ketchup o mayo — kusang kid-approved naman ito kahit walang spice.
fil.nutritionNote: Deep-fried ito, kaya ituring na weekend o party dish sa halip na weeknight regular; i-balance ang plato ng vegetable side at bawasan ang mayo dip.

recipes.title: Chicken Katsu
recipes.description: Butterflied chicken breast pounded thin, breaded in panko and deep-fried until shatter-crisp, sliced and drizzled with a tangy ketchup-Worcestershire sauce — the everyday cutlet on every teishoku menu.

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken breast (about 160g each), butterflied and pounded to 1cm thickness

steps: Butterfly each chicken breast (kannon-biraki) and pound to an even 1cm thickness; season both sides with salt and pepper.
Whisk together ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce and sugar in a small bowl to make a quick tonkatsu sauce; set aside.
Set up three shallow trays: flour, beaten egg, and panko.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then press firmly into the panko to coat evenly on both sides.
Heat oil in a heavy pot to 170°C (340°F) and fry one or two cutlets at a time, 3-4 minutes, flipping halfway, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on a wire rack and rest 2 minutes before slicing into 1-inch strips.
Serve over shredded cabbage with the tonkatsu sauce drizzled on top or on the side.
tips: Pounding the chicken to an even thickness is what keeps it from drying out before the crust browns.
Store-bought tonkatsu sauce (Bulldog brand) is the everyday shortcut; the ketchup-Worcestershire mix here gets close without a special-order bottle.
recipes.nutritionNote: Deep-fried like karaage, so keep it a once-or-twice-a-week treat; serve with the shredded cabbage for fibre and let the vegetables — not extra sauce — fill out the plate.

fil.description: Chicken breast na binutterfly at pinipi, binreaded sa panko at pinirito hanggang shatter-crisp, hiniwa at binuhusan ng maasim na ketchup-Worcestershire sauce — ang everyday cutlet na nasa bawat teishoku menu.
ingredients: boneless, skinless chicken breast (mga 160g each), binutterfly at pinipi to 1cm thickness
steps: I-butterfly ang bawat chicken breast (kannon-biraki) tapos pipiin to an even 1cm thickness; timplahan ang dalawang sides ng asin at paminta.
I-whisk ang ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce at sugar sa maliit na bowl para gumawa ng quick tonkatsu sauce; itabi.
Ihanda ang three shallow trays: flour, beaten egg, at panko.
I-dredge ang bawat cutlet sa flour, isawsaw sa egg, tapos idiin nang maigi sa panko para pantay na mabalutan ang dalawang sides.
Painitin ang mantika sa heavy pot to 170°C (340°F) tapos i-fry ang isa o dalawang cutlets at a time, for 3-4 minutes, binabaligtad halfway, hanggang deep golden at maluto na.
I-drain sa wire rack tapos pahingahin for 2 minutes bago hiwain into 1-inch strips.
Ihain sa ibabaw ng shredded cabbage na may tonkatsu sauce na binuhos sa ibabaw o sa tabi.
tips: Ang pagpipi sa manok to an even thickness ang pumipigil dito na matuyo bago mag-brown ang crust.
Ang store-bought tonkatsu sauce (Bulldog brand) ang everyday shortcut; ang ketchup-Worcestershire mix dito ay malapit na sa lasa kahit walang special-order na bote.
fil.nutritionNote: Deep-fried tulad ng karaage, kaya i-keep as a once-or-twice-a-week treat; ihain na may shredded cabbage para sa fibre, tapos hayaang ang mga gulay — hindi extra sauce — ang magpuno sa plato.

recipes.title: Cucumber Sunomono
recipes.localTitle: きゅうりとわかめの酢の物
recipes.description: Thinly sliced cucumber and rehydrated wakame tossed in a sweet-tangy rice vinegar dressing — a refreshing, crunchy palate cleanser that cuts through the richness of a fried or braised main.

ingredients.item: Japanese or Persian cucumbers, thinly sliced
ingredients.note: or English cucumber with the seeds scooped out

ingredients.item: kosher salt, for salting the cucumbers

steps: Combine the vinegar, sugar, salt and soy sauce in a small saucepan; warm over medium heat, whisking until the sugar fully dissolves, then let cool.
Soak the dried wakame in a bowl of water 5 minutes until fully rehydrated, then drain and squeeze out excess water.
Peel the cucumber skin in alternating stripes for a decorative edge, then slice into very thin rounds.
Toss the cucumber slices with the 1 tsp salt and let sit 5 minutes to draw out excess moisture.
Squeeze the cucumber firmly by the handful to remove the released liquid.
Combine the cucumber, wakame, sesame seeds and cooled dressing in a bowl and toss well.
Serve immediately for the crunchiest texture, chilled or at room temperature.
tips: Squeeze the cucumber hard after salting, or the dressing turns watery by the time it reaches the table.
recipes.nutritionNote: A genuinely low-sodium, no-oil side (just 0.5 tsp soy sauce for the whole batch); use it to offset a saltier main like tonjiru or saba misoni in the same meal.

fil.description: Thinly sliced na cucumber at rehydrated na wakame na binalutan ng matamis-maasim na rice vinegar dressing — isang refreshing at crunchy palate cleanser na pumuputol sa bigat ng fried o braised na main.
ingredients: Japanese o Persian cucumbers, hiniwa nang manipis
steps: Ihalo ang vinegar, sugar, asin at toyo sa maliit na saucepan; painitin over medium heat, hinahalo hanggang matunaw nang buo ang sugar, tapos hayaang lumamig.
Ibabad ang dried wakame sa mangkok ng tubig for 5 minutes hanggang fully rehydrated, tapos i-drain at piniga ang excess na tubig.
Balatan ang cucumber skin nang paikot-ikot para may decorative edge, tapos hiwain into very thin rounds.
I-toss ang cucumber slices sa 1 tsp na asin tapos hayaang mag-sit for 5 minutes para lumabas ang excess moisture.
Pigain nang maigi ang cucumber by the handful para maalis ang lumabas na liquid.
Ihalo ang cucumber, wakame, sesame seeds at ang pinalamig na dressing sa mangkok tapos i-toss nang maigi.
Ihain agad para sa pinaka-crunchy na texture, chilled o sa room temperature.
tips: Pigain nang malakas ang cucumber pagkatapos i-asin, o mananubigan ang dressing pagdating sa mesa.
fil.nutritionNote: Talagang low-sodium at walang-oil na side (0.5 tsp na toyo lang para sa buong batch); gamitin para i-balance ang mas maalat na main tulad ng tonjiru o saba misoni sa parehong meal.

recipes.title: Ginger Pork
recipes.localTitle: 豚の生姜焼き (Buta no Shogayaki)
recipes.description: Thin pork loin pan-fried and glazed in a punchy soy-mirin-ginger sauce with sautéed onion — a five-ingredient weeknight staple found on nearly every teishoku set-meal menu.

ingredients.note: ask the butcher to slice it paper-thin, or partially freeze and slice yourself

ingredients.item: knob of ginger (about 10cm), grated, juice reserved
ingredients.note: bottled ginger juice works in a pinch

steps: Grate the ginger and a little onion, keeping their juices for the sauce.
Combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, half the ginger juice and the grated onion in a bowl to make the sauce.
Toss the pork with the marinating sake and the remaining ginger juice; dust lightly with flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the pork in batches until no longer pink; transfer to a plate.
Sauté the sliced onion in the same pan until translucent, about 6-8 minutes.
Return the pork to the pan, pour in the sauce, and simmer 2 minutes, spooning the sauce over the meat until glossy and slightly thickened.
Serve hot with shredded raw cabbage and rice.
tips: Dust the pork with flour right before cooking, not earlier — it helps the sauce cling and thicken without going gluey.
recipes.nutritionNote: The glaze is salty-sweet; the classic pairing of a big pile of raw shredded cabbage adds fibre and dilutes the sodium per bite, so don't skip it.

fil.description: Manipis na pork loin na pinirito sa pan at ni-glaze sa matapang na soy-mirin-ginger sauce na may sauteed sibuyas — five-ingredient weeknight staple na makikita halos sa bawat teishoku set-meal menu.
ingredients: kinudkod na sibuyas na may juice
steps: Kudkurin ang luya at kaunting sibuyas, itabi ang mga juice para sa sauce.
Ihalo ang toyo, mirin, sake, asukal, kalahati ng ginger juice at ang kinudkod na sibuyas sa mangkok para gawin ang sauce.
I-toss ang pork sa sake pang-marinate at ang natitirang ginger juice; budburan nang bahagya ng flour, ipagpag ang sobra.
Painitin ang oil sa malaking skillet sa medium-high heat at lutuin ang pork nang paka-batch hanggang hindi na pink; ilipat sa plato.
I-saute ang hiniwang sibuyas sa parehong pan hanggang malambot at translucent, mga 6-8 minutes.
Ibalik ang pork sa pan, ibuhos ang sauce, at i-simmer for 2 minutes, budburan ng sauce sa karne hanggang glossy at bahagyang lumapot.
Ihain mainit na may shredded raw cabbage at kanin.
tips: Budburan ng flour ang pork bago mismo lutuin, hindi masyadong maaga — para dumikit at lumapot nang maayos ang sauce, hindi gooey.
fil.nutritionNote: Salty-sweet ang glaze; ang classic pairing na malaking pile ng raw shredded cabbage ay nagdadagdag ng fibre at nagpapabawas sa sodium per bite, kaya huwag i-skip.

recipes.title: Gyudon
recipes.description: Paper-thin beef and onion simmered in a savory-sweet dashi-soy broth and ladled over rice with pickled ginger — Japan's favourite fast, cheap beef bowl.

ingredients.item: thinly sliced beef (ribeye or chuck), cut into 3-inch pieces
ingredients.note: partially freeze the beef 15 minutes to slice it paper-thin
or 1 cup water plus 1 tsp instant dashi powder

ingredients.item: pickled red ginger (beni shoga), for garnish

steps: Thinly slice the onion and cut the scallion diagonally into thin pieces.
In a large cold frying pan, combine dashi, sake, mirin, soy sauce and sugar, stirring to dissolve the sugar.
Scatter the onion over the sauce, then layer the beef slices on top, spreading to cover the onion.
Cover, turn the heat to medium, and once simmering reduce to low; cook 3-4 minutes, skimming any foam and fat from the broth.
Sprinkle the scallion on top, cover, and cook 1 more minute until the beef is just cooked through.
Serve over bowls of hot rice, spooning extra broth on top, and garnish with pickled red ginger.
tips: Simmer gently rather than boiling — hard boiling toughens the thin beef slices.
recipes.nutritionNote: The sauce is soy-sauce-forward and salty; serve with a vegetable side like shredded cabbage or cucumber salad instead of extra soy sauce at the table.

fil.description: Manipis na beef at sibuyas na sinimmer sa savory-sweet na dashi-soy broth at binuhusan sa kanin na may pickled ginger — ang paborito ng Japan na fast, cheap na beef bowl.
ingredients: manipis na hiniwang beef (ribeye o chuck), hiniwa nang 3-inch
steps: Hiwain nang manipis ang sibuyas at ihiwa ang scallion nang pahilis, manipis na piraso.
Sa malaking cold frying pan, ihalo ang dashi, sake, mirin, toyo at asukal, haluin hanggang matunaw ang asukal.
Ikalat ang sibuyas sa ibabaw ng sauce, tapos patungan ng beef slices, ikalat para matakpan ang sibuyas.
Takpan, i-set sa medium heat, tapos pag nagsi-simmer na i-lower sa low; lutuin for 3-4 minutes, tinatanggal ang foam at fat sa broth.
Budburan ng scallion sa ibabaw, takpan, at lutuin for 1 more minute hanggang maluto na ang beef.
Ihain sa mangkok ng mainit na kanin, budburan ng extra broth, at topan ng pickled red ginger.
tips: I-simmer nang mahinay lang, huwag pakuluin nang malakas — pag hard boiling, tumitigas ang manipis na beef slices.
fil.nutritionNote: Soy-sauce-forward at maalat ang sauce; ihain kasabay ng vegetable side tulad ng shredded cabbage o cucumber salad sa halip na dagdag na toyo sa table.

recipes.title: Japanese Curry Rice
recipes.description: Chicken, carrot and potato simmered in stock and melted into a thick, mildly spiced roux — the one-pot family dinner nearly every Japanese pantry keeps a box of curry roux for.

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks
ingredients.note: or swap in thinly sliced pork for pork curry using the same method
or water, or half stock and half water

ingredients.item: Japanese curry roux, mild (e.g. S&B Golden Curry or House Vermont Curry)
ingredients.note: about 100g, roughly half a standard box

steps: Cut the onion into thick wedges, carrot into rolling-cut chunks, and potatoes into large quarters; soak the potatoes in water 15 minutes to remove excess starch.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion until soft and golden, about 5 minutes; add the garlic and ginger and stir until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring, until no longer pink on the outside.
Pour in the stock, then add the grated apple, honey, soy sauce and ketchup; the liquid should just cover the ingredients.
Add the carrot and drained potatoes, bring to a boil, and skim off any foam.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Turn off the heat, break the curry roux into pieces, and dissolve it a little at a time in ladlefuls of the hot liquid, stirring it back into the pot.
Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat 5-10 minutes, stirring often, until thickened; watch that it doesn't catch on the bottom.
Serve ladled over rice, with fukujinzuke pickles on the side if you have them.
tips: Curry roux blocks range from mild to very hot — use the mild (amakuchi) block for a family pot; it still has a warm background spice, not real heat.
recipes.kidNote: Use the mild block for the whole pot rather than making a separate spicy batch — Japanese curry roux at 'mild' is genuinely gentle and is what most families serve to a 6-year-old.
recipes.nutritionNote: Curry roux is high in fat and sodium from the roux block itself; bulk out the pot with extra carrot and potato and serve alongside a simple salad to stretch the vegetables.

fil.description: Manok, carrot at patatas na sinimmer sa stock at natunaw sa makapal, mild ang spice na roux — ang one-pot family dinner na halos bawat Japanese pantry ay may nakatagong box ng curry roux.
ingredients: sibuyas, hiniwa nang makapal na wedges
patatas, quartered at binabad for 15 minutes
boneless na hita ng manok na walang balat, hiniwa nang chunks
Japanese curry roux, mild (hal. S&B Golden Curry o House Vermont Curry)
steps: Hiwain ang sibuyas nang makapal na wedges, ang carrot nang rolling-cut chunks, at ang patatas nang malalaking quarters; ibabad ang patatas sa tubig for 15 minutes para matanggal ang sobrang starch.
Painitin ang oil sa malaking pot sa medium heat at i-saute ang sibuyas hanggang malambot at golden, mga 5 minutes; idagdag ang bawang at luya at haluin hanggang mabango.
Idagdag ang manok at lutuin, haluin, hanggang hindi na pink sa labas.
Ibuhos ang stock, tapos idagdag ang kinudkod na mansanas, pulot, toyo at ketchup; dapat halos matakpan ng liquid ang mga sangkap.
Idagdag ang carrot at ang tinuyong patatas, pakuluin, at alisin ang foam.
Takpan at i-simmer sa medium-low heat for 15 minutes, haluin paminsan-minsan, hanggang halos malambot na ang gulay.
Patayin ang apoy, dagdagin ang curry roux sa maliliit na piraso, at tunawin nang paunti-unti gamit ang mainit na liquid, ihalo pabalik sa pot.
I-simmer nang bukas sa medium-low heat for 5-10 minutes, haluin madalas, hanggang lumapot; bantayan para hindi masunog sa ilalim.
Ihain nang nakabuhos sa kanin, may side na fukujinzuke pickles kung meron.
tips: Malawak ang range ng curry roux blocks mula mild hanggang very hot — gamitin ang mild (amakuchi) block para sa family pot; may background spice pa rin ito pero hindi totoong maanghang.
fil.kidNote: Gamitin ang mild block para sa buong pot sa halip na gumawa ng hiwalay na spicy batch — talagang mahinahon ang Japanese curry roux sa 'mild' at ito ang iniserve ng karamihan ng pamilya sa 6-year-old.
fil.nutritionNote: Mataas sa fat at sodium ang curry roux mismo; dagdagan ang pot ng extra carrot at patatas at ihain kasabay ng simpleng salad para ma-stretch ang gulay.

recipes.title: Katsudon
recipes.description: A freshly fried pork cutlet simmered briefly with onion in a sweet soy-dashi broth, bound with soft-set egg, and slid over hot rice — the heartier, fried-cutlet cousin of oyakodon.

ingredients.item: boneless pork loin cutlets (about 120g each), pounded to 1cm thick
egg, lightly beaten, for the sauce

ingredients.note: or 2 cups hot water plus 2 tsp instant dashi powder

steps: Season the pork cutlets with salt and pepper; dredge each in flour, dip in beaten egg, then coat in panko, pressing to adhere.
Heat oil in a heavy pot to 170°C (340°F) and fry the cutlets 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through; drain and slice into strips.
Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a small frying pan and bring to a simmer.
Add a quarter of the sliced onion per portion and simmer 2 minutes until softened.
Lay a sliced cutlet on top of the onion, pour a quarter of the beaten egg around and over it, cover, and cook 30 seconds.
Drizzle the remaining egg over the top, cover, and cook 1 minute more until just set but still a little runny in the centre.
Slide the cutlet-and-egg mixture over a bowl of hot rice, spooning any extra sauce on top; repeat for the remaining portions.
Scatter with scallion and serve immediately.
tips: Cook one portion at a time in a small pan — it's how the egg sets neatly around the cutlet instead of scrambling.
recipes.nutritionNote: A fried cutlet plus egg plus rice is heavy on fat and sodium all at once; serve a side of raw or pickled vegetables and treat it as a once-a-week bowl rather than a Tuesday default like oyakodon.

fil.description: Bagong pritong pork cutlet na sini-simmer nang saglit kasama ng sibuyas sa matamis na soy-dashi broth, binuklod ng soft-set egg, tapos isinasalang sa mainit na kanin — ang mas heavy, fried-cutlet cousin ng oyakodon.
ingredients: boneless pork loin cutlets (mga 120g each), pinipi to 1cm thick
itlog, lightly beaten, para sa sauce
steps: Timplahan ang pork cutlets ng asin at paminta; i-dredge ang bawat isa sa flour, isawsaw sa beaten egg, tapos balutin sa panko, idiin para dumikit.
Painitin ang mantika sa heavy pot to 170°C (340°F) tapos i-fry ang cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side hanggang golden at maluto na; i-drain tapos hiwain into strips.
Ihalo ang dashi, toyo, mirin at sugar sa maliit na frying pan tapos pakuluin nang dahan-dahan.
Idagdag ang isang-fourth ng hiniwang sibuyas per portion tapos i-simmer for 2 minutes hanggang lumambot.
Ilagay ang isang hiniwang cutlet sa ibabaw ng sibuyas, buhusan ng isang-fourth ng beaten egg sa paligid at ibabaw nito, takpan, tapos lutuin for 30 seconds.
Buhusan ng natitirang egg sa ibabaw, takpan, tapos lutuin for 1 minute more hanggang just set pero medyo runny pa sa gitna.
Isalang ang cutlet-and-egg mixture sa ibabaw ng isang mangkok ng mainit na kanin, buhusan ng extra sauce sa ibabaw; ulitin para sa natitirang portions.
Budburan ng scallion tapos ihain agad.
tips: Lutuin ang isang portion at a time sa maliit na kawali — ganito na-se-set nang maayos ang itlog sa paligid ng cutlet sa halip na mag-scramble.
fil.nutritionNote: Ang fried cutlet plus itlog plus kanin ay heavy sa fat at sodium nang sabay; ihain na may side ng raw o pickled na gulay at ituring itong once-a-week bowl sa halip na Tuesday default tulad ng oyakodon.

recipes.title: Kinpira Gobo
recipes.description: Julienned burdock root and carrot stir-fried in sesame oil, then glazed in a quick soy-mirin-sugar sauce until glossy and tender-crisp — the everyday bento side found in nearly every Japanese fridge.

ingredients.item: dried red chili pepper, seeded and sliced into rounds
ingredients.note: optional; leave out for the kids' portion, it's easy to fish out whole

steps: Scrape the gobo skin with the back of a knife, slice diagonally into thin ovals, then cut into fine matchsticks; soak in water 10 minutes, changing the water once, to remove bitterness.
Drain the gobo well and julienne the carrot into matchsticks of a similar size.
Heat the sesame oil in a large pan over medium heat and stir-fry the gobo 2-3 minutes until it starts to soften.
Add the carrot and continue stir-frying 2-3 minutes until both vegetables are tender-crisp.
Add the sugar, sake, mirin and soy sauce; toss to coat evenly.
Stir in the chili pepper, if using, and cook until the liquid has mostly evaporated and the vegetables look glossy.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds, toss once more, and serve warm or at room temperature.
tips: Kinpira keeps 3-4 days refrigerated and is a classic bento box filler — make a double batch on a Sunday for lunchboxes through the week.
recipes.nutritionNote: One of the few fibre-forward, low-fat sides in a washoku spread; good to pair with a fattier fried main like katsu or karaage to balance the plate.

fil.description: Julienned na burdock root at carrot na sini-stir-fry sa sesame oil, tapos binalutan ng quick soy-mirin-sugar sauce hanggang makintab at tender-crisp — ang everyday bento side na makikita halos sa bawat Japanese fridge.
ingredients: dried red chili pepper, tinanggalan ng buto at hiniwa into rounds
steps: Kayurin ang balat ng gobo gamit ang likod ng kutsilyo, hiwain diagonally into thin ovals, tapos gawing manipis na matchsticks; ibabad sa tubig for 10 minutes, pinapalitan ang tubig once, para maalis ang pait.
I-drain nang maigi ang gobo tapos i-julienne ang carrot into matchsticks ng parehong size.
Painitin ang sesame oil sa malaking kawali over medium heat tapos i-stir-fry ang gobo for 2-3 minutes hanggang magsimulang lumambot.
Idagdag ang carrot tapos ipagpatuloy ang stir-fry for 2-3 minutes hanggang tender-crisp ang dalawa.
Idagdag ang sugar, sake, mirin at toyo; i-toss para mabalutan nang pantay.
Ihalo ang chili pepper, kung gagamitin, tapos lutuin hanggang halos matuyo ang liquid at maging makintab ang gulay.
Budburan ng sesame seeds, i-toss ulit, tapos ihain mainit o sa room temperature.
tips: Ang kinpira ay tumatagal ng 3-4 days sa ref at classic bento box filler — gumawa ng double batch tuwing Sunday para sa lunchbox sa buong linggo.
fil.nutritionNote: Isa sa iilang fibre-forward at low-fat na side sa washoku spread; magandang isabay sa mas mataba na fried main tulad ng katsu o karaage para ma-balance ang plato.

recipes.title: Kitsune Udon
recipes.description: Thick, chewy udon noodles in a clear bonito dashi broth topped with sweet soy-simmered fried tofu pouches — the coziest, mildest noodle soup in the Japanese home repertoire.

ingredients.note: or use 2 tsp instant dashi powder in place of steps 1-2
or regular soy sauce, using slightly less
store-bought seasoned pouches, or simmer plain abura-age in dashi, soy sauce and mirin yourself

ingredients.item: udon noodle servings (fresh, frozen or dried)

steps: Soak the kombu in the water for 30 minutes, then heat slowly until small bubbles form; remove the kombu just before it boils.
Add the katsuobushi, simmer 15 seconds, then turn off the heat and let the flakes settle 10-15 minutes before straining — this is the dashi.
Return the dashi to a saucepan, add the mirin, sugar, soy sauce and salt, and bring to a boil, then hold at a gentle simmer.
Squeeze any excess liquid from the inari age pouches; thinly slice the scallion and narutomaki.
Boil the udon noodles according to the package directions (about 1 minute for frozen, longer for dried), then drain thoroughly.
Divide the noodles between deep bowls, ladle the hot broth over the top, and top with inari age, narutomaki and scallion.
Serve immediately with shichimi togarashi on the side.
tips: Keep frozen udon on hand — it cooks from frozen in about a minute and has a springier bite than dried noodles.
recipes.kidNote: Like miso soup, this broth carries a strong bonito-dashi flavour; if the kids are new to it, start with a slightly diluted broth and work up to the full-strength recipe.
recipes.nutritionNote: The broth and seasoned tofu pouches both add sodium; balance the bowl with a side of the sesame spinach or another plain vegetable rather than extra toppings.

fil.description: Makapal, chewy na udon noodles sa malinaw na bonito dashi broth na may toppings na sweet soy-simmered fried tofu pouches — ang pinaka-cozy, pinaka-mild na noodle soup sa Japanese home repertoire.
ingredients: udon noodle servings (fresh, frozen o dried)
steps: Ibabad ang kombu sa tubig for 30 minutes, tapos painitin nang dahan-dahan hanggang magkaroon ng maliliit na bubbles; alisin ang kombu bago pa kumulo.
Idagdag ang katsuobushi, i-simmer for 15 seconds, tapos patayin ang apoy at hayaang lumubog ang flakes for 10-15 minutes bago i-strain — ito na ang dashi.
Ibalik ang dashi sa saucepan, idagdag ang mirin, asukal, toyo at asin, pakuluin, tapos ibaba sa mahinang simmer.
Pigain ang sobrang liquid sa inari age pouches; hiwain nang manipis ang scallion at narutomaki.
Pakuluin ang udon noodles ayon sa package directions (mga 1 minute para sa frozen, mas matagal para sa dried), tapos i-drain nang mabuti.
Hatiin ang noodles sa malalim na mangkok, buhusan ng mainit na broth, at topan ng inari age, narutomaki at scallion.
Ihain agad na may shichimi togarashi sa tabi.
tips: Magtago ng frozen udon — nagluluto ito mula frozen in about a minute at mas springy ang bite kaysa dried noodles.
fil.kidNote: Tulad ng miso soup, malakas ang bonito-dashi flavor ng broth na ito; kung bago pa lang ang mga bata dito, simulan sa medyo diluted na broth at unti-untiin papunta sa full-strength recipe.
fil.nutritionNote: Nagdadagdag ng sodium ang broth at ang seasoned tofu pouches; i-balance ang mangkok ng side na sesame spinach o ibang plain vegetable sa halip na dagdag na toppings.

recipes.title: Miso Soup with Tofu and Wakame
recipes.description: Silky tofu and wakame in a bonito-kombu dashi, finished with dissolved miso paste — the five-minute soup that opens almost every Japanese meal, savory without being heavy.

ingredients.note: or skip steps 1-3 and stir 1 tsp instant dashi powder into the hot water instead

ingredients.item: soft or silken tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes

ingredients.note: white (shiro) miso is milder and sweeter; red (aka) miso is saltier — many families blend the two

steps: Soak the kombu in the water and heat slowly over medium-low heat; remove the kombu just before the water boils.
Add the katsuobushi, return to a boil, and simmer 30 seconds.
Turn off the heat, let the bonito flakes sink for about 10 minutes, then strain through a fine sieve — this is the dashi.
Return the dashi to the pot, add the tofu and wakame, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Ladle a little hot dashi into a small bowl, dissolve the miso paste into it, then stir it back into the pot; do not let the soup boil again once the miso is in.
Scatter scallion over the top and serve immediately.
tips: Never boil the soup once the miso is added — high heat cooks off its aroma and flattens the flavour.
recipes.kidNote: The bonito dashi has a pronounced savoury edge that some young kids find strong at first; use a little less miso in their bowls and let them ease into the full recipe.
recipes.nutritionNote: Miso paste is one of the saltiest ingredients in Japanese cooking; this pot already keeps to a moderate 4 tbsp for 4 bowls, so skip extra soy sauce elsewhere in the same meal.

fil.description: Malambot na tofu at wakame sa bonito-kombu dashi, tinapos ng tinunaw na miso paste — ang five-minute soup na nagbubukas halos sa bawat Japanese meal, savory pero hindi mabigat.
ingredients: katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes), maluwag na sukat
soft o silken tofu, hiniwa nang 1/2-inch cubes
steps: Ibabad ang kombu sa tubig at painitin nang dahan-dahan sa medium-low heat; alisin ang kombu bago pa kumulo ang tubig.
Idagdag ang katsuobushi, pakuluin ulit, at i-simmer for 30 seconds.
Patayin ang apoy, hayaang lumubog ang bonito flakes for about 10 minutes, tapos i-strain sa fine sieve — ito na ang dashi.
Ibalik ang dashi sa pot, idagdag ang tofu at wakame, at pakuluin nang bahagya.
Kumuha ng kaunting mainit na dashi sa maliit na mangkok, tunawin ang miso paste dito, tapos ihalo pabalik sa pot; huwag hayaang kumulo ulit ang sabaw pag nasa loob na ang miso.
Budburan ng scallion sa ibabaw at ihain agad.
tips: Huwag hayaang kumulo ang soup pag nailagay na ang miso — nawawala ang aroma at flat ang flavor sa high heat.
fil.kidNote: Malakas ang lasa ng bonito dashi na baka masyadong strong para sa ilang batang bata; gamitan ng mas kaunting miso ang mangkok nila at unti-untiin lang hanggang sa full recipe.
fil.nutritionNote: Isa sa pinaka-maalat na sangkap sa Japanese cooking ang miso paste; medyo katamtaman na ang 4 tbsp para sa 4 na mangkok dito, kaya i-skip na lang ang extra toyo sa ibang bahagi ng meal.

recipes.title: Nikujaga
recipes.description: Thin beef, potato, carrot and shirataki noodles simmered in a soy-mirin-dashi broth until the potatoes fall apart — the definitive home-style simmered dish, better the next day.

ingredients.item: thinly sliced beef (ribeye or chuck), cut into bite-sized pieces
shirataki noodles, parboiled and cut in half
ingredients.note: or use soaked glass noodles, or omit if unavailable
or 2 cups water plus 2 tsp instant dashi powder

steps: Blanch the snow peas in salted boiling water 1 minute and set aside; parboil the shirataki noodles per package directions, drain, and cut roughly in half.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté the onion wedges over medium heat until coated and starting to soften.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it apart, until no longer pink.
Add the potatoes, carrot and shirataki; stir to coat in the rendered fat and juices.
Pour in the dashi, bring to a boil, and skim off any foam.
Add the sugar, sake, soy sauce and mirin; cover with a drop lid (otoshibuta) or a parchment round and simmer 12-14 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Remove from the heat and let stand, uncovered, at least 15 minutes so the potatoes finish absorbing the broth.
Stir in the blanched snow peas, gently reheat, and serve in deep bowls with the broth.
tips: A drop lid keeps the potatoes submerged so they cook evenly without breaking apart — a round of parchment paper with a steam hole works as a substitute.
This is a classic nimono (simmered dish): it tastes even better after resting off the heat, or reheated the next day.
recipes.nutritionNote: A balanced one-pot of meat, potato and vegetable; the broth itself is salty, so give young kids a smaller ladle of liquid and bulk their bowl with extra potato and carrot instead.

fil.description: Manipis na beef, patatas, carrot at shirataki noodles na sinimmer sa soy-mirin-dashi broth hanggang malambot na malambot ang patatas — ang tunay na home-style simmered dish, mas masarap pa kinabukasan.
ingredients: manipis na hiniwang beef (ribeye o chuck), hiniwa nang bite-size
shirataki noodles, pinarboil at hiniwa nang kalahati
snow peas, tinanggalan ng strings, blanched
steps: I-blanch ang snow peas sa maalat na kumukulong tubig for 1 minute at itabi; i-parboil ang shirataki noodles ayon sa package directions, i-drain, at hiwain nang kalahati.
Painitin ang oil sa malaking pot at i-saute ang sibuyas wedges sa medium heat hanggang mabalutan at nagsisimulang lumambot.
Idagdag ang beef at lutuin, hatiin ang mga piraso, hanggang hindi na pink.
Idagdag ang patatas, carrot at shirataki; haluin para mabalutan sa fat at juices.
Ibuhos ang dashi, pakuluin, at alisin ang foam.
Idagdag ang asukal, sake, toyo at mirin; takpan ng drop lid (otoshibuta) o parchment round at i-simmer for 12-14 minutes hanggang malambot ang patatas.
Alisin sa apoy at hayaang tumigil, nakabukas, for at least 15 minutes para masipsip pa ng patatas ang broth.
Ihalo ang blanched snow peas, painitin ulit nang bahagya, at ihain sa malalim na mangkok kasama ang broth.
tips: Pinapanatili ng drop lid ang patatas na nakalubog para pantay ang pagkaluto nang hindi nadudurog — pwedeng gamitin din ang parchment paper na may butas para sa singaw.
Classic nimono ito: mas masarap pa pagkatapos mahimlay off the heat, o kinabukasan pag-init ulit.
fil.nutritionNote: Balanced na one-pot ng karne, patatas at gulay; maalat mismo ang broth, kaya bigyan ang maliliit na bata ng mas kaunting sabaw at dagdagan na lang ng patatas at carrot ang mangkok nila.

recipes.title: Onigiri
recipes.description: Warm rice hand-shaped into triangles around a savoury filling and wrapped in nori — the portable, no-recipe-needed staple of Japanese lunchboxes, made here with salted salmon and soy-bonito okaka.

ingredients.item: nori seaweed sheets, cut into strips
soy sauce, for the okaka filling

steps: Season the salmon fillet with the 0.5 tsp salt and pan-sear over medium heat until just cooked through, about 4-5 minutes per side; cool and flake into large pieces, discarding skin and bones.
For the okaka filling, mix the katsuobushi with the soy sauce in a small bowl until evenly moistened.
Keep the cooked rice warm; wet your hands and rub a pinch of salt evenly over both palms.
Scoop about 1/2 cup of rice into one palm, press a shallow indent in the centre, and add a spoonful of one filling.

Cover the filling with a little more rice, then cup your hands and gently press the rice into a triangle, rotating and pressing firmly on each of the three edges — do not squeeze hard or the rice turns dense.
Wrap a strip of nori around the base of each onigiri just before serving so it stays crisp.
Repeat with the remaining rice and fillings, making about 8 onigiri total.
tips: Keep the rice warm while shaping — cold rice won't hold together — and always salt your palms rather than the rice itself, so each bite isn't oversalted.
recipes.nutritionNote: A plain, low-sodium way to serve rice on its own; the okaka and salted salmon fillings add just enough seasoning without needing extra soy sauce at the table.

fil.description: Mainit na kanin na hinugis by hand into triangles sa paligid ng masarap na filling tapos binalot ng nori — ang portable at no-recipe-needed staple ng Japanese lunchboxes, ginawa dito na may salted salmon at soy-bonito okaka.
ingredients: nori seaweed sheets, hiniwa into strips
steps: Timplahan ang salmon fillet ng 0.5 tsp na asin tapos i-pan-sear over medium heat hanggang just cooked through, mga 4-5 minutes per side; palamigin tapos i-flake into large pieces, itapon ang balat at buto.
Para sa okaka filling, ihalo ang katsuobushi sa toyo sa maliit na bowl hanggang evenly moistened.
Panatilihing mainit ang cooked rice; basain ang kamay tapos kuskusin ang kaunting asin nang pantay-pantay sa dalawang palad.
Kumuha ng mga 1/2 cup na kanin sa isang palad, gumawa ng shallow indent sa gitna, tapos maglagay ng isang kutsarang filling.

Takpan ang filling ng kaunti pang kanin, tapos ikuyom ang mga kamay at dahan-dahang idiin ang kanin into a triangle, iniikot at idiniin nang maigi ang bawat isa sa tatlong edges — huwag pisilin nang malakas o dedensong ang kanin.
Balutin ng strip ng nori ang base ng bawat onigiri bago mismo ihain para manatiling malutong.
Ulitin para sa natitirang kanin at fillings, gumagawa ng mga 8 onigiri total.
tips: Panatilihing mainit ang kanin habang hinuhugis — hindi magkakadikit ang malamig na kanin — tapos laging asinan ang palad sa halip na ang kanin mismo, para hindi masobrahan ang alat sa bawat kagat.
fil.nutritionNote: Isang plain at low-sodium na paraan para ihain ang kanin nang mag-isa; ang okaka at salted salmon fillings ay nagdadagdag lang ng sapat na timpla nang hindi na kailangan pa ng extra toyo sa mesa.

recipes.title: Oyakodon
recipes.description: Chicken and onion simmered in a sweet soy-dashi sauce, finished with a soft-set egg and poured over hot rice — the one-bowl dinner every Japanese kid grows up on.

ingredients.item: boneless, skin-on chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.note: or 1 cup hot water plus 1 tsp instant dashi powder

ingredients.item: mitsuba or scallion, chopped, for garnish

steps: Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a bowl or pan and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the sliced onion and chicken to the sauce in a large frying pan; cover and simmer over medium heat 4-5 minutes until the chicken is nearly cooked through.
Drizzle half the beaten egg evenly over the top, cover, and cook 30 seconds.
Drizzle the remaining egg over the top, cover, and cook about 1 minute more until just set but still glossy and a little runny in the centre.
Slide the chicken-and-egg mixture over bowls of hot rice, spooning any extra sauce on top.
Scatter with mitsuba or scallion and serve immediately.
tips: Traditionally each portion is cooked individually in a small oyakodon pan for a neater slide onto the rice; one big pan works fine for a family dinner.
recipes.kidNote: Cook the egg a little further (fully set, not runny) for younger kids who aren't used to a soft-cooked yolk.
recipes.nutritionNote: The soy-mirin sauce is salty-sweet; balance the sodium with a side of pickled or raw vegetables rather than extra soy sauce at the table.

fil.description: Manok at sibuyas na sinimmer sa matamis na toyo-dashi sauce, tapos tinapos ng soft-set na itlog at ibinuhos sa mainit na kanin — yung one-bowl dinner na kinalakihan ng bawat batang Hapon.
ingredients: boneless na hita ng manok na may balat, hiniwa nang bite-size
steps: Ihalo ang dashi, toyo, mirin at asukal sa mangkok o kaldero at haluin hanggang matunaw ang asukal.
Idagdag ang hiniwang sibuyas at manok sa sauce sa loob ng malaking frying pan; takpan at i-simmer sa medium heat for 4-5 minutes hanggang halos maluto na ang manok.
Ibuhos ang kalahati ng hinalong itlog nang pantay-pantay sa ibabaw, takpan, at lutuin for 30 seconds.
Ibuhos ang natitirang itlog sa ibabaw, takpan, at lutuin for 1 minute more hanggang mag-set pero glossy pa rin at bahagyang runny sa gitna.
Idulas ang manok-at-itlog na timpla sa ibabaw ng mangkok ng mainit na kanin, budburan ng extra sauce sa ibabaw.
Budburan ng mitsuba o scallion at ihain agad.
tips: Karaniwan, isa-isang niluluto ang bawat serving sa maliit na oyakodon pan para maayos ang pagdulas sa kanin; pwede rin gamit ang isang malaking pan kung pang-family dinner.
fil.kidNote: Lutuin nang mas matagal ang itlog (fully set, hindi runny) para sa mas batang kids na hindi pa sanay sa soft-cooked yolk.
fil.nutritionNote: Salty-sweet ang soy-mirin sauce; i-balance ang sodium gamit ang side na pickled o raw vegetables kaysa dagdag na toyo sa table.

recipes.title: Saba Misoni
recipes.description: Mackerel fillets blanched to remove their strong smell, then simmered slowly in a ginger-miso sauce until glossy and tender — a classic izakaya and home-dinner-table fish dish, best made a day ahead.

ingredients.item: knob of ginger (about 8cm), half sliced and half julienned for garnish

ingredients.note: avoid sweet white miso here, it's too mild for this dish

ingredients.item: miso paste, red or dark, for finishing

steps: Score a shallow cross in the skin side of each mackerel fillet to help it cook evenly and absorb the sauce.
Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the fillets one at a time for 10-15 seconds, then shock in ice water; this removes the strong fishy smell. Drain well.
Combine the water, sake, mirin, sugar, sliced ginger and half the miso in a wide skillet and bring to a boil, stirring to dissolve the miso.
Lay the mackerel skin-side up in the simmering sauce, cover with a drop lid, and simmer over medium-low heat 12-13 minutes.
Dissolve the remaining miso into the sauce and drizzle in the soy sauce, tilting the pan to baste the fish.
Remove from heat, cover, and let the fish rest in the sauce 20-30 minutes off the heat to absorb the flavour.
Reheat gently over medium heat without boiling hard, plate, and top with the julienned ginger.
tips: Blanching the fish first is the step that keeps this from tasting overly 'fishy' — don't skip it.
Like most nimono, it tastes even better the next day; make it a day ahead and reheat gently.
recipes.kidNote: Mackerel is an oily, strongly flavoured fish that some kids need to grow into; flake each piece carefully off the bone before serving and start the kids with a smaller portion alongside plain rice.
recipes.nutritionNote: Mackerel is rich in omega-3s but the miso sauce is salty and the fish itself is fatty; serve with extra rice and a plain vegetable side rather than a second salty dish in the same meal.

fil.description: Mackerel fillets na binlanch para maalis ang matapang na amoy, tapos sini-simmer nang mabagal sa ginger-miso sauce hanggang makintab at malambot — isang classic izakaya at home-dinner-table na fish dish, mas masarap kung gagawin isang araw bago ihain.
ingredients: knob ng luya (mga 8cm), kalahati hiniwa at kalahati julienned pang-garnish
miso paste, red o dark, pang-finishing
steps: Gumawa ng shallow cross sa skin side ng bawat mackerel fillet para pantay ang pagkaluto at masipsip ang sauce.
Pakuluin ang isang pot ng tubig tapos i-blanch ang fillets one at a time for 10-15 seconds, tapos i-shock sa ice water; ito ang nag-aalis ng matapang na amoy ng isda. I-drain nang maigi.
Ihalo ang tubig, sake, mirin, sugar, hiniwang luya at kalahati ng miso sa malapad na skillet tapos pakuluin, hinahalo hanggang matunaw ang miso.
Ilagay ang mackerel skin-side up sa kumukulong sauce, takpan ng drop lid, tapos i-simmer over medium-low heat for 12-13 minutes.
Tunawin ang natitirang miso sa sauce tapos patakan ng toyo, ikiling ang kawali para ma-baste ang isda.
Alisin sa heat, takpan, tapos hayaang magpahinga ang isda sa sauce for 20-30 minutes off the heat para masipsip ang lasa.
I-reheat nang dahan-dahan over medium heat nang hindi hinahayaang kumulo nang malakas, ihain sa plato, tapos tuktukan ng julienned na luya.
tips: Ang pag-blanch sa isda muna ang hakbang na pumipigil dito na maging masyadong 'malansa' — huwag laktawan.
Tulad ng karamihan sa nimono, mas masarap ito kinabukasan; gawin isang araw bago tapos i-reheat nang dahan-dahan.
fil.kidNote: Ang mackerel ay oily at matapang na lasa na isda na kailangan pang masanay ng ilang bata; i-flake nang maigi ang bawat piraso mula sa buto bago ihain tapos simulan ang mga bata sa mas maliit na portion kasama ng plain rice.
fil.nutritionNote: Mayaman sa omega-3 ang mackerel pero maalat ang miso sauce at mataba ang isda mismo; ihain na may extra kanin at plain vegetable side sa halip na isa pang maalat na ulam sa parehong meal.

recipes.title: Salmon Teriyaki
recipes.localTitle: 鮭の照り焼き (Sake no Teriyaki)
recipes.description: Pan-seared salmon steamed briefly under a lid, then glazed in a glossy soy-mirin-sake sauce until sticky-sweet — ready faster than delivery and a sure hit with kids.
steps: Pat the salmon dry, season both sides with salt and pepper, then dust evenly with flour.
Combine sake, mirin, soy sauce and sugar in a bowl and stir or briefly warm to dissolve the sugar.
Heat oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat; sear the salmon skin-side down 3 minutes until golden.
Flip the fillets, add the 2 tbsp steaming sake, cover, reduce heat to low, and steam 3-5 minutes until just cooked through.
Transfer the salmon to a plate, pour the teriyaki sauce into the pan, and bring to a boil.
Return the salmon to the pan and spoon the sauce over until glossy and slightly thickened; serve at once with the pan sauce drizzled on top.
tips: Dredging the fish in flour before searing is what lets the sauce cling and reduce to a glossy glaze instead of a thin liquid.
recipes.kidNote: Salmon is a fattier fish; flake each portion and check carefully for stray pin bones before serving to the 6-year-old — most kids love the sweet glaze.
recipes.nutritionNote: A good source of omega-3s from the salmon, but the glaze is sugar-and-soy heavy; keep any extra table soy sauce off the rice and pair with a plain vegetable side.

fil.description: Pan-seared salmon na steamed nang sandali sa ilalim ng takip, tapos ni-glaze sa makintab na soy-mirin-sake sauce hanggang sticky-sweet — mas mabilis pa sa delivery at sigurado ang thumbs-up ng mga bata.
ingredients: skin-on salmon fillets (mga 150g each, 2cm ang kapal)
steps: I-pat dry ang salmon, budburan ng asin at paminta ang dalawang side, tapos budburan nang pantay ng flour.
Ihalo ang sake, mirin, toyo at asukal sa mangkok, haluin o bahagyang initin hanggang matunaw ang asukal.
Painitin ang oil at butter sa malaking skillet sa medium heat; i-sear ang salmon skin-side down for 3 minutes hanggang golden.
I-flip ang fillets, idagdag ang 2 tbsp sake pang-steam, takpan, ibaba ang heat sa low, at i-steam for 3-5 minutes hanggang maluto na.
Ilipat ang salmon sa plato, ibuhos ang teriyaki sauce sa pan, at painitin hanggang kumulo.
Ibalik ang salmon sa pan at budburan ng sauce hanggang glossy at bahagyang lumapot; ihain agad na may pan sauce sa ibabaw.
tips: Ang pag-dredge sa isda sa flour bago i-sear ang dahilan kung bakit dumidikit at lumalapot ang sauce sa halip na maging manipis na likido.
fil.kidNote: Mas mataba ang salmon; i-flake ang bawat portion at suriin nang mabuti kung may natitirang pin bones bago ihain sa 6-year-old — karamihan ng bata mahilig sa sweet glaze.
fil.nutritionNote: Magandang source ng omega-3s mula sa salmon, pero mabigat sa asukal at toyo ang glaze; iwasan ang dagdag na toyo sa kanin at ihain kasabay ng plain vegetable side.

recipes.title: Spinach with Sesame Dressing
recipes.localTitle: ほうれん草の胡麻和え (Horenso no Gomaae)
recipes.description: Blanched spinach squeezed dry and tossed in a nutty ground-sesame, soy and sugar dressing — a make-ahead vegetable side and one of the few genuinely low-sodium dishes on the table.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium-high heat, shaking constantly, until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Grind most of the seeds in a mortar and pestle, leaving some whole for texture, then stir in the soy sauce and sugar to make the dressing.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and set an ice bath nearby.
Add the spinach stems first, hold for 20 seconds, then submerge the leaves; cook 30-45 seconds total until just tender.
Plunge the spinach immediately into the ice water to stop the cooking and set the colour.
Squeeze the spinach firmly to remove excess water, then cut into 1-inch lengths.
Toss the spinach with the sesame dressing just before serving.
tips: Squeeze the spinach hard — really hard — or the dressing turns watery and slides off instead of clinging to the leaves.
The dressed spinach keeps 3 days refrigerated, so make a double batch for lunchboxes.
recipes.nutritionNote: One of the few genuinely low-sodium dishes in a washoku spread; lean on it for iron and fibre when the rest of the meal (miso soup, teriyaki) is already salty.

fil.description: Blanched na spinach na piniga hanggang tuyo at tinoss sa malinamnam na ground-sesame, toyo at asukal na dressing — make-ahead na vegetable side at isa sa iilang genuinely low-sodium na ulam sa table.
steps: Toastin ang sesame seeds sa tuyong pan sa medium-high heat, ipagpag nang paulit-ulit, hanggang mabango, mga 1-2 minutes.
Gilingin ang karamihan ng seeds gamit ang mortar and pestle, mag-iwan ng ilan na buo para sa texture, tapos ihalo ang toyo at asukal para sa dressing.
Pakuluin ang maalat na tubig sa pot at maghanda ng ice bath sa tabi.
Isawsaw muna ang tangkay ng spinach, hawakan for 20 seconds, tapos ilubog ang mga dahon; lutuin for 30-45 seconds total hanggang malambot lang.
Isawsaw agad ang spinach sa ice water para itigil ang pagkaluto at ma-set ang kulay.
Pigain nang mabuti ang spinach para matanggal ang sobrang tubig, tapos hiwain nang 1-inch.
I-toss ang spinach sa sesame dressing bago mismo ihain.
tips: Pigain nang husto ang spinach — talagang husto — kung hindi tumutubig ang dressing sa halip na dumikit sa mga dahon.
Tumatagal ng 3 days sa fridge ang dressed spinach, kaya gumawa ng doble para sa baon.
fil.nutritionNote: Isa sa iilang genuinely low-sodium na ulam sa washoku spread; asahan ito para sa iron at fibre lalo na kung maalat na ang ibang ulam (miso soup, teriyaki).

recipes.title: Tamagoyaki
recipes.description: Layers of lightly sweetened egg rolled into a neat rectangle in a small pan — a bento-box staple and often the first dish many Japanese kids learn to help cook.

ingredients.note: or regular soy sauce, using slightly less

ingredients.item: neutral oil, for greasing the pan

steps: In a bowl, combine the eggs, sugar, salt, soy sauce and water; 'cut' through the mixture with chopsticks in a zigzag motion rather than whisking, to avoid incorporating air.
Heat a rectangular tamagoyaki pan (or small frying pan) over medium heat and wipe with an oiled paper towel.
Pour in a thin layer of the egg mixture, tilting the pan to coat evenly, and pop any air bubbles.
Once the bottom sets but the top is still a little wet, roll the egg from the far edge toward you into a log.
Oil the pan again, slide the rolled omelette to the far side, then pour in another thin layer of egg underneath and around it.
Repeat rolling and adding layers until all the egg mixture is used, about 3-4 layers total.
Press the finished roll gently to neaten the shape, then let cool 5 minutes before slicing into 6-8 pieces.
tips: Keep the heat at medium, not high — tamagoyaki should set gently in layers rather than brown or puff.
Wrapping the warm roll in a bamboo sushi mat for a minute helps it hold a neat rectangular shape as it cools.
recipes.nutritionNote: A low-effort, low-sodium protein compared to the rest of a washoku spread (this batch uses only 2 tsp soy sauce across 6 eggs) — a good way to stretch a meal or fill a lunchbox.

fil.description: Layers ng bahagyang matamis na itlog na rolled papuntang neat na rectangle sa maliit na pan — bento-box staple at kadalasan ang unang ulam na natututunan ng maraming batang Hapon na lutuin.
steps: Sa mangkok, ihalo ang itlog, asukal, asin, toyo at tubig; 'gupitin' ang timpla gamit ang chopsticks sa zigzag motion sa halip na batihin, para hindi masyadong pumasok ang hangin.
Painitin ang rectangular na tamagoyaki pan (o maliit na frying pan) sa medium heat at punasan ng oiled paper towel.
Ibuhos ang manipis na layer ng egg mixture, itagilid ang pan para pantay ang pagkalat, at butasin ang mga air bubbles.
Kapag naka-set na ang ilalim pero medyo basa pa ang taas, i-roll ang itlog mula sa malayong gilid papunta sa'yo para gumawa ng log.
Grasahan ulit ang pan, idulas ang rolled omelette sa malayong side, tapos ibuhos ang isa pang manipis na layer ng itlog sa ilalim at paligid nito.
Ulitin ang pag-roll at pagdagdag ng layers hanggang maubos ang egg mixture, mga 3-4 layers total.
Diinan nang bahagya ang tapos na roll para ayusin ang hugis, tapos hayaang lumamig for 5 minutes bago hiwain nang 6-8 pieces.
tips: Panatilihin ang heat sa medium, hindi high — dapat mag-set nang dahan-dahan ang tamagoyaki sa layers sa halip na mag-brown o mamaga.
Ang pagbalot sa warm roll gamit ang bamboo sushi mat for a minute ay tumutulong para hawakan nito ang neat na rectangular shape habang lumalamig.
fil.nutritionNote: Low-effort, low-sodium na protina kumpara sa ibang ulam sa washoku spread (2 tsp lang na toyo ang gamit ng batch na ito para sa 6 na itlog) — magandang paraan para ma-stretch ang meal o punuin ang lunchbox.

recipes.title: Tonjiru
recipes.description: Pork belly and a full pot of root vegetables, konnyaku and tofu simmered in dashi and finished with miso — a heartier, meal-in-a-bowl cousin of miso soup that's substantial enough to be the main dish.

ingredients.item: thinly sliced pork belly, cut into bite-sized pieces
gobo (burdock root), scraped and sliced diagonally, soaked in water 10 minutes
konnyaku block, torn into bite-sized pieces, blanched 2 minutes
soft or medium tofu, torn into large pieces

steps: Cut the pork belly, onion, daikon, carrot and gobo into similar bite-sized pieces; soak the gobo in water 10 minutes to remove bitterness, then drain.
Heat the sesame oil in a large pot over medium heat and stir-fry the pork until no longer pink.
Add the onion, daikon, carrot and gobo; stir-fry 2-3 minutes until the vegetables are coated in the rendered fat.
Add the konnyaku and aburaage, then pour in the dashi; bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat 12-15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Add the tofu and simmer 2 more minutes to warm through.
Ladle a little hot broth into a bowl, dissolve the miso into it, then stir it back into the pot; do not let the soup boil again once the miso is in.
Stir in the grated ginger, ladle into bowls, and garnish with scallion and a shake of shichimi togarashi.
tips: Like nikujaga, tonjiru tastes even better the next day once the root vegetables have fully absorbed the broth.
recipes.nutritionNote: A hearty, vegetable-heavy soup, but the miso and aburaage both add sodium; serve it as the main dish of the meal rather than alongside another salty main like teriyaki or curry.

fil.description: Liempo at buong pot ng root vegetables, konnyaku at tofu na sini-simmer sa dashi tapos tinapos ng miso — isang mas hearty at meal-in-a-bowl na cousin ng miso soup na sapat na maging main dish mismo.
ingredients: thinly sliced na liempo, hiniwa into bite-sized pieces
daikon radish, hiniwa into quarters tapos sliced
carrot, hiniwa into quarters tapos sliced
gobo (burdock root), kinayod at hiniwa diagonally, ibinabad sa tubig for 10 minutes
konnyaku block, pinunit into bite-sized pieces, blanched for 2 minutes
soft o medium tofu, pinunit into large pieces
steps: Hiwain ang liempo, sibuyas, daikon, carrot at gobo into similar bite-sized pieces; ibabad ang gobo sa tubig for 10 minutes para maalis ang pait, tapos i-drain.
Painitin ang sesame oil sa malaking pot over medium heat tapos i-stir-fry ang baboy hanggang wala nang pink.
Idagdag ang sibuyas, daikon, carrot at gobo; i-stir-fry for 2-3 minutes hanggang mabalutan ang gulay ng rendered fat.
Idagdag ang konnyaku at aburaage, tapos ibuhos ang dashi; pakuluin, tinatanggal ang anumang bula.
Takpan tapos i-simmer over medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes hanggang tender ang gulay.
Idagdag ang tofu tapos i-simmer for 2 minutes more para mainit.
Sumandok ng kaunting mainit na broth sa mangkok, tunawin ang miso dito, tapos ihalo pabalik sa pot; huwag nang hayaang kumulo ang soup kapag nasa loob na ang miso.
Ihalo ang grated luya, sumandok papunta sa mangkok, tapos tuktukan ng scallion at kaunting shichimi togarashi.
tips: Tulad ng nikujaga, mas masarap ang tonjiru kinabukasan kapag fully na-absorb na ng root vegetables ang broth.
fil.nutritionNote: Isang hearty at vegetable-heavy na sabaw, pero ang miso at aburaage ay parehong nagdadagdag ng sodium; ihain bilang main dish ng meal sa halip na kasabay ng isa pang maalat na main tulad ng teriyaki o curry.

recipes.title: Yakisoba
recipes.description: Steamed wheat noodles stir-fried with pork belly and cabbage in a sweet-tangy Worcestershire-ketchup sauce — the sizzling griddle food of summer festivals, made in one pan at home.

ingredients.note: or 4 servings fresh chukamen or ramen noodles, blanched and drained

steps: Whisk together the Worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce, ketchup, soy sauce and sugar; taste and adjust the sweetness.
Loosen the noodles with a splash of water or in the microwave, then warm briefly on a hot griddle or in a wok; transfer to a plate.
Cook the pork belly in oil over high heat until no longer pink; season with a little pepper.
Add the onion, then the carrot, stir-frying 1-2 minutes each.
Add the cabbage, shiitake and scallion; stir-fry until the cabbage wilts.
Return the noodles to the pan, pour over the sauce, and toss everything together until evenly coated and glossy.
Serve immediately, topped with aonori and pickled red ginger if using.
tips: Ketchup brands and Worcestershire sauces vary a lot in sweetness and tang between brands — taste the sauce before adding it and adjust with a little extra sugar or soy sauce.
recipes.nutritionNote: The Worcestershire-ketchup sauce is sweet and salty but lighter on sodium than a straight soy sauce dish; load the pan with extra cabbage and carrot so vegetables outweigh the noodles.

fil.description: Steamed na wheat noodles na stir-fried kasama ang pork belly at repolyo sa sweet-tangy Worcestershire-ketchup sauce — ang sizzling griddle food ng summer festivals, ginawa sa isang pan lang sa bahay.
steps: Ihalo ang Worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce, ketchup, toyo at asukal; tikman at i-adjust ang tamis.
Luwagan ang noodles gamit ang kaunting tubig o sa microwave, tapos painitin nang bahagya sa mainit na griddle o wok; ilipat sa plato.
Lutuin ang pork belly sa oil sa high heat hanggang hindi na pink; timplahan ng kaunting paminta.
Idagdag ang sibuyas, tapos ang carrot, stir-fry for 1-2 minutes each.
Idagdag ang repolyo, shiitake at scallion; stir-fry hanggang malanta ang repolyo.
Ibalik ang noodles sa pan, ibuhos ang sauce, at i-toss ang lahat hanggang pantay na na-coat at glossy.
Ihain agad, topan ng aonori at pickled red ginger kung gagamitin.
tips: Iba-iba ang tamis at asim ng ketchup at Worcestershire sauce depende sa brand — tikman muna ang sauce bago idagdag at i-adjust ng dagdag na asukal o toyo.
fil.nutritionNote: Sweet at salty ang Worcestershire-ketchup sauce pero mas mababa sa sodium kaysa straight na toyo dish; punuin ang pan ng extra repolyo at carrot para mas marami ang gulay kaysa noodles.

recipes.title: Zaru Soba
recipes.description: Chewy buckwheat noodles boiled, rinsed and chilled, piled on a bamboo mat and dipped bite by bite into a cold kombu-bonito mentsuyu — the noodle dish Japanese households reach for on the hottest days.

ingredients.item: iced water, for diluting the sauce

ingredients.note: optional; keep off the kids' dipping cups

steps: Bring the sake and mirin to a boil in a small saucepan and simmer 30 seconds to cook off the alcohol.
Add the soy sauce, kombu and katsuobushi; simmer 5 minutes, then remove from heat and let cool completely.
Strain the sauce through a fine sieve, discarding the solids — this is the concentrated mentsuyu; refrigerate until cold.
Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a boil, fan the soba noodles in, and cook per package directions, about 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally to keep them from clumping.
Drain the noodles and rinse under cold running water, rubbing them gently with your hands to wash off the surface starch.
Shock the noodles in a bowl of ice water 30 seconds, then drain thoroughly and pile onto a bamboo mat or plate.
Dilute the concentrated mentsuyu with the iced water in individual dipping cups.
Scatter the noodles with shredded nori and serve with the dipping sauce, scallion and wasabi on the side.
tips: Rinsing and rubbing the boiled noodles under cold water is what gives zaru soba its signature chewy bite — skipping it leaves the noodles starchy and soft.
recipes.kidNote: Keep the wasabi off the kids' dipping cups — the plain mentsuyu and noodles are already a mild, familiar flavour for them.
recipes.nutritionNote: A cool, light noodle dish for hot weather, but the mentsuyu is soy-sauce concentrated; dip rather than pour the sauce over the noodles to control how much sodium each bite gets.

fil.description: Chewy na buckwheat noodles na pinakuluan, binanlawan at pinalamig, itinambak sa bamboo mat tapos isinasawsaw bite by bite sa malamig na kombu-bonito mentsuyu — ang noodle dish na hinahanap ng mga Japanese household sa pinakamainit na araw.
steps: Pakuluin ang sake at mirin sa maliit na saucepan tapos i-simmer for 30 seconds para maluto ang alcohol.
Idagdag ang toyo, kombu at katsuobushi; i-simmer for 5 minutes, tapos alisin sa heat at hayaang lumamig nang buo.
Salain ang sauce sa fine sieve, itapon ang solids — ito ang concentrated mentsuyu; i-refrigerate hanggang lumamig.
Pakuluin ang malaking pot ng unsalted na tubig, ikalat ang soba noodles papasok, tapos lutuin per package directions, mga 4-5 minutes, hinahalo paminsan-minsan para hindi magdikit-dikit.
I-drain ang noodles tapos banlawan sa tumatakbong malamig na tubig, kinukuskos nang dahan-dahan ng kamay para matanggal ang surface starch.
I-shock ang noodles sa mangkok ng ice water for 30 seconds, tapos i-drain nang maigi at itambak sa bamboo mat o plato.
I-dilute ang concentrated mentsuyu ng iced water sa individual dipping cups.
