ingredients.note: ask the butcher for outer skirt steak; flank steak is an easy substitute

ingredients.item: white onion, thickly sliced into rounds, for grilling

ingredients.note: sold frozen at Mexican/international grocers in Manila

ingredients.item: lime, cut into wedges, for serving

steps: Roast the unpeeled garlic cloves in a dry skillet over medium heat, turning often, until the skins are blotchy black and the cloves feel soft, about 10 minutes; cool, then peel.
Blend the roasted garlic with the lime juice, oil, oregano, salt and pepper into a loose marinade.
Pour half the marinade over the steak in a shallow dish, turning to coat, and let it sit at room temperature 20-30 minutes; reserve the other half.
Heat a charcoal or gas grill, or a heavy griddle pan, until very hot.
Grill the steak and onion rounds directly over the heat, about 3-4 minutes per side for the steak, until charred outside and still pink in the middle.
Rest the steak on a cutting board 5 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Drizzle the sliced steak with the reserved marinade and serve with the grilled onions, warm corn tortillas and lime wedges.
tips: If marinating longer than 30 minutes, refrigerate the steak; lime juice starts to firm up the meat's surface if left too long at room temperature.
No grill? A cast-iron griddle screaming hot on the stovetop gets a very close result indoors.
recipes.nutritionNote: A good source of iron and protein; balance the fattier cut with extra grilled vegetables or a side salad, and keep tortilla portions modest for younger kids.

fil.description: Garlicky lime-marinated skirt steak na iginrill nang mainit at mabilis, tapos hiniwa nang manipis against the grain, ito ang backbone ng northern Mexican asada gatherings na sinasabayan ng tortillas at salsa.
ingredients: fresh lime juice, mga 4 na lime
white onion, hiniwa nang makapal into rounds, pang-grill
steps: I-roast ang bawang na may balat pa sa dry skillet sa medium heat, baliktarin paminsan-minsan, hanggang mag-itim-itim ang balat at lumambot ang laman, mga 10 minutes; palamigin, tapos balatan.
I-blend ang roasted garlic with lime juice, oil, oregano, asin at paminta para maging loose marinade.
Ibuhos ang kalahati ng marinade sa steak sa shallow dish, i-toss para mabalutan, tapos hayaang maupo sa room temperature for 20-30 minutes; itabi ang kalahati.
Painitin ang charcoal o gas grill, o heavy griddle pan, hanggang sumingaw ang init.
I-grill ang steak at onion rounds directly sa apoy, mga 3-4 minutes per side para sa steak, hanggang mag-char sa labas pero pink pa rin sa gitna.
Ipahinga ang steak sa cutting board for 5 minutes, tapos hiwain nang manipis against the grain.
Budburan ng itinabing marinade ang hiniwang steak tapos ihain kasama ng grilled onions, warm corn tortillas at lime wedges.
tips: Kung mag-marinate ng mas matagal sa 30 minutes, ilagay sa fridge ang steak; nagsisimula kasing tumigas ang surface ng karne kapag matagal sa room temperature ang lime juice.
Walang grill? Ang cast-iron griddle na sobrang init sa stovetop ay malapit na malapit ang resulta kahit indoors.
fil.nutritionNote: Magandang source ng iron at protein; i-balance ang fattier cut with extra grilled vegetables o side salad, tapos konti lang ang tortilla portions para sa mas batang kids.

recipes.title: Cheese-Stuffed Poblano Chiles
recipes.description: Roasted poblano peppers stuffed with melting cheese, dipped in a fluffy egg batter and fried golden, then simmered briefly in a light tomato sauce, a Puebla classic that is mild, not fiery.

ingredients.note: poblano is a mild chile; large green bell pepper is a milder, less authentic stand-in if unavailable

ingredients.item: queso fresco or Oaxaca cheese, cut into strips

ingredients.note: dried guajillo and ancho chiles are available from Mexican specialty importers online in Manila

steps: Char the poblanos directly over a gas flame or under a hot broiler, turning until the skins blister black all over.
Seal the charred peppers in a plastic bag for 10 minutes to steam, then rub off the blackened skin under cool running water.
Slit each pepper lengthwise, leaving the stem intact, remove the seeds and veins, pat dry, and stuff generously with cheese strips.
For the sauce, boil the guajillo and ancho chiles 5 minutes to soften, then blend with the tomatoes, garlic, onion, broth and oregano until smooth; simmer 10 minutes and keep warm.
Beat the egg whites with the salt to soft peaks, then fold in the yolks to make a light batter.
Dust each stuffed pepper in flour, then dip fully in the egg batter to coat.
Fry in hot oil, turning once, until puffed and golden on all sides, about 3-4 minutes total; drain on paper towels.
Serve the fried chiles warm, napped with the tomato sauce.
tips: Keep a toothpick or two in the slit if the pepper wants to gape open; it holds the cheese in during frying.
Work with room-temperature cheese sticks so they melt through by the time the batter turns golden, without leaking out entirely.
recipes.nutritionNote: This is a fried, cheese-forward dish; balance the plate with the tomato sauce's vegetables and a side of rice or beans rather than more fried food.

source.name: My Latina Table (method cross-checked against Mely Martinez's Chile Relleno recipe on Mexico in My Kitchen)

fil.description: Roasted poblano peppers na pinuno ng cheese na natutunaw, ni-dip sa fluffy egg batter tapos pinirito hanggang golden, saka ni-simmer nang sandali sa light tomato sauce, isang Puebla classic na hindi maanghang, mild lang.
ingredients: queso fresco o Oaxaca cheese, hiniwa into strips
itlog, hiniwalay ang puti at pula
steps: I-char ang poblanos directly sa gas flame o sa ilalim ng hot broiler, baliktarin hanggang mag-itim at mag-blister ang balat sa lahat ng parte.
Ilagay ang charred peppers sa plastic bag for 10 minutes para ma-steam, tapos kuskusin ang itim na balat sa ilalim ng cool running water.
Gupitin nang paayon ang bawat pepper, iwan ang tangkay, alisin ang buto at veins, patuyuin, tapos punuin nang husto ng cheese strips.

Para sa sauce, pakuluan ang guajillo at ancho chiles for 5 minutes hanggang lumambot, tapos i-blend with tomatoes, garlic, onion, broth at oregano hanggang smooth; i-simmer for 10 minutes tapos panatilihing mainit.
Batihin ang egg whites with asin hanggang mag-soft peaks, tapos ihalo ang yolks para maging light batter.
I-dust ang bawat stuffed pepper sa flour, tapos i-dip nang husto sa egg batter para mabalutan.
Iprito sa hot oil, baliktarin isang beses, hanggang mag-puff at mag-golden sa lahat ng gilid, mga 3-4 minutes total; i-drain sa paper towels.
Ihain ang fried chiles habang mainit, binuhusan ng tomato sauce.
tips: Maglagay ng toothpick sa slit kung gustong bumuka ang pepper; nakakapigil ito sa cheese habang pinipirito.
Gamitin ang cheese sticks na room-temperature para matunaw nang tama sa oras na mag-golden na ang batter, nang hindi lumalabas nang tuluyan.
fil.nutritionNote: Fried at cheese-forward na dish ito; i-balance ang plato with vegetables ng tomato sauce at side ng rice o beans instead na mas maraming fried food.

recipes.title: Chicken in Green Pumpkin Seed Sauce
recipes.description: Chicken simmered in a bright green sauce of toasted pumpkin seeds, tomatillos and roasted poblano, a nutty central-Mexican pipián that tastes earthy and herbal rather than fiery.

ingredients.item: white onion, half quartered for poaching and half chopped for the sauce
garlic, divided (2 whole for poaching, 3 for the sauce)

ingredients.note: sold raw and shelled at health-food or baking-supply stores in Manila; do not use salted roasted pepitas

ingredients.item: poblano pepper, roasted, peeled and seeded
ingredients.note: green bell pepper is a milder, less authentic stand-in if poblano is unavailable
for a milder family pot, omit and pass hot sauce at the table
a traditional thickener for the sauce

steps: Poach the chicken in the water with the quartered onion half and 2 whole garlic cloves, 25-30 minutes until cooked through; lift out the chicken and reserve 2 cups of the broth.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until they puff and start to pop, 4-5 minutes; watch closely so they don't scorch, then cool.
Simmer the tomatillos and serrano in a small pot of water 8-10 minutes until they turn from bright to olive green and soften; drain.
Blend the toasted pumpkin seeds, cooked tomatillos and serrano, roasted poblano, chopped onion, remaining garlic, romaine, cilantro and 1.5 cups of the reserved broth until completely smooth.
Heat the lard in a wide pot over medium heat, pour in the blended sauce carefully as it will spatter, and stir constantly for the first 3-4 minutes so it doesn't scorch or split.
Simmer the sauce uncovered, stirring occasionally, 10-12 minutes until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon and deepens to olive green.
Add the chicken pieces, season with salt, cover and simmer gently 10 minutes to heat through without letting the sauce boil hard.
Serve hot over rice with lime wedges.
tips: Keep the heat gentle once the sauce is in the pot; pumpkin-seed sauces can split into oil and solids if boiled hard.
Toast the pepitas slowly over low heat, they turn bitter if scorched.
recipes.nutritionNote: Pumpkin seeds add plant protein, iron and healthy fats to the lean chicken; serve with rice or corn tortillas and skip extra oil since the sauce is already rich.

source.name: Mexico in My Kitchen (Mely Martinez, Mole Verde / Pipián Verde)

fil.description: Manok na ni-simmer sa maberdeng sauce ng toasted pumpkin seeds, tomatillos at roasted poblano, isang malasa at herbal na central-Mexican pipián na hindi naman ganoon kaanghang.
ingredients: hita at paa ng manok, may buto
white onion, kalahati quartered pang-poach at kalahati chopped para sa sauce
bawang, hatiin (2 buo pang-poach, 3 para sa sauce)
poblano pepper, inihaw, binalatan at inalisan ng buto
steps: I-poach ang manok sa tubig kasama ang quartered onion half at 2 whole garlic cloves, 25-30 minutes hanggang maluto; alisin ang manok at itabi ang 2 cups ng broth.
I-toast ang pumpkin seeds sa dry skillet sa medium-low heat, haluin nang patuloy, hanggang lumaki at magsimulang pumutok, 4-5 minutes; bantayan nang mabuti para hindi masunog, tapos palamigin.
I-simmer ang tomatillos at serrano sa maliit na pot ng tubig for 8-10 minutes hanggang mag-olive green mula sa bright green at lumambot; i-drain.
I-blend ang toasted pumpkin seeds, cooked tomatillos at serrano, roasted poblano, chopped onion, natitirang bawang, romaine, cilantro at 1.5 cups ng reserved broth hanggang maging completely smooth.
Painitin ang lard sa wide pot sa medium heat, ibuhos ang blended sauce nang mabagal kasi mag-splatter ito, at haluin nang patuloy for the first 3-4 minutes para hindi masunog o mag-split.
I-simmer ang sauce nang walang takip, haluin paminsan-minsan, 10-12 minutes hanggang lumapot enough para ma-coat ang likod ng spoon at maging olive green.
Idagdag ang chicken pieces, timplahan ng asin, takpan at i-simmer nang mahinay for 10 minutes para uminit without letting the sauce boil hard.
Ihain mainit over rice na may lime wedges.
tips: Panatilihing mahinay ang apoy once nasa pot na ang sauce; pwedeng mag-split ang pumpkin-seed sauce into oil and solids kapag pinakuluan nang malakas.
I-toast ang pepitas nang mabagal sa low heat, kasi mapapait ito kapag na-scorch.
fil.nutritionNote: Nagdadagdag ang pumpkin seeds ng plant protein, iron at healthy fats sa lean chicken; ihain with rice o corn tortillas at wag nang magdagdag ng oil kasi mayaman na ang sauce.

recipes.title: Chicken Tinga
recipes.description: Shredded chicken simmered in a smoky chipotle-tomato sauce with soft onions, a Puebla home-kitchen staple used to fill tacos, tostadas and tortas across central Mexico.

ingredients.item: white onion, half quartered for poaching and half thinly sliced for the saute
garlic, divided (2 whole for poaching, 2 minced for the sauce)
canned chipotle peppers in adobo, finely chopped
ingredients.note: sold in small cans at Mexican/international aisles or online specialty groceries in Manila; use 1 tbsp for a milder household batch
to taste; or a mild farmer's cheese if queso fresco isn't available

steps: Place the chicken in a pot with the water, the quartered half-onion and 2 whole garlic cloves; bring to a boil, then simmer 20 minutes until cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, reserve 1 cup of the poaching broth, and once cool enough to handle, shred the meat into bite-sized strips.
Blend the tomatoes, chipotles in adobo, remaining 2 garlic cloves, oregano, black pepper and the reserved broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium-low heat and cook the sliced onion until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the blended sauce, raise the heat to medium and simmer uncovered 5-7 minutes until it darkens and thickens slightly.
Lower the heat, stir in the shredded chicken, cover and simmer 15-20 minutes until the sauce clings to the meat rather than pooling underneath.
Season with salt and serve warm over tostadas or folded into warm corn tortillas with crumbled queso fresco and avocado.
tips: Start with 1 tablespoon of chipotle for a mild family batch and pass extra chopped chipotle at the table for adults who want more heat.
Tinga tastes even better the next day; make it ahead and reheat gently with a splash of broth.
recipes.nutritionNote: Lean protein from chicken balanced by tomato; go easy on the oil and pair with a lime-dressed cabbage slaw or extra vegetables since the dish itself is light on fiber.

source.name: Mexican Food Journal (method verified against Mely Martinez's Chicken Tinga on Mexico in My Kitchen)

fil.description: Shredded chicken na ni-simmer sa smoky chipotle-tomato sauce with soft onions, isang Puebla home-kitchen staple na ginagamit pantapal ng tacos, tostadas at tortas sa buong central Mexico.
ingredients: hitang walang buto o breast ng manok
white onion, kalahati hiniwa nang malaki para sa poaching at kalahati hiniwa nang manipis para sa saute
bawang, hinati (2 buo para sa poaching, 2 tinadtad para sa sauce)
de-latang chipotle peppers in adobo, tinadtad nang pino
chicken broth, itinabi mula sa poaching
steps: Ilagay ang manok sa pot kasama ang tubig, yung kalahating onion na hiniwa nang malaki, at 2 buong garlic cloves; pakuluin, tapos i-simmer for 20 minutes hanggang maluto.
Alisin ang manok sa pot, itabi ang 1 cup ng broth, tapos pag medyo lamig na, i-shred ang karne into bite-sized strips.
I-blend ang tomatoes, chipotles in adobo, natitirang 2 garlic cloves, oregano, paminta at yung itinabing broth hanggang maging smooth.
Painitin ang oil sa wide skillet sa medium-low heat, tapos lutuin yung hiniwang onion hanggang lumambot at maging translucent, mga 5 minutes.
Ibuhos ang blended sauce, taasan ang heat to medium, tapos i-simmer nang bukas for 5-7 minutes hanggang dumilim at lumapot nang kaunti.
Hinaan ang heat, ihalo yung shredded chicken, takpan tapos i-simmer for 15-20 minutes hanggang dumikit ang sauce sa karne instead na naiipon lang sa ilalim.
Timplahan ng asin tapos ihain habang mainit sa ibabaw ng tostadas o nakabalot sa warm corn tortillas na may queso fresco at avocado.
tips: Magsimula sa 1 tablespoon ng chipotle para sa mild family batch, tapos maglagay na lang ng extra chopped chipotle sa table para sa mga adults na gustong maanghang.
Mas masarap pa ang tinga kinabukasan; pwede itong lutuin nang maaga tapos i-reheat lang nang dahan-dahan with a splash of broth.
fil.nutritionNote: Lean protein galing sa manok, balanced ng tomato; konti lang sa oil, tapos isabay sa lime-dressed cabbage slaw o extra vegetables dahil mababa ang fiber ng dish mismo.

recipes.title: Cochinita Pibil
recipes.description: Pork shoulder marinated in tangy achiote and sour orange, wrapped in banana leaf and slow-roasted until it shreds with a fork, Yucatan's signature pit-style barbacoa adapted for a home oven.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into large chunks

ingredients.note: sold as achiote paste or recado rojo at Latin grocers; order online if unavailable in Manila, do not substitute plain paprika
or mix 3 parts regular orange juice to 1 part lime juice plus a splash of vinegar

ingredients.item: banana leaves, softened over a flame
ingredients.note: widely available fresh or frozen in Manila; or line the dish with parchment and foil if unavailable

ingredients.item: red onion, thinly sliced and pickled in lime juice

ingredients.note: serve on the side only, keep off the kids' plates entirely

steps: Blend the achiote paste, sour orange juice, lime juice, onion, garlic, salt and cumin into a smooth, brick-red marinade.
Coat the pork chunks thoroughly in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight.
Soften the banana leaves briefly over an open flame or in a hot dry pan until pliable, then use them to line a deep baking dish, letting the edges hang over the sides.
Pour the marinated pork and all its liquid into the lined dish, then fold the banana leaf edges over the top to fully enclose the meat.
Cover tightly with foil and bake at 165C (325F) for about 3.5 hours, until the pork shreds easily with two forks.
Uncover, shred the pork directly in its juices, and stir in enough cooking liquid to keep it moist but not soupy.
Serve wrapped in warm corn tortillas, topped with pickled red onion, with sliced habanero on the side for anyone who wants extra heat.
tips: The pork must marinate at least 6 hours, overnight is better, for the achiote and citrus to fully penetrate; plan the day before.
No banana leaves is fine; the dish loses a little earthiness but the achiote and slow roasting still deliver the classic flavor.
recipes.nutritionNote: Pork shoulder is fattier than loin, so trim visible fat before marinating and serve with the pickled onion and extra shredded cabbage for acidity and fiber.

source.name: Isabel Eats (method cross-checked against Mely Martinez's Cochinita Pibil on Mexico in My Kitchen)

fil.description: Pork shoulder na ni-marinate sa tangy achiote at sour orange, binalot sa banana leaf tapos slow-roasted hanggang mag-shred na lang gamit ang fork, ito ang signature pit-style barbacoa ng Yucatan na in-adapt para sa home oven.
ingredients: pork shoulder, hiniwa into large chunks
red onion, hiniwa nang manipis at pinickle sa lime juice
steps: I-blend ang achiote paste, sour orange juice, lime juice, onion, bawang, asin at cumin para maging smooth, brick-red na marinade.
Ibalot nang husto ang pork chunks sa marinade, takpan, tapos ipa-fridge for at least 6 hours o overnight.
Palambutin nang sandali ang banana leaves sa apoy o sa hot dry pan hanggang maging pliable, tapos gamitin para i-line ang deep baking dish, hayaang lumabas ang edges sa gilid.
Ibuhos ang marinated pork at lahat ng liquid nito sa lined dish, tapos tiklupin ang edges ng banana leaf sa ibabaw para mabalot nang husto ang karne.
Takpan nang mahigpit ng foil tapos i-bake at 165C (325F) for about 3.5 hours, hanggang mag-shred nang madali ang pork gamit ang two forks.
Alisin ang takip, i-shred ang pork directly sa juices nito, tapos ihalo ang sapat na cooking liquid para manatiling moist pero hindi soupy.
Ihain nakabalot sa warm corn tortillas, top ng pickled red onion, may sliced habanero sa tabi para sa sinumang gustong magdagdag ng anghang.
tips: Dapat mag-marinate ang pork for at least 6 hours, mas maganda kung overnight, para tumagos nang husto ang achiote at citrus; i-plan bago ang araw na lulutuin.
Okay lang kung walang banana leaves; medyo mawawala ang earthiness pero ang achiote at slow roasting ay sapat pa rin para sa classic flavor.
fil.nutritionNote: Mas mataba ang pork shoulder kumpara sa loin, kaya tanggalin ang visible fat bago mag-marinate tapos ihain with pickled onion at extra shredded cabbage para sa acidity at fiber.

recipes.title: Crispy Rolled Chicken Tacos
recipes.description: Corn tortillas rolled tight around shredded chicken and fried until crackling-crisp, then finished with crema, salsa and queso fresco, festive party food that disappears fast at kids' birthdays.

ingredients.note: warm before rolling so they don't crack
optional; keeps rolls from unraveling while frying
or sour cream thinned with a little milk

ingredients.item: salsa, red or green, served on the side
ingredients.note: keep chile out of the kids' portion; offer salsa as a table condiment so each person adds their own heat

steps: Poach the chicken in the water with onion, garlic and salt 20 minutes until cooked through; cool and shred finely.
Warm the tortillas briefly on a dry griddle or wrapped in a damp towel so they roll without cracking.
Place 2-3 tablespoons of shredded chicken along one edge of each tortilla, roll tightly into a cigar shape, and secure with a toothpick if needed.
Heat 1.5 cups oil in a deep skillet to 180C (350F).
Fry the flautas in batches, seam-side down first, turning occasionally, until golden and crisp all over, 3-4 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and remove the toothpicks.
Pile onto a platter over shredded lettuce and top with crema, queso fresco and diced tomato.
Serve immediately with salsa on the side so each person adds their own.
tips: Frying seam-side down first helps seal the roll before it can unravel in the oil.
Fry in small batches so the oil temperature doesn't drop, which keeps the tortillas crisp rather than greasy.
recipes.nutritionNote: A fried, crowd-pleasing party dish; balance the plate with the lettuce and tomato garnish and a side of beans rather than more fried food.

fil.description: Corn tortillas na ni-roll nang mahigpit sa shredded chicken at pinrito hanggang crackling-crisp, tapos finished with crema, salsa at queso fresco, festive party food na mabilis maubos sa birthday ng mga bata.
ingredients: salsa, red o green, ihahain sa tabi
steps: I-poach ang manok sa tubig kasama ang onion, bawang at asin for 20 minutes hanggang maluto; palamigin at i-shred nang pino.
Painitin nang kaunti ang tortillas sa dry griddle o balutin ng damp towel para hindi mabasag habang niro-roll.
Ilagay ang 2-3 tablespoons ng shredded chicken sa isang gilid ng bawat tortilla, i-roll nang mahigpit into cigar shape, at tali ng toothpick kung kailangan.
Painitin ang 1.5 cups oil sa deep skillet to 180C (350F).
I-fry ang flautas in batches, seam-side down muna, i-turn paminsan-minsan, hanggang golden at crisp all over, 3-4 minutes per batch.
I-drain sa paper towels at alisin ang toothpicks.
Ilagay sa platter over shredded lettuce at topping ng crema, queso fresco at diced tomato.
Ihain agad with salsa sa tabi para bawat isa maglagay ng sarili nilang heat.
tips: Nakakatulong ang pag-fry seam-side down muna para ma-seal ang roll bago pa mag-unravel sa oil.
I-fry in small batches para hindi bumaba ang temperature ng oil, para manatiling crisp ang tortillas kesa maging greasy.
fil.nutritionNote: Fried, crowd-pleasing party dish; i-balance ang plate with lettuce at tomato garnish at side ng beans kesa magdagdag pa ng fried food.

recipes.title: Deviled Shrimp
recipes.description: Jumbo shrimp seared then bathed in a fiery guajillo and chile de arbol sauce, a beach-shack classic from the Pacific and Gulf coasts named for its glossy red heat.

ingredients.item: large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails on

ingredients.note: dried guajillo chiles are sold at Mexican/specialty grocers online in Manila; buy extra, they keep well dried
this is where the real heat lives, omit entirely for the kids' batch and add back only for the adults' pot

ingredients.item: water, for soaking chiles and blending

steps: Season the shrimp with salt and refrigerate while you make the sauce.
Toast the guajillo and arbol chiles briefly in a dry pan until fragrant, then cover with hot water and soak 15-20 minutes until soft; drain.
Blend the softened chiles with the tomatoes, garlic, cumin, onion and 1 cup fresh water until completely smooth.
For a kid-friendly batch, blend a second small portion of sauce using only the guajillo chiles, no arbol, and cook a portion of shrimp in that instead.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sear the shrimp about 1 minute per side, until just starting to turn pink; remove and set aside.
Pour the chile sauce into the same skillet, bring to a simmer, and cook 5 minutes until slightly thickened, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the shrimp to the skillet and toss to coat, cooking just 1-2 minutes more until opaque; do not overcook or the shrimp turn rubbery.
Scatter with cilantro and serve immediately with lime wedges, rice and warm tortillas.
tips: Buy the shrimp already peeled and deveined to keep this a genuine 30-minute weeknight dish.
Toasting the dried chiles 30 seconds per side before soaking deepens the flavor; watch closely, they burn fast.
recipes.kidNote: Blend a separate batch of sauce with guajillo only (no chile de arbol) for the kids' shrimp, and keep the arbol-spiked version in its own pan for the adults so everyone's plate matches their own heat tolerance.
recipes.nutritionNote: Shrimp is lean and high in protein; the sauce is chile-forward rather than creamy, so this pairs well with rice and a simple salad without adding much extra fat.

fil.description: Jumbo shrimp na ni-sear tapos binuhusan ng fiery guajillo at chile de arbol sauce, isang beach-shack classic mula sa Pacific at Gulf coasts na pinangalanan dahil sa glossy red heat nito.
ingredients: malaking shrimp, balat na tinanggal at de-vein, may tail
guajillo chiles, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
chile de arbol, tinanggalan ng tangkay
tubig, pambabad ng chiles at pang-blend
steps: Timplahan ang shrimp ng asin tapos ipa-fridge habang ginagawa ang sauce.
I-toast nang sandali ang guajillo at arbol chiles sa dry pan hanggang umamoy maganda, tapos takpan ng hot water at ibabad for 15-20 minutes hanggang lumambot; i-drain.
I-blend ang softened chiles with tomatoes, garlic, cumin, onion at 1 cup fresh water hanggang maging completely smooth.
Para sa kid-friendly batch, mag-blend ng second small portion ng sauce gamit lang ang guajillo chiles, walang arbol, tapos lutuin doon ang portion ng shrimp para sa mga bata.
I-melt ang butter sa large skillet sa medium-high heat tapos i-sear ang shrimp mga 1 minute per side, hanggang magsimulang mag-pink; alisin at itabi.
Ibuhos ang chile sauce sa parehong skillet, pakuluin nang bahagya, tapos lutuin for 5 minutes hanggang lumapot nang kaunti, kinakayod ang browned bits sa ilalim.
Ibalik ang shrimp sa skillet tapos i-toss para mabalutan, lutuin lang ng 1-2 minutes more hanggang maging opaque; wag i-overcook para hindi mag-rubbery ang shrimp.
Budburan ng cilantro tapos ihaing agad with lime wedges, rice at warm tortillas.
tips: Bumili na lang ng shrimp na peeled and deveined na para manatiling totoong 30-minute weeknight dish ito.
Ang pag-toast ng dried chiles for 30 seconds per side bago ibabad ay nagpapalalim ng lasa; bantayan nang mabuti, mabilis kasi itong masunog.
fil.kidNote: Mag-blend ng separate batch ng sauce na guajillo lang (walang chile de arbol) para sa shrimp ng mga bata, tapos itago ang bersyon na may arbol sa sarili nitong pan para sa adults, para bawat isa ay may sariling level ng anghang.
fil.nutritionNote: Ang shrimp ay lean at mataas sa protein; ang sauce ay chile-forward instead na creamy, kaya bagay itong isabay sa rice at simple salad nang hindi nagdadagdag ng sobrang taba.

recipes.title: Garlic Shrimp
recipes.description: Shrimp seared fast in butter and a generous amount of garlic until golden and glossy, a coastal Mexican classic that comes together in the time it takes to cook rice.

ingredients.item: large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails on

ingredients.note: yes, this much; the dish is meant to be heavily garlicky

ingredients.item: dried guajillo chile, seeded and thinly sliced
ingredients.note: optional, for color and mild warmth; omit entirely for the mildest version

steps: Season the shrimp with salt and set aside.
Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the minced garlic and sliced guajillo, if using, and cook gently 1-2 minutes, stirring, until the garlic turns pale golden; watch closely, burnt garlic turns bitter.
Raise the heat to medium-high, add the shrimp in a single layer, and cook undisturbed 1-2 minutes until pink on the bottom.
Flip the shrimp and cook 1-2 minutes more until just opaque all the way through; do not overcook or they turn rubbery.
Remove from heat, stir in the lime juice, and toss to coat.
Scatter with parsley and serve immediately with lime wedges, rice and warm tortillas.
tips: Keep the garlic moving in the butter so it toasts evenly without burning.
Buy shrimp already peeled and deveined to keep this a genuine weeknight dish.
recipes.nutritionNote: Shrimp is lean and high in protein; this dish leans buttery, so balance the plate with rice, a green salad or steamed vegetables rather than more fat.

fil.description: Shrimp na ginisa nang mabilis sa butter at maraming-marami bawang hanggang golden at makintab, isang coastal Mexican classic na matatapos sa oras lang na iluto mo ang rice.
ingredients: malaking shrimp, binalatan at inalisan ng ugat, may tail
dried guajillo chile, inalisan ng buto at hiwain nang manipis
tinadtad na fresh parsley o cilantro
steps: Timplahan ang shrimp ng asin at itabi.
Tunawin ang butter with olive oil sa large skillet sa medium heat.
Idagdag ang minced garlic at sliced guajillo, kung gagamitin, at lutuin nang mahinay for 1-2 minutes, haluin, hanggang mag-pale golden ang bawang; bantayan nang mabuti, mapapait ang sunog na bawang.
Lakasan ang apoy to medium-high, ilagay ang shrimp in a single layer, at lutuin nang wag gagalawin for 1-2 minutes hanggang mag-pink sa ilalim.
I-flip ang shrimp at lutuin for 1-2 minutes more hanggang maluto through; wag i-overcook kundi magiging rubbery ito.
Alisin sa apoy, ihalo ang lime juice, at i-toss para mabalutan.
Budburan ng parsley at ihain agad with lime wedges, rice at warm tortillas.
tips: Panatilihing gumagalaw ang bawang sa butter para mag-toast nang pantay without masunog.
Bumili ng shrimp na peeled and deveined na para manatiling genuine weeknight dish ito.
fil.nutritionNote: Lean at high-protein ang shrimp; medyo buttery ang dish na ito, kaya i-balance ang plato with rice, green salad o steamed vegetables kesa dagdag pang taba.

recipes.title: Green Chilaquiles
recipes.description: Fried tortilla chips simmered briefly in a tangy tomatillo-serrano salsa until just softened, topped with crema, queso fresco and a fried egg, the classic Mexican breakfast for using up yesterday's tortillas.

ingredients.note: or 1 pack (200 g) plain tortilla chips; day-old tortillas fried at home give the most authentic texture
use 1, or deseed, for a milder pot; blend a small chile-free portion of sauce separately for the kids and keep the fuller-heat batch for the adults
or sour cream thinned with milk

steps: If frying your own tortillas, cut into wedges and fry in batches in hot oil until crisp and golden; drain on paper towels. Skip this step if using store-bought chips.
Simmer the tomatillos and serrano chiles in a pot of water 10-12 minutes until they turn from bright to olive green and soften.
Blend the cooked tomatillos and chiles with the garlic, onion, cilantro, water and salt until smooth.
Pour the salsa into a wide skillet and simmer 5 minutes until it thickens slightly and loses its raw taste.
Add the tortilla chips to the skillet and gently fold them into the sauce, cooking just 1-2 minutes so they soften slightly but keep some bite; do not let them sit or they turn mushy.
Divide among plates immediately and top with a fried egg, queso fresco, crema and sliced onion.
tips: Chilaquiles wait for no one, fold the chips into the sauce only right before serving.
Make the salsa verde ahead and refrigerate it, then the dish comes together in minutes on a busy morning.
recipes.kidNote: Blend a small batch of the tomatillo sauce with just 1 seeded serrano (or none) for the kids' portion, and keep the fuller-heat sauce in a separate pan for the adults so each plate matches its own heat tolerance.
recipes.nutritionNote: Pair with a fried or scrambled egg for protein since the dish itself is mostly carbohydrate and fried tortilla; go light on the crema if serving often.

fil.description: Fried tortilla chips na ni-simmer nang saglit sa tangy tomatillo-serrano salsa hanggang lumambot lang nang kaunti, topped with crema, queso fresco at pritong itlog, ang classic Mexican breakfast para maubos ang tortillas kahapon.
steps: Kung magpi-prito ng sariling tortillas, hiwain into wedges at i-fry in batches sa hot oil hanggang crisp at golden; i-drain sa paper towels. Laktawan ang step na ito kung gagamit ng store-bought chips.
I-simmer ang tomatillos at serrano chiles sa pot ng tubig for 10-12 minutes hanggang mag-olive green mula sa bright at lumambot.
I-blend ang cooked tomatillos at chiles with bawang, onion, cilantro, tubig at asin hanggang smooth.
Ibuhos ang salsa sa wide skillet at i-simmer for 5 minutes hanggang lumapot nang kaunti at mawala ang raw taste.
Idagdag ang tortilla chips sa skillet at ihalo nang dahan-dahan sa sauce, lutuin lang 1-2 minutes para lumambot nang kaunti pero may bite pa rin; wag hayaang tumagal o magiging mushy ito.
Hatiin sa plato agad at topping ng fried egg, queso fresco, crema at sliced onion.
tips: Hindi naghihintay ang chilaquiles, ihalo lang ang chips sa sauce right before serving.
Gawin ang salsa verde ahead of time at i-refrigerate, tapos matatapos ang dish in minutes on a busy morning.
fil.kidNote: I-blend ang maliit na batch ng tomatillo sauce na may 1 seeded serrano lang (or wala talaga) para sa share ng mga bata, tapos itabi ang mas maanghang na sauce sa ibang pan para sa mga adults, para tugma sa heat tolerance ng bawat isa ang plato.
fil.nutritionNote: I-pair with fried o scrambled egg for protein kasi mostly carbohydrate at fried tortilla ang dish; konti lang sa crema kung madalas i-serve ito.

recipes.title: Green Enchiladas
recipes.description: Corn tortillas filled with shredded chicken, bathed in a bright tomatillo-serrano salsa and crema, then baked with melted cheese, central Mexico's classic Sunday-lunch enchilada.

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs

ingredients.note: sold at some specialty grocers and online in Manila; or substitute drained canned tomatillos
use up to 2 for more heat, or deseed for milder
or sour cream thinned with a little milk

ingredients.item: queso fresco or Oaxaca cheese, crumbled or shredded

steps: Poach the chicken in a pot of water until cooked through, about 15-20 minutes; cool and shred into bite-sized pieces.
Simmer the tomatillos, serrano and garlic in the water for about 15 minutes until the tomatillos turn from bright to olive green and are soft.
Blend the cooked tomatillos, chile and garlic with the onion, 1 cup of the cooking water, crema and cilantro until smooth.
Warm a little oil in a skillet and quickly dip each tortilla a few seconds per side to soften without crisping.
Fill each tortilla with shredded chicken, roll it up, and lay seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the tomatillo-crema sauce evenly over the rolled enchiladas and scatter cheese on top.
Bake at 180C (350F) for 15-20 minutes until the cheese melts and the sauce bubbles at the edges.
Drizzle with extra crema, scatter sliced onion, and serve immediately while the tortillas are still tender.
tips: Dip, don't soak, the tortillas in warm oil; a few seconds keeps them pliable without turning greasy.
Assemble and refrigerate a few hours ahead, then bake just before serving so the tortillas don't go soggy.
recipes.nutritionNote: The crema and cheese add richness, so balance the plate with a simple side salad or extra shredded lettuce and tomato rather than more cheese.

source.name: The Kitchn (Mely Martinez's Enchiladas Verdes, from The Mexican Home Kitchen)

fil.description: Corn tortillas na pinuno ng shredded chicken, binuhusan ng bright tomatillo-serrano salsa at crema, tapos binake with melted cheese, ito ang classic Sunday-lunch enchilada ng central Mexico.
ingredients: chicken breast o thighs, walang buto at balat
tomatillos, tinanggalan ng husk at hinugasan
queso fresco o Oaxaca cheese, dinurog o kinudkod
steps: I-poach ang manok sa pot ng tubig hanggang maluto, mga 15-20 minutes; palamigin tapos i-shred into bite-sized pieces.
I-simmer ang tomatillos, serrano at bawang sa tubig for about 15 minutes hanggang mag-olive green ang tomatillos mula bright green at lumambot.
I-blend ang niluto na tomatillos, chile at bawang with onion, 1 cup ng cooking water, crema at cilantro hanggang maging smooth.
Painitin ang kaunting oil sa skillet tapos i-dip nang mabilis ang bawat tortilla ng ilang seconds per side para lumambot nang hindi crispy.
Punuin ang bawat tortilla ng shredded chicken, i-roll, tapos ilagay nang seam-side down sa baking dish.
Ibuhos nang pantay ang tomatillo-crema sauce sa ibabaw ng rolled enchiladas tapos budburan ng cheese sa ibabaw.
I-bake at 180C (350F) for 15-20 minutes hanggang mag-melt ang cheese at mag-bubble ang sauce sa gilid.
Budburan ng extra crema, ilagay ang sliced onion, tapos ihaing agad habang malambot pa ang tortillas.
tips: I-dip lang, wag ibabad, ang tortillas sa warm oil; ilang seconds lang para manatiling pliable nang hindi nagiging maalinsangan sa taba.
Pwedeng i-assemble tapos ipa-fridge ng ilang hours bago, tapos i-bake na lang just before serving para hindi mag-soggy ang tortillas.
fil.nutritionNote: Ang crema at cheese ay nagdadagdag ng richness, kaya i-balance ang plato with simple side salad o extra shredded lettuce at tomato instead na mas maraming cheese.

recipes.title: Meatballs in Chipotle Broth
recipes.description: Rice-studded beef meatballs simmered in a smoky chipotle-tomato broth until tender, a nostalgic weeknight soup that Mexican kids grow up asking for by name.

ingredients.note: hierbabuena is traditional; cilantro is a fine substitute

ingredients.item: canned chipotle peppers in adobo, chopped
ingredients.note: start with 1 tbsp for a milder family pot; keep extra chipotle on the side for adults who want more heat

steps: Mix the ground beef, rice, egg, chopped onion, garlic, mint, salt and pepper in a bowl until just combined; don't overwork the mixture.
Roll into golf-ball sized meatballs, about 16 total, and set aside on a tray.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic and chipotle with 1 cup of the broth until smooth.
Pour the blended sauce into a large pot, bring to a simmer, and cook 8-10 minutes until it deepens in color and loses its raw smell.
Add the remaining broth and bring to a gentle boil.
Carefully drop in the meatballs one at a time; simmer uncovered, without stirring too much, 25-30 minutes until cooked through and the rice inside is tender.
Season with salt and skim any foam from the surface.
Ladle into bowls, sprinkle with cilantro and serve with warm tortillas.
tips: Don't stir vigorously once the meatballs go in, let the broth do the work or they'll break apart.
The raw rice inside each meatball needs the full simmer time to cook through, so don't rush the last step.
recipes.nutritionNote: A protein-rich soup with rice already built in; round it out with a side salad or extra broth vegetables like chayote or carrot.

fil.description: Beef meatballs na may rice sa loob, ni-simmer sa smoky chipotle-tomato broth hanggang lumambot, isang nostalgic weeknight soup na talagang hahanapin ng mga batang Mexicano by name.
ingredients: canned chipotle peppers in adobo, tinadtad
steps: Ihalo ang giniling na baka, rice, itlog, chopped onion, bawang, mint, asin at pepper sa bowl hanggang just combined; wag i-overwork ang mixture.
Ibilog into golf-ball sized meatballs, mga 16 total, at itabi sa tray.
I-blend ang tomatoes, onion, bawang at chipotle with 1 cup ng broth hanggang smooth.
Ibuhos ang blended sauce sa large pot, pakuluin, at lutuin for 8-10 minutes hanggang dumilim ang kulay at mawala ang raw smell.
Idagdag ang natitirang broth at pakuluin nang mahinay.
Dahan-dahang ilagay ang meatballs isa-isa; i-simmer nang bukas, wag masyadong haluin, 25-30 minutes hanggang maluto at lumambot ang rice sa loob.
Timplahan ng asin at alisin ang foam sa ibabaw.
Isabit sa bowls, budburan ng cilantro at ihain with warm tortillas.
tips: Wag haluin nang malakas once nasa broth na ang meatballs, hayaan ang broth ang gumawa ng trabaho kundi mag-break apart sila.
Kailangan ng raw rice sa loob ng bawat meatball ng buong simmer time para maluto, kaya wag i-rush ang last step.
fil.nutritionNote: Protein-rich soup na may kasamang rice na; kumpletuhin with side salad o extra broth vegetables tulad ng chayote o carrot.

recipes.title: Mexican Noodle Soup
recipes.description: Toasted vermicelli coils simmered in a light tomato broth until just tender, the everyday soup Mexican kids grow up on, made with pantry staples in about twenty minutes.

ingredients.note: coiled vermicelli sold as fideo or fideos cortados; broken thin spaghetti or vermicelli noodles work as a substitute

steps: Blend the canned tomatoes with their juice, garlic, oregano, salt and cumin until completely smooth.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat, add the dry fideo noodles, and stir constantly 3-4 minutes until they turn from pale to deep golden brown.
Carefully pour in the blended tomato mixture, it will spatter, and stir to coat the toasted noodles.
Add the broth, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 5-7 minutes until the noodles are tender but not mushy.
Taste and adjust the salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with cilantro, queso fresco, avocado and a squeeze of lime.
tips: Toasting the noodles until deep golden, not just tan, is what gives this soup its nutty flavor; don't rush this step.
The noodles keep absorbing broth as they sit, so serve immediately or thin with extra broth when reheating.
recipes.nutritionNote: A light, easy-to-digest soup that's gentle on kids' stomachs; add extra broth or a side of beans to make it a more complete meal.

fil.description: Toasted vermicelli coils na ni-simmer sa light tomato broth hanggang lumambot lang, ito ang everyday soup na kinalakihan ng mga batang Mexican, gawa sa pantry staples in about twenty minutes.
steps: I-blend ang de-latang tomatoes with juice nito, garlic, oregano, asin at cumin hanggang maging completely smooth.
Painitin ang oil sa large pot sa medium heat, ilagay ang dry fideo noodles, tapos haluin nang tuluy-tuloy for 3-4 minutes hanggang mag-deep golden brown mula pale.
Ibuhos nang maingat ang blended tomato mixture, mag-sisplatter ito, tapos haluin para mabalutan ang toasted noodles.
Idagdag ang broth, pakuluin, tapos hinaan sa simmer, takpan, at lutuin for 5-7 minutes hanggang lumambot ang noodles pero hindi mushy.
Tikman at ayusin ang asin.
Isalok sa bowls tapos top ng cilantro, queso fresco, avocado at pigang lime.
tips: Ang pag-toast ng noodles hanggang deep golden, hindi lang tan, ang nagbibigay ng nutty flavor sa soup na ito; wag magmadali sa step na ito.
Patuloy na sumisipsip ng broth ang noodles habang nakatiwangwang, kaya ihaing agad o lagyan ng extra broth pag nag-reheat.
fil.nutritionNote: Light at easy-to-digest na soup na hindi bumabagabag sa tiyan ng mga bata; magdagdag ng extra broth o side ng beans para maging mas complete meal.

recipes.title: Mexican Red Rice
recipes.description: Rice toasted in oil until golden, then simmered in a blended tomato, garlic and onion sauce until every grain turns out fluffy and separate, the standard side for nearly every Mexican meal.

ingredients.note: left whole for aroma only, removed before serving; omit for a completely mild pot

steps: Rinse the rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear, then drain well.
Blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic with half a cup of the broth until completely smooth; set aside.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and toast the rice, stirring often, until it turns opaque and pale golden, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the blended tomato mixture, it will sizzle, stirring to coat every grain, and cook 2 minutes to cook off the raw tomato taste.
Add the remaining broth, carrots and peas if using, the whole serrano, cilantro sprig and salt; stir once.
Bring to a boil, reduce to the lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook without lifting the lid for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and let it rest, covered, 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork before serving.
tips: Stir the rice only once it hits a boil; constant stirring after that releases starch and makes it gummy instead of fluffy.
Resist lifting the lid while it cooks; the trapped steam is doing the work.
recipes.nutritionNote: A simple carbohydrate side; pair with beans and a protein like tinga or carne asada to round out the plate with fiber and protein.

source.name: Mexico in My Kitchen (Mely Martinez's Arroz Rojo method, cross-checked against RecipeTin Eats)

fil.description: Rice na ni-toast sa oil hanggang golden, tapos ni-simmer sa blended tomato, garlic at onion sauce hanggang maging fluffy at hiwa-hiwalay ang bawat butil, ito ang standard side sa halos lahat ng Mexican meal.
steps: Hugasan ang rice sa cold water hanggang halos maging clear na, tapos i-drain nang mabuti.
I-blend ang tomatoes, onion at garlic with half a cup ng broth hanggang completely smooth; itabi muna.
Painitin ang oil sa saucepan sa medium heat tapos i-toast ang rice, haluin madalas, hanggang mag-opaque at pale golden, mga 5 minutes.
Ibuhos ang blended tomato mixture, magsi-sizzle ito, haluin para mabalutan ang bawat butil, tapos lutuin for 2 minutes para mawala ang raw tomato taste.
Idagdag ang natitirang broth, carrots at peas kung gagamitin, whole serrano, cilantro sprig at asin; haluin nang isang beses lang.
Pakuluin, hinaan sa pinakamababang heat, takpan nang mahigpit, tapos lutuin nang hindi binubuksan ang takip for 15 minutes.
Alisin sa apoy tapos ipahinga, nakatakip, for 10 minutes, saka lukubin gamit ang fork bago ihain.
tips: Haluin lang ang rice bago pa ito kumulo; kapag paulit-ulit hinalo pagkatapos, lumalabas ang starch at nagiging malagkit instead na fluffy.
Iwasang buksan ang takip habang nagluluto; ang trapped steam ang gumagawa ng trabaho.
fil.nutritionNote: Simpleng carbohydrate side; isabay sa beans at protein tulad ng tinga o carne asada para maging complete ang plato with fiber at protein.

recipes.title: Mushroom Quesadillas
recipes.description: Corn tortillas griddled with melted Oaxaca cheese and mushrooms sauteed with epazote and chile, a Mexico City street-stall staple that also makes a fast, meatless weeknight dinner.

ingredients.note: wild mushrooms are traditional in central Mexico; button or cremini are the easiest reliable substitute
deseed for a milder filling, or omit entirely
hard to find in Manila, order dried epazote online, or substitute a little chopped cilantro plus a pinch of dried oregano
mozzarella is the closest easy substitute

steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, chile and garlic, stir well, and cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms release their liquid and it mostly evaporates, 6-8 minutes.
Stir in the epazote and salt in the last minute of cooking, then remove from heat.
Warm the corn tortillas on a dry griddle or comal until pliable, about 20 seconds per side.
Place a tortilla on the griddle, scatter cheese over half, top with a spoonful of the mushroom filling, and fold the tortilla over.
Press gently and cook 1-2 minutes per side until the tortilla is lightly toasted and the cheese has melted through.
Serve immediately with salsa on the side.
tips: Let the mushrooms fully release and cook off their own liquid before folding the quesadilla, or the tortilla will turn soggy.
Corn tortillas tear more easily than flour; warm them first so they fold without cracking.
recipes.nutritionNote: A meatless, fiber-rich option; the cheese provides protein and calcium, but keep portions moderate to avoid excess saturated fat if serving often.

source.name: Mexico in My Kitchen (sauteed mushroom filling), assembly per La Cocina de Leslie's Quesadillas de Hongos

fil.description: Corn tortillas na iginriddle with melted Oaxaca cheese at mushrooms na ginisa with epazote at chile, isang Mexico City street-stall staple na pwede ring maging fast, meatless weeknight dinner.
steps: Painitin ang oil sa skillet sa medium heat tapos lutuin ang onion hanggang maging translucent, mga 3 minutes.
Idagdag ang mushrooms, chile at garlic, haluin nang mabuti, tapos lutuin nang bukas, haluin paminsan-minsan, hanggang lumabas ang liquid ng mushrooms at halos ma-evaporate, 6-8 minutes.
Ihalo ang epazote at asin sa huling minuto ng pagluluto, tapos alisin sa apoy.
Painitin ang corn tortillas sa dry griddle o comal hanggang maging pliable, mga 20 seconds per side.
Ilagay ang tortilla sa griddle, budburan ng cheese sa kalahati, lagyan ng isang kutsara ng mushroom filling, tapos tiklupin ang tortilla.
Pindutin nang dahan-dahan tapos lutuin for 1-2 minutes per side hanggang lightly toasted ang tortilla at natunaw nang husto ang cheese.
Ihaing agad with salsa sa tabi.
tips: Hayaang lumabas nang husto at ma-evaporate ang liquid ng mushrooms bago tiklupin ang quesadilla, kung hindi mag-soggy ang tortilla.
Mas madaling mapunit ang corn tortillas kumpara sa flour; painitin muna para hindi mabasag kapag tiniklop.
fil.nutritionNote: Meatless, fiber-rich na option; nagbibigay ng protein at calcium ang cheese, pero konti lang ang portions para iwas sa excess saturated fat kung madalas ihahain.

recipes.title: Picadillo
recipes.description: Ground beef simmered with potatoes, carrots and tomato until saucy, a homey everyday filling Mexican mothers make for tacos, stuffed peppers or simply spooned over rice.

ingredients.note: optional; more common in northern Mexican kitchens

steps: Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the ground beef, breaking it up with a spoon, and cook until no longer pink, 6-8 minutes, draining off excess fat if the mix looks greasy.
Stir in the tomatoes, cumin and bay leaf, and cook 3-4 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Add the potatoes, carrot and broth, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes until the vegetables are just tender.
Stir in the peas, season with salt and pepper, and simmer uncovered 5 minutes more until the sauce thickens slightly and clings to the meat.
Remove the bay leaf and serve warm with warm corn tortillas or rice.
tips: Dice the potatoes small and uniform so they finish cooking in the same time as the beef.
Picadillo is even better the next day and freezes well for a quick future dinner.
recipes.nutritionNote: A balanced one-pot mix of protein, potato starch and vegetables; drain the grease after browning fattier beef to keep the dish lighter.

fil.description: Giniling na baka na ni-simmer sa patatas, carrot at kamatis hanggang saucy, isang homey everyday filling na madalas gawin ng mga Mexican mothers para sa tacos, stuffed peppers o basta ibuhos sa ibabaw ng rice.
ingredients: patatas, binalatan at dinice nang maliit
carrot, binalatan at dinice nang maliit
steps: Painitin ang oil sa wide skillet sa medium heat at lutuin ang onion hanggang lumambot, mga 3 minutes.
Idagdag ang bawang at lutuin for 1 minute hanggang bumango.
Idagdag ang giniling na baka, dikdikin gamit ang spoon, at lutuin hanggang hindi na pink, 6-8 minutes, i-drain ang sobrang taba kung maoily ang mixture.
Ihalo ang tomatoes, cumin at bay leaf, at lutuin for 3-4 minutes hanggang mag-breakdown ang tomatoes.
Idagdag ang patatas, carrot at broth, pakuluin, takpan, at lutuin for 15 minutes hanggang lumambot lang ang gulay.
Ihalo ang peas, timplahan ng asin at pepper, at i-simmer nang bukas for 5 minutes more hanggang lumapot nang kaunti ang sauce at dumikit sa karne.
Alisin ang bay leaf at ihain mainit with warm corn tortillas o rice.
tips: I-dice ang patatas nang maliit at pantay para maluto nang sabay sa beef.
Mas masarap pa ang picadillo the next day at freezer-friendly for a quick future dinner.
fil.nutritionNote: Balanced na one-pot mix ng protein, potato starch at gulay; i-drain ang grease after browning ng mataba na beef para mas light ang dish.

recipes.title: Red Pozole
recipes.description: Pork and hominy simmered in a deep guajillo-ancho broth and finished at the table with cabbage, radish and lime, the celebration soup for birthdays and Mexican Independence Day.

ingredients.item: pork spare ribs or baby back ribs
ingredients.note: or use all pork shoulder if ribs aren't available
cacahuazintle hominy sold canned or frozen at Latin/specialty grocers online in Manila; canned white corn kernels are a last-resort substitute though the texture differs
order dried guajillo and ancho chiles from a Mexican/Latin specialty grocer online if a local market doesn't carry them; they keep for months dried
table-only garnish, this is where the real heat is added; keep it off the kids' bowls entirely and let each adult spoon in their own

steps: Combine the pork shoulder, ribs, quartered onion and whole garlic cloves in a large pot with the water; bring to a boil, skim the foam, then reduce to a gentle simmer 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat is fork-tender.
Lift out the meat, discard the bones and any large fat, shred or chunk the meat, and return it to the strained broth.
Meanwhile, soak the guajillo and ancho chiles in a bowl of hot water 20-25 minutes until soft and pliable.
Drain the chiles and blend them with the sauce garlic, oregano and a cup of the broth until completely smooth.
Heat the oil in a skillet, pour in the chile puree, and simmer 10 minutes, stirring often as it will splatter, until it deepens in color.
Strain the chile sauce into the pot of broth and meat to keep the pozole silky, add the drained hominy, and simmer 20-30 minutes until the hominy is tender.
Season with salt, keeping the pot itself mild; do not add chile piquin to the pot.
Ladle into deep bowls and let everyone garnish their own portion with cabbage, onion, radish and lime, adding crushed piquin or hot salsa only to the bowls that want it.
tips: This is a weekend project; the broth alone needs 2 to 2.5 hours, so start it in the morning for an evening meal.
Straining the chile puree into the broth removes the tough chile skins and keeps the pozole smooth rather than gritty.
recipes.kidNote: Keep the pot's chile base to guajillo and ancho only, it's warm, not fiery, and put the crushed chile piquin and any hot salsa out as table garnishes so each person, including the kids, spoons in their own heat.
recipes.nutritionNote: A hearty, protein-rich stew with fiber from the hominy; load up the table-side cabbage and radish to round it into a fuller vegetable serving.

source.name: Cooks Without Borders (Mely Martinez's Pozole Rojo)

fil.description: Pork at hominy na ni-simmer sa deep guajillo-ancho broth tapos tinatapos sa table with cabbage, radish at lime, ito ang celebration soup para sa birthdays at Mexican Independence Day.
ingredients: pork spare ribs o baby back ribs
guajillo chiles, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
ancho chiles, tinanggalan ng tangkay at buto
steps: Pagsamahin ang pork shoulder, ribs, quartered onion at whole garlic cloves sa large pot kasama ang tubig; pakuluin, alisin ang foam, tapos hinaan sa gentle simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours hanggang maging fork-tender ang karne.
Alisin ang karne, itapon ang bones at malalaking taba, i-shred o i-chunk ang karne, tapos ibalik sa strained broth.
Samantala, ibabad ang guajillo at ancho chiles sa bowl ng hot water for 20-25 minutes hanggang lumambot at maging pliable.
I-drain ang chiles tapos i-blend kasama ang bawang, oregano at isang cup ng broth hanggang completely smooth.
Painitin ang oil sa skillet, ibuhos ang chile puree, tapos i-simmer for 10 minutes, haluin madalas dahil magsi-splatter ito, hanggang dumilim ang kulay.
I-strain ang chile sauce papunta sa pot ng broth at karne para manatiling silky ang pozole, idagdag ang drained hominy, tapos i-simmer for 20-30 minutes hanggang lumambot ang hominy.
Timplahan ng asin, panatilihing mild ang pot mismo; wag maglagay ng chile piquin sa pot.
Isalok sa deep bowls tapos hayaang mag-garnish ang bawat isa ng sarili nilang portion with cabbage, onion, radish at lime, idagdag lang ang crushed piquin o hot salsa sa bowls na gusto nito.
tips: Weekend project ito; ang broth lang mismo kailangan ng 2 to 2.5 hours, kaya simulan sa umaga kung para sa hapunan.
Ang pag-strain ng chile puree papunta sa broth ay nag-aalis ng matigas na balat ng chile at pinapanatiling smooth ang pozole instead na gritty.
fil.kidNote: Panatilihing guajillo at ancho lang ang chile base ng pot, medyo warm lang ito, hindi fiery, tapos ilagay na lang ang crushed chile piquin at anumang hot salsa bilang table garnishes para bawat isa, kasama ang mga bata, sarili nilang isasalok ang gustong anghang.
fil.nutritionNote: Hearty at protein-rich na stew with fiber galing sa hominy; magdagdag ng table-side cabbage at radish para maging mas complete ang vegetable serving.

recipes.title: Roasted Poblano Strips in Cream
recipes.description: Roasted poblano strips simmered in a light garlic cream with sweet corn, a mild, silky side dish or taco filling found on nearly every central Mexican comedor menu.

ingredients.note: fresh, frozen or canned and drained
or sour cream thinned with a little milk

steps: Char the poblanos directly over a gas flame or under a hot broiler, turning, until blackened all over.
Seal the charred peppers in a plastic bag or covered bowl for 10 minutes to steam, then rub off the skin under cool running water.
Remove the stems and seeds, then slice the peppers into thin strips.
Heat the oil or butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft and translucent, 4-5 minutes.
Add the garlic and corn and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in the poblano strips and cook 2-3 minutes to combine the flavors.
Lower the heat, stir in the crema and salt, and simmer gently 3-4 minutes until warmed through; do not boil hard or the crema can split.
Scatter with cheese if using and serve warm as a side or tortilla filling.
tips: Poblanos vary in heat from pepper to pepper; taste a small piece after roasting, and if a batch runs spicier than expected, add extra crema and corn to mellow it for the kids' plates.
recipes.nutritionNote: Vegetable-forward with real fiber from the peppers and corn; the cream and cheese add richness, so keep this a side rather than the main dish, or thin the crema with milk for a lighter version.

fil.description: Roasted poblano strips na ni-simmer sa light garlic cream na may sweet corn, isang mild at silky side dish o taco filling na makikita sa halos lahat ng central Mexican comedor menu.
steps: I-char ang poblanos directly over gas flame o under hot broiler, i-turn, hanggang mag-itim all over.
Ilagay ang charred peppers sa plastic bag o covered bowl for 10 minutes para mag-steam, tapos kuskusin ang balat under cool running water.
Alisin ang tangkay at buto, tapos hiwain ang peppers into thin strips.
Painitin ang oil o butter sa skillet sa medium heat at lutuin ang onion hanggang lumambot at translucent, 4-5 minutes.
Idagdag ang bawang at corn at lutuin for 2 minutes.
Ihalo ang poblano strips at lutuin for 2-3 minutes para mag-combine ang flavors.
Hinaan ang apoy, ihalo ang crema at asin, at i-simmer nang mahinay for 3-4 minutes hanggang uminit; wag pakuluin nang malakas kundi mag-split ang crema.
Budburan ng cheese kung gagamitin at ihain mainit as side o tortilla filling.
tips: Iba-iba ang anghang ng poblanos per pepper; tikman ang maliit na piraso after roasting, at kung mas maanghang than expected ang batch, magdagdag ng extra crema at corn para mas mellow para sa plato ng mga bata.
fil.nutritionNote: Vegetable-forward with real fiber from the peppers and corn; nagdadagdag ang cream at cheese ng richness, kaya panatilihin itong side kesa main dish, o i-thin ang crema with milk for lighter version.

recipes.title: Tortilla Soup
recipes.description: A pasilla-tomato broth ladled over crisp fried tortilla strips and topped with avocado, cheese and crema, the soup nearly every Mexico City kitchen serves before the main course.

ingredients.item: corn tortillas, cut into thin strips
vegetable oil, for frying the tortillas

ingredients.note: dried pasilla sold by Mexican/Latin specialty importers online in Manila; substitute 1 ancho chile if unavailable
or sour cream thinned with milk

steps: Fry the tortilla strips in batches in the hot oil until crisp and golden, about 2 minutes; drain on paper towels and set aside.
Soak the pasilla chile in hot water 10 minutes until soft, then drain.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic and softened pasilla until completely smooth.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pot over medium heat, pour in the blended sauce, and cook, stirring, 8-10 minutes until it darkens and thickens.
Add the broth, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer 10 minutes and season with salt.
Just before serving, divide the fried tortilla strips among bowls and ladle the hot broth over them so they stay crisp at the table.
Top with avocado, queso fresco and a drizzle of crema, with lime wedges alongside.
tips: Add the tortilla strips to the bowl last, always, or they turn soggy sitting in the broth.
The salsa base can be made a day ahead and refrigerated; fry the tortillas fresh right before serving.
recipes.nutritionNote: A light tomato-based broth; keep the fried tortilla strips and crema portions modest for a lighter bowl, or bake the strips instead of frying for less oil.

source.name: 196 Flavors (recipe validated by Mely Martinez of Mexico in My Kitchen)

fil.description: Pasilla-tomato broth na binuhos sa crisp fried tortilla strips at topped with avocado, cheese at crema, ang soup na halos lahat ng kusina sa Mexico City ay iniihain bago ang main course.
ingredients: corn tortillas, hiwain into thin strips
pasilla chile, tanggalan ng tangkay at buto
steps: I-fry ang tortilla strips in batches sa hot oil hanggang crisp at golden, mga 2 minutes; i-drain sa paper towels at itabi.
I-soak ang pasilla chile sa hot water for 10 minutes hanggang lumambot, tapos i-drain.
I-blend ang tomatoes, onion, bawang at softened pasilla hanggang completely smooth.
Painitin ang 1 tablespoon oil sa pot sa medium heat, ibuhos ang blended sauce, at lutuin, haluin, for 8-10 minutes hanggang dumilim at lumapot.
Idagdag ang broth, pakuluin, tapos hinaan sa simmer for 10 minutes at timplahan ng asin.
Bago ihain, hatiin ang fried tortilla strips sa bowls at isabit ang mainit na broth dito para manatiling crisp sa table.
Topping ng avocado, queso fresco at drizzle ng crema, with lime wedges sa tabi.
tips: Idagdag ang tortilla strips sa bowl last, palagi, kundi magiging soggy ito.
Pwedeng gawin ang salsa base isang araw bago at i-refrigerate, tapos i-fry ang tortillas fresh right before serving.
fil.nutritionNote: Light na tomato-based broth; panatilihing modest ang fried tortilla strips at crema portions para mas light ang bowl, o i-bake na lang ang strips instead of pag-frito para less oil.

recipes.title: Veracruz-Style Fish
recipes.description: White fish fillets gently simmered in a Spanish-influenced tomato sauce with olives, capers and pickled jalapenos, Veracruz's coastal answer to Mediterranean flavors landing on Mexican shores.

ingredients.item: white fish fillets, about 150 g each
ingredients.note: red snapper (huachinango) is traditional; tilapia or cream dory are easy local substitutes
or use 1 can (400 g) whole peeled tomatoes, more reliable off-season
jalapenos en escabeche; or use pickled banana peppers if unavailable

ingredients.item: ground cinnamon or a pinch of nutmeg

steps: Season the fish fillets with lime juice and salt, then set aside while you make the sauce.
Heat the olive oil in a wide, deep skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant, then stir in the chopped tomatoes, olives, capers, pickled jalapenos, bay leaf and cinnamon.
Simmer the sauce uncovered 10-12 minutes until it thickens and loses its raw-tomato smell.
Nestle the fish fillets into the sauce, spooning some sauce over the top, cover, and simmer gently 8-10 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
Taste and adjust salt, then remove the bay leaf.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve straight from the pan with white rice.
tips: Simmer the fish gently; a hard boil will break the fillets apart before they finish cooking.
Make the sauce up to a day ahead, it deepens in flavor overnight, and only poach the fish just before serving.
For the kids' plates, spoon sauce around the jalapeno slices rather than over them, or fish the slices out before serving.
recipes.nutritionNote: Lean white fish with tomatoes and olive oil is a heart-healthy combination; watch the sodium from olives and capers and skip added salt at the table.

fil.description: White fish fillets na ni-simmer nang dahan-dahan sa Spanish-influenced tomato sauce with olives, capers at pickled jalapenos, ito ang coastal answer ng Veracruz sa Mediterranean flavors na dumating sa Mexican shores.
ingredients: lime, kinuha ang juice, para sa fish
steps: Timplahan ang fish fillets ng lime juice at asin, tapos itabi muna habang ginagawa ang sauce.
Painitin ang olive oil sa wide, deep skillet sa medium heat tapos lutuin ang onion hanggang lumambot, mga 4 minutes.
Idagdag ang bawang tapos lutuin for 1 minute hanggang umamoy maganda, saka ihalo ang chopped tomatoes, olives, capers, pickled jalapenos, bay leaf at cinnamon.
I-simmer ang sauce nang bukas for 10-12 minutes hanggang lumapot at mawala ang amoy ng raw tomato.
Ilagay ang fish fillets sa loob ng sauce, budburan ng kaunting sauce sa ibabaw, takpan, tapos i-simmer nang dahan-dahan for 8-10 minutes hanggang mag-flake nang madali ang fish.
Tikman at ayusin ang asin, tapos alisin ang bay leaf.
Budburan ng parsley tapos ihain straight from the pan with white rice.
tips: I-simmer nang dahan-dahan ang fish; kapag hard boil, mawawasak ang fillets bago pa matapos maluto.
Pwede gawin ang sauce up to a day ahead, mas lumalalim ang lasa overnight, tapos i-poach na lang ang fish just before serving.
Para sa plato ng mga bata, ilagay ang sauce sa paligid ng jalapeno slices instead na sa ibabaw nito, o kunin na lang ang slices bago ihain.
fil.nutritionNote: Ang lean white fish with tomatoes at olive oil ay heart-healthy combination; bantayan ang sodium mula sa olives at capers tapos wag nang magdagdag pa ng asin sa table.

recipes.title: Zucchini with Corn
recipes.description: Mexican zucchini and sweet corn sauteed with onion, tomato and a touch of chile, a quick everyday vegetable side that home cooks like Mely Martinez say they could eat daily.

ingredients.note: deseed for milder, or omit entirely for a fully mild pot
regular green zucchini is a close substitute
fresh off the cob is traditional; frozen or canned works too

steps: Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until translucent, 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and chile and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the diced zucchini and corn and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the chopped tomatoes, cover, and cook 8-10 minutes until the zucchini is tender but not mushy and the tomatoes have broken down into a light sauce.
Uncover, season with salt, and simmer 2-3 minutes more to let any extra liquid evaporate.
Scatter with queso fresco if using and serve warm as a side, or spoon over rice for a light meal.
tips: Don't overcook the zucchini, it should still hold its shape; cut it into even pieces so it cooks at the same rate as the corn.
recipes.nutritionNote: A fiber- and vitamin-rich vegetable side that's naturally low in fat; a good way to get the kids eating vegetables since the corn sweetness balances the zucchini.

fil.description: Mexican zucchini at sweet corn na ginisa sa onion, kamatis at kaunting chile, isang mabilis na everyday vegetable side na sabi ng mga home cook gaya ni Mely Martinez ay puwede na nilang kainin araw-araw.
steps: Painitin ang oil sa wide skillet sa medium heat at lutuin ang onion hanggang translucent, 3 minutes.
Idagdag ang bawang at chile at lutuin for 1 minute hanggang bumango.
Ihalo ang diced zucchini at corn at lutuin for 5 minutes, haluin paminsan-minsan.
Idagdag ang chopped tomatoes, takpan, at lutuin for 8-10 minutes hanggang lumambot ang zucchini pero hindi mushy at mag-breakdown ang tomatoes into light sauce.
Buksan, timplahan ng asin, at i-simmer for 2-3 minutes more para mag-evaporate ang extra liquid.
Budburan ng queso fresco kung gagamitin at ihain mainit as side, o ilagay sa ibabaw ng rice for a light meal.
tips: Wag i-overcook ang zucchini, dapat hindi ito nawawalan ng shape; hiwain nang pantay para maluto sabay ng corn.
fil.nutritionNote: Fiber- at vitamin-rich na vegetable side na naturally low in fat; good way para makakain ng gulay ang mga bata kasi binabalance ng tamis ng corn ang zucchini.
